# Design system starter

> Design system starter where design-system drift fails the build.

Import only from `src/index.ts`. Every export's props, variants, stories, tokens and usage rules: [design-system.manifest.json](design-system.manifest.json) ([schema](design-system.manifest.schema.json)). Every usage doc and guide in full: [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt). Rules for all UI work:

```text
UI rules (design system v0)
- Style only with semantic tokens. No hex, rgb, px, ms or other raw values;
  allowed literals are inherit, currentColor, transparent, none, auto, 0, 1px, 100%.
- Compose system components and layout primitives, imported from src/index.ts.
  Never import radix-ui outside src/components or src/primitives, or
  react-aria-components and @internationalized/* outside src/components.
- Never restyle a system component with className or style. Need a new look?
  Propose a variant. UNSAFE_className / UNSAFE_style are escape hatches that need
  a lint disable with a reason, an owner and a removal condition.
- Before creating a component, walk the decision ladder: template → variant →
  component → primitive. Stop at the first yes.
- Missing token? Add a semantic token in tokens/ (with a dark value for colours),
  run npm run tokens. Never write a literal instead.
- New pages start from PageHeader (the one h1, status, actions) inside the right
  layout: AppShell for signed-in pages (fill its slots; never rebuild the frame),
  AuthLayout for signed-out pages, FocusedLayout for multi-step tasks; PageLayout
  for a page's sub-nav or aside. Copy the matching golden example: list → ListPage,
  record → RecordPage, create/edit → CreateEditFlow, settings → SettingsPage,
  sign-in → SignInPage, wizard → SetupWizard, dashboard → DashboardPage,
  queue/inbox → InboxPage, admin console → AdminConsole, error/404 → ErrorPages.
  Not other screens.
- Links go through Link (or Nav, NavTabs, Breadcrumbs); the app injects its router
  once with LinkProvider. NavTabs for sections that are routes, Tabs for panels in place.
- CSS: inside a declared @layer, BEM-lite classes, logical properties only,
  variants as closed data-* attributes, state via aria/native attributes,
  specificity ≤ 0,3,0, no !important, no ids.
- Every new variant, size or state gets a story. Every new exported component,
  layout or primitive gets a usage doc in docs/usage/<Name>.usage.tsx (when to
  use, when not to, do/don't, accessibility); tests/unit/docs.test.tsx fails
  without one. Lint, npm run check and the gallery (visual + axe + WCAG 2.2 checks) must pass.
- A story that renders an open modal is tagged ['modal-open', '!autodocs'].
- WCAG 2.2 AA is part of the gate: targets ≥ 24px or spaced (size.target-min),
  focus never hidden behind sticky content (scroll containers use
  space.scroll-padding.*), password fields as TextField type="password" with
  autoComplete (username, current-password or new-password, one-time-code),
  never block paste, pass AppShell's help from the shell composition, never
  ask twice in a multi-step flow, and any drag declares data-drag-alternative.
- Never add an eslint-disable or stylelint-disable without a reason after "--".
- Format every number, date, amount and list with useFormat() (LocaleProvider
  sets locale and time zone). Money is integer minor units + currency code.
- AI: render model output with StreamingText (never raw HTML), cite sources
  with Citation + SourcesList, mark unaccepted AI content with AiMarker, and
  never let AI write without ReviewChanges (or an explicit accept) and an Undo.
  The assistant acts only through the person's own can() and named mutations.
- Keyboard shortcuts go through useShortcut (never a bare keydown listener):
  every shortcut mirrors a visible control and shows its keys there (Tooltip
  shortcut, MenuItem.shortcut, Kbd). Reserved keys are refused and conflicts
  reported; single-key shortcuts can be turned off in the ? overlay.
```

## Components

- [Accordion](docs/usage/Accordion.usage.tsx): A stack of titled sections that open and close
- [AiMarker](docs/usage/AiMarker.usage.tsx): Marks content the AI wrote and a person hasn't accepted or…
- [Avatar](docs/usage/Avatar.usage.tsx): Showing who: record owners, activity authors
- [Badge](docs/usage/Badge.usage.tsx): A record’s status in a table row, title or card: a word plus a tone
- [Banner](docs/usage/Banner.usage.tsx): Ongoing state for a page or region
- [Breadcrumbs](docs/usage/Breadcrumbs.usage.tsx): Path back up a genuinely nested hierarchy
- [Button](docs/usage/Button.usage.tsx): To run an action on this page: save, create, delete, open a dialog
- [Card](docs/usage/Card.usage.tsx): A bounded surface for one titled block of a page
- [ChatThread](docs/usage/ChatThread.usage.tsx): The list of turns in a conversation
- [Checkbox](docs/usage/Checkbox.usage.tsx): An independent yes/no inside a form that is saved with the form
- [Citation](docs/usage/Citation.usage.tsx): A numbered inline citation, [1]
- [CodeBlock](docs/usage/CodeBlock.usage.tsx): Monospaced code in a keyboard-scrollable region
- [Combobox](docs/usage/Combobox.usage.tsx): A text field with a list of options that narrows as you type
- [CommandPalette](docs/usage/CommandPalette.usage.tsx): The command palette
- [Composer](docs/usage/Composer.usage.tsx): Where the person writes to the assistant
- [ContextMenu](docs/usage/ContextMenu.usage.tsx): Actions on a thing, where the pointer or focus is: right-click
- [CopyButton](docs/usage/CopyButton.usage.tsx): Copies a value to the clipboard
- [DatePicker](docs/usage/DatePicker.usage.tsx): A calendar date
- [Dialog](docs/usage/Dialog.usage.tsx): Modal dialog
- [Disclosure](docs/usage/Disclosure.usage.tsx): One section that shows and hides its details
- [Divider](docs/usage/Divider.usage.tsx): A hairline between blocks or inline groups
- [Drawer](docs/usage/Drawer.usage.tsx): Modal side sheet over a scrim
- [EmptyState](docs/usage/EmptyState.usage.tsx): What a list, table or panel shows instead of its content
- [Feedback](docs/usage/Feedback.usage.tsx): Thumbs up or down on one AI result
- [FileUpload](docs/usage/FileUpload.usage.tsx): Picks files with a button and, as an enhancement
- [Heading](docs/usage/Heading.usage.tsx): Page titles and section titles, in outline order
- [HoverCard](docs/usage/HoverCard.usage.tsx): A supplementary preview of a link's destination
- [InlineEdit](docs/usage/InlineEdit.usage.tsx): A value you can change where it's shown
- [Kbd](docs/usage/Kbd.usage.tsx): A key or a keyboard shortcut, shown as key caps
- [Link](docs/usage/Link.usage.tsx): An inline or standalone text link
- [Menu](docs/usage/Menu.usage.tsx): Action menu
- [Message](docs/usage/Message.usage.tsx): One turn in a ChatThread: a header, the content
- [Meter](docs/usage/Meter.usage.tsx): How much of a limit is used: seats, storage, API calls
- [MultiSelect](docs/usage/MultiSelect.usage.tsx): Choosing several values from a list that narrows as you type
- [Nav](docs/usage/Nav.usage.tsx): Vertical navigation: the app's primary sidebar or a section sub-nav
- [NavTabs](docs/usage/NavTabs.usage.tsx): Section navigation that looks like tabs but is links
- [NumberField](docs/usage/NumberField.usage.tsx): A number typed in the reader's own format
- [PageHeader](docs/usage/PageHeader.usage.tsx): The top of every page
- [Pagination](docs/usage/Pagination.usage.tsx): Moves through a long, server-paged list
- [Popover](docs/usage/Popover.usage.tsx): A small non-modal panel anchored to its trigger, for a few controls
- [Progress](docs/usage/Progress.usage.tsx): Determinate progress through a task
- [RadioGroup](docs/usage/RadioGroup.usage.tsx): One choice from a few visible options
- [ReviewChanges](docs/usage/ReviewChanges.usage.tsx): Changes an AI proposes, reviewed before anything happens
- [SearchField](docs/usage/SearchField.usage.tsx): A search input: type="search", a search icon
- [SegmentedControl](docs/usage/SegmentedControl.usage.tsx): One value from a few, always exactly one
- [Select](docs/usage/Select.usage.tsx): Single-choice list
- [Skeleton](docs/usage/Skeleton.usage.tsx): Placeholder for content on first load
- [Slider](docs/usage/Slider.usage.tsx): Picks a number, or a range
- [Spinner](docs/usage/Spinner.usage.tsx): Indeterminate progress for short or briefly unpredictable waits
- [Stat](docs/usage/Stat.usage.tsx): One headline number in a tile: label, value and an optional change
- [Stepper](docs/usage/Stepper.usage.tsx): Where someone is in an ordered task
- [StreamingText](docs/usage/StreamingText.usage.tsx): Text that arrives token by token
- [Suggestion](docs/usage/Suggestion.usage.tsx): A multi-line text field that can show an inline AI…
- [Switch](docs/usage/Switch.usage.tsx): An on/off setting that takes effect as a setting, not a form answer
- [Table](docs/usage/Table.usage.tsx): Data table: native table semantics, sticky header, tabular numbers
- [Tabs](docs/usage/Tabs.usage.tsx): Tabs: arrow-key roving focus and ARIA wiring come from Radix Tabs
- [Tag](docs/usage/Tag.usage.tsx): A compact value: an active filter chip, a label on a record
- [Text](docs/usage/Text.usage.tsx): Running text, descriptions and metadata
- [TextField](docs/usage/TextField.usage.tsx): Short free text: names, emails, amounts, search, passwords
- [Textarea](docs/usage/Textarea.usage.tsx): Multi-line text
- [Timeline](docs/usage/Timeline.usage.tsx): A dated list of events: a record's activity, an audit trail, a feed
- [Toast](docs/usage/Toast.usage.tsx): Declarative toast
- [Toggle](docs/usage/Toggle.usage.tsx): A button that stays pressed
- [Toolbar](docs/usage/Toolbar.usage.tsx): A row of related controls that is one tab stop
- [Tooltip](docs/usage/Tooltip.usage.tsx): Tooltip on hover and focus, dismissed with Escape

## Primitives

- [Box](docs/usage/Box.usage.tsx): Padding around content, from the inset scale
- [Center](docs/usage/Center.usage.tsx): Horizontally centred column with a bounded measure
- [Cluster](docs/usage/Cluster.usage.tsx): Horizontal group that wraps gracefully
- [Cover](docs/usage/Cover.usage.tsx): Vertically centres its content in the available block size
- [Frame](docs/usage/Frame.usage.tsx): Holds media to a fixed aspect ratio and crops it to fill
- [Grid](docs/usage/Grid.usage.tsx): Auto-fit card grid
- [Imposter](docs/usage/Imposter.usage.tsx): Positions an overlay over the centre of its container
- [Reel](docs/usage/Reel.usage.tsx): A single row that scrolls sideways
- [Sidebar](docs/usage/Sidebar.usage.tsx): Side region beside main content
- [Stack](docs/usage/Stack.usage.tsx): Vertical flow with consistent spacing
- [Switcher](docs/usage/Switcher.usage.tsx): A row of equal items that becomes a column, all at once
- [VisuallyHidden](docs/usage/VisuallyHidden.usage.tsx): Content that screen readers announce but the screen doesn't…

## Layouts

- [AppShell](docs/usage/AppShell.usage.tsx): The app frame every signed-in page renders inside
- [AssistantPanel](docs/usage/AssistantPanel.usage.tsx): The assistant beside the page, in AppShell's `assistant` slot
- [AuthLayout](docs/usage/AuthLayout.usage.tsx): The frame for signed-out pages
- [FocusedLayout](docs/usage/FocusedLayout.usage.tsx): The frame for a focused, multi-step task
- [PageLayout](docs/usage/PageLayout.usage.tsx): The regions of a page's body, below its PageHeader
- [SplitView](docs/usage/SplitView.usage.tsx): A list and the selected item side by side

## Utilities

- [LocaleProvider](docs/usage/LocaleProvider.usage.tsx): Sets the locale and time zone every system and app format reads
- [createFormatter](docs/usage/LocaleProvider.usage.tsx): Formats for one locale and time zone
- [currencyDigits](docs/usage/LocaleProvider.usage.tsx): Decimal places a currency's minor unit has: USD 2, JPY 0, BHD 3
- [useFormat](docs/usage/LocaleProvider.usage.tsx): The named formats for the current locale and time zone
- [vars](src/tokens/tokens.ts): Semantic and component tokens as var() references

## Components reference

### Accordion

component · `src/components/Accordion/Accordion.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Accordion.usage.tsx`

A stack of titled sections that open and close: steps an agent took, FAQ-style details. Each title is a heading wrapping a button with aria-expanded; arrow keys move between titles. From Radix Accordion. `single` (default) keeps one open; `multiple` lets several stay open.

Props:
- `items: readonly AccordionItem[]`
- `headingLevel?: 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6` = `3`: Heading level of each item's title, so the outline stays right where it sits.
- `type?: 'single'`
- `value?: string`
- `defaultValue?: string`
- `onValueChange?: (value: string) => void`

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: headingLevel (2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6); type (multiple | single).

**When to use**

- A stack of titled sections where people open one or a few: the steps an agent took, grouped settings help, an FAQ.
- `single` (default) keeps one open; `multiple` lets several stay open. Set `headingLevel` to fit the page outline.

**When not to use**

- One section of details → `Disclosure`
- Sections that are pages of their own → `NavTabs`
- A form split into steps → the Wizard archetype (`SetupWizard`)

**Do:** Each title names a step and its status sits beside it.

```tsx
<Accordion
  defaultValue="check"
  items={[
    { value: 'search', title: 'Search records', meta: <Badge tone="success">Done</Badge>, content: '12 records matched.' },
    { value: 'check', title: 'Check permissions', meta: <Badge tone="success">Done</Badge>, content: 'You can move 10 of them.' },
  ]}
/>
```

**Don't:** Every section holds one line: show the lines instead.

```tsx
<Accordion
  items={[
    { value: 'a', title: 'Owner', content: 'Sam Rivera' },
    { value: 'b', title: 'Status', content: 'Active' },
  ]}
/>
```

**Accessibility**

- Each title is a heading at `headingLevel` wrapping a button with `aria-expanded` (Radix Accordion). Arrow keys move between titles; Home and End jump.
- A disabled item stays in the list and says why in its title or content.

Stories: `components-accordion--single`, `components-accordion--multiple`, `components-accordion--all-closed`, `components-accordion--with-disabled-item`.
Composes: Disclosure, Icon.
Tokens read: `color.bg.hover`, `color.border.default`, `color.fg.default`, `ease.standard`, `icon.stroke`, `motion.fast`, `radius.control`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.target-min`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.2xs`, `space.inset.lg`, `space.inset.xs`, `text.body`, `text.label`.

### AiMarker

component · `src/components/AiMarker/AiMarker.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/AiMarker.usage.tsx`

Marks content the AI wrote and a person hasn't accepted or edited yet: a sparkle and a text label on the AI tint. Never colour alone, and never on content a person wrote.

Props:
- `children?: string` = `'AI-generated'`: What the AI did, in words: "AI-generated", "Drafted with AI", "Suggested by AI". The text carries the meaning; the tint only reinforces it.
- `variant?: 'badge' | 'inline'` = `'badge'`: badge: a pill beside a block or a field. inline: a quiet label inside a line of text or a header.
- …plus the native attributes of `AriaAttributes`, `Attributes`, `DOMAttributes`, `HTMLAttributes`, `RefAttributes`.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: variant (badge | inline).

**When to use**

- Content the AI wrote that a person hasn’t accepted or edited yet: a drafted field, a generated summary, a proposed change.
- `badge` beside a block or field; `inline` in a header or a line of text (an assistant turn’s header).

**When not to use**

- Content a person accepted or edited → nothing: remove the mark, or record “edited” in the content’s history
- A button that runs an AI action → a `Button` with the sparkle and a verb (“Suggest description”)
- A status → `Badge`

**Do:** The label says what the AI did; the tint and sparkle only reinforce it.

```tsx
<Cluster gap="sm">
  <Text as="span">Summary</Text>
  <AiMarker>Drafted with AI</AiMarker>
</Cluster>
```

**Don't:** A sparkle alone: colour and an icon aren’t a label, and it reads as decoration.

```tsx
<Cluster gap="sm">
  <Text as="span">Summary ✦</Text>
</Cluster>
```

**Accessibility**

- The text is the meaning (WCAG 1.4.1): it is read with the content, and the tint only reinforces it. The sparkle icon is hidden from assistive technology.
- Keep the label short and specific; it is read every time the content is.

Stories: `components-aimarker--badge`, `components-aimarker--inline`, `components-aimarker--custom-label`.
Composes: Icon.
Tokens read: `color.ai.bg`, `color.ai.border`, `color.ai.fg`, `font.weight.strong`, `icon.stroke`, `radius.pill`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.inset.2xs`, `space.inset.sm`, `text.caption`.

### Avatar

component · `src/components/Avatar/Avatar.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Avatar.usage.tsx`

Props:
- `name: string`: The person's name: the accessible name, and the source of the initials fallback. Required.
- `src?: string`: Photo URL. Falls back to initials when absent or when it fails to load.
- `size?: AvatarSize` = `'md'`
- `decorative?: boolean` = `false`: Hide from assistive tech when the name is already visible beside the avatar.
- …plus the native attributes of `AriaAttributes`, `Attributes`, `DOMAttributes`, `HTMLAttributes`, `RefAttributes`.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: size (sm | md | lg).
States: decorative.

**When to use**

- Showing who: record owners, activity authors, the signed-in user in the account menu trigger.

**When not to use**

- Representing a company, product or file → an icon or plain text
- The only place a person’s name appears in a list → the name as text, with the avatar beside it

**Do:** Beside the visible name, the avatar is `decorative`, so the name isn’t read twice.

```tsx
<Cluster gap="xs">
  <Avatar name="Sam Rivera" size="sm" decorative />
  <Text as="span">Sam Rivera</Text>
</Cluster>
```

**Don't:** A row of initials with no names: people have to hover to find out who is who.

```tsx
<Cluster gap="2xs">
  <Avatar name="Sam Rivera" size="sm" />
  <Avatar name="Alex Kim" size="sm" />
  <Avatar name="Jo Park" size="sm" />
</Cluster>
```

**Accessibility**

- `name` is required: it is the accessible name and the source of the initials fallback.
- Set `decorative` when the name is already visible next to it.

Stories: `components-avatar--initials`, `components-avatar--single-name`, `components-avatar--small`, `components-avatar--large`, `components-avatar--with-image`, `components-avatar--decorative`.
Tokens read: `color.bg.subtle`, `color.border.default`, `color.fg.default`, `font.weight.strong`, `radius.pill`, `size.avatar.lg`, `size.avatar.md`, `size.avatar.sm`, `text.caption`, `text.label`.

### Badge

component · `src/components/Badge/Badge.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Badge.usage.tsx`

Props:
- `tone?: BadgeTone` = `'neutral'`: Status tone. Map domain statuses to tones in one place; a new status extends the map, not the Badge.
- `indicator?: 'icon' | 'dot' | 'none'` = `'icon'`: Non-colour cue beside the text: a tone icon (default) or a dot.
- `children: string`: Text label. Required: status is never conveyed by colour alone.
- …plus the native attributes of `AriaAttributes`, `Attributes`, `DOMAttributes`, `HTMLAttributes`, `RefAttributes`.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: tone (success | warning | danger | info | neutral); indicator (icon | dot | none).

**When to use**

- A record’s status in a table row, title or card: a word plus a tone.
- Map domain statuses to tones in one place (the examples keep one status-to-tone map); a new status extends the map.

**When not to use**

- A message that needs a sentence or an action → `Banner`
- A count or a filter chip → text, or a proposal for a new component

**Do:** One short word per status, the same word everywhere it appears.

```tsx
<Cluster gap="xs">
  <Badge tone="success">Approved</Badge>
  <Badge tone="warning">Pending</Badge>
  <Badge tone="neutral">Draft</Badge>
</Cluster>
```

**Don't:** Sentences in badges, and a danger tone for something that isn’t a problem.

```tsx
<Cluster gap="xs">
  <Badge tone="danger">New feature available now</Badge>
</Cluster>
```

**Accessibility**

- Text is required: status is never colour alone, and tones add an icon or dot as a second cue.
- Tone text meets 4.5:1 on its background in light and dark.

Stories: `components-badge--success`, `components-badge--warning`, `components-badge--danger`, `components-badge--info`, `components-badge--neutral`, `components-badge--with-dot`, `components-badge--danger-with-dot`, `components-badge--text-only`.
Composes: Icon.
Tokens read: `color.status.danger.bg`, `color.status.danger.border`, `color.status.danger.fg`, `color.status.info.bg`, `color.status.info.border`, `color.status.info.fg`, `color.status.neutral.bg`, `color.status.neutral.border`, `color.status.neutral.fg`, `color.status.success.bg`, `color.status.success.border`, `color.status.success.fg`, `color.status.warning.bg`, `color.status.warning.border`, `color.status.warning.fg`, `font.weight.strong`, `icon.stroke`, `radius.pill`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.2xs`, `space.inset.sm`, `text.caption`.

### Banner

component · `src/components/Banner/Banner.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Banner.usage.tsx`

Ongoing state for a page or region: sits full width at the top of what it describes. Events get a Toast.

Props:
- `tone?: BannerTone` = `'info'`: Severity. Always shown as icon + text as well as colour.
- `title?: string`: Short bold lead ("Seat limit almost reached").
- `children: ReactNode`: One sentence, or a list of links (an error summary).
- `action?: ReactNode`: The fixing action, as a Button ("Add seats", "Review import").
- `onDismiss?: () => void`: Shows a dismiss button. The caller removes the banner.
- `dismissLabel?: string` = `'Dismiss'`
- `announce?: boolean` = `true`: Live-region semantics by tone: danger and warning are role="alert" (assertive), info and success role="status" (polite). Render the banner when the condition starts; a banner present at page load is announced too, so keep load-time banners rare. Set false when focus moves to the banner instead (an error summary): announcing it as well would say it twice. A banner that isn't announced but has a title becomes a named region, so moving focus to it (with tabIndex={-1}) still tells assistive technology what it is.
- …plus the native attributes of `AriaAttributes`, `Attributes`, `DOMAttributes`, `HTMLAttributes`, `RefAttributes`.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: tone (info | success | warning | danger).
States: announce.

**When to use**

- A page-level message that stays until it is resolved: a failed load, a limit reached, an error summary after submit.
- Put the fixing action in `action`.

**When not to use**

- A passing confirmation → `Toast`
- An error on one field → the field’s `error` prop
- Marketing or announcements → nothing in the product frame; they erode trust in real warnings

**Do:** What happened, then how to fix it, with the fix one click away.

```tsx
<Banner tone="warning" title="Seat limit almost reached" action={<Button variant="secondary" size="sm">Add seats</Button>}>
  9 of 10 seats are in use. New invites will fail at the limit.
</Banner>
```

**Don't:** A warning tone with no explanation or next step.

```tsx
<Banner tone="danger">Error.</Banner>
```

**Accessibility**

- Tone sets the live region: danger and warning are `role="alert"`, info and success `role="status"`.
- Render the banner when the condition starts; one already present on page load is not announced.
- Tone is shown as an icon and text as well as colour.

Stories: `components-banner--info`, `components-banner--success`, `components-banner--warning`, `components-banner--danger`, `components-banner--dismissible`, `components-banner--silent`.
Composes: Icon.
Tokens read: `color.fg.default`, `color.status.danger.bg`, `color.status.danger.border`, `color.status.danger.fg`, `color.status.info.bg`, `color.status.info.border`, `color.status.info.fg`, `color.status.success.bg`, `color.status.success.border`, `color.status.success.fg`, `color.status.warning.bg`, `color.status.warning.border`, `color.status.warning.fg`, `icon.stroke`, `radius.control`, `radius.surface`, `size.grid-item.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.target-min`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.md`, `text.body`, `text.label`.

### Breadcrumbs

component · `src/components/Breadcrumbs/Breadcrumbs.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Breadcrumbs.usage.tsx`

Path back up a genuinely nested hierarchy. A trail with no ancestors is decoration: leave it out.

Props:
- `items: readonly BreadcrumbLink[]`: Ancestors, outermost first. Every ancestor is a link.
- `current: string`: The current page: plain text with aria-current="page". Matches the page title.
- `label?: string` = `'Breadcrumb'`: Accessible name of the navigation landmark.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

**When to use**

- Pages below the top level (a record, a settings category) in AppShell’s `breadcrumbs` slot.

**When not to use**

- Top-level pages reached from the main nav → no breadcrumbs; the nav already shows where you are
- Steps in a flow → a heading that names the step

**Do:** Every ancestor is a link; the current page matches the page title.

```tsx
<Breadcrumbs items={[{ label: 'Records', href: '/records' }]} current="Hardware lease" />
```

**Don't:** History instead of hierarchy: the trail repeats where you clicked, not where the page lives.

```tsx
<Breadcrumbs
  label="Visited pages"
  items={[
    { label: 'Home', href: '/home' },
    { label: 'Search', href: '/search' },
    { label: 'Records', href: '/records' },
    { label: 'Search', href: '/search?q=lease' },
  ]}
  current="Hardware lease"
/>
```

**Accessibility**

- A labelled nav landmark with an ordered list; the current page is text with `aria-current="page"`.
- Separators are decorative and hidden from assistive tech.

Stories: `components-breadcrumbs--one-ancestor`, `components-breadcrumbs--deep-trail`.
Composes: Icon, Link.
Tokens read: `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.link`, `color.fg.muted`, `focus.ring.offset`, `focus.ring.width`, `icon.stroke`, `radius.indicator`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `space.gap.2xs`, `text.body`, `text.label`.

### Button

component · `src/components/Button/Button.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Button.usage.tsx`

Props:
- `children: ReactNode`: Visible label. Required: icon-only buttons need `aria-label` and a Tooltip.
- `variant?: ButtonVariant` = `'primary'`: Visual intent. A new look is a new variant here, never a new component.
- `size?: ButtonSize` = `'md'`
- `icon?: IconName`: Leading icon from the system set. Decorative: the label remains the accessible name.
- `loading?: boolean` = `false`: Pending state: shows a spinner, keeps the label (so the accessible name survives) and blocks activation with aria-disabled, so focus is not lost.
- …plus the native attributes of `AriaAttributes`, `Attributes`, `ButtonHTMLAttributes`, `DOMAttributes`, `HTMLAttributes`, `RefAttributes`.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: variant (primary | secondary | ghost | danger); size (sm | md | lg).
States: loading.

**When to use**

- To run an action on this page: save, create, delete, open a dialog.
- One `primary` per view for the main next step; `secondary` for the rest; `ghost` in dense rows and toolbars.
- `danger` for the action that destroys data, usually as the confirm button of a Dialog.

**When not to use**

- Going to another page or record → a link (`<a href>`), or a `Nav` or `Breadcrumbs` item
- Choosing one of several actions from a crowded header → `Menu` behind a "More" button
- Toggling a setting on or off → `Switch`

**Do:** One primary action, with the alternative as secondary. Labels are verb-first and say what happens.

```tsx
<Cluster gap="sm">
  <Button variant="secondary">Cancel</Button>
  <Button>Create record</Button>
</Cluster>
```

**Don't:** Two primaries compete for the same attention, and "OK" doesn’t say what it does.

```tsx
<Cluster gap="sm">
  <Button>Save draft</Button>
  <Button>OK</Button>
</Cluster>
```

**Accessibility**

- A visible label is required; it is the accessible name. An icon-only button needs `aria-label` and a `Tooltip`.
- `loading` keeps the button focusable and its name intact, and blocks activation with `aria-disabled`.
- Defaults to `type="button"`; set `type="submit"` on the form’s submit button.

Stories: `components-button--primary`, `components-button--secondary`, `components-button--ghost`, `components-button--danger`, `components-button--small`, `components-button--large`, `components-button--with-icon`, `components-button--loading`, `components-button--disabled`, `components-button--secondary-disabled`.
Composes: Icon, Spinner.
Tokens read: `button.danger.bg`, `button.danger.bg-hover`, `button.danger.fg`, `button.ghost.bg-hover`, `button.ghost.fg`, `button.primary.bg`, `button.primary.bg-hover`, `button.primary.fg`, `button.secondary.bg`, `button.secondary.bg-hover`, `button.secondary.border`, `button.secondary.fg`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.border.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.muted`, `ease.linear`, `ease.standard`, `focus.ring.width`, `icon.stroke`, `motion.fast`, `motion.spin`, `radius.control`, `radius.pill`, `size.control.lg`, `size.control.md`, `size.control.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.target-min`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.lg`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `text.body-lg`, `text.label`.

### Card

component · `src/components/Card/Card.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Card.usage.tsx`

A bounded surface for one titled block of a page: a record section, a settings group.

Props:
- `children: ReactNode`: CardHeader, CardBody and CardFooter, in that order. Each is optional.
- …plus the native attributes of `AriaAttributes`, `Attributes`, `DOMAttributes`, `HTMLAttributes`, `RefAttributes`.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

#### CardBody

component, part of Card.

Props:
- `children: ReactNode`

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`.

#### CardFooter

component, part of Card.

Props:
- `children: ReactNode`
- `justify?: 'end' | 'between'` = `'end'`: end: actions only. between: a status on the start side, actions on the end.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`.

#### CardHeader

component, part of Card.

Props:
- `title: string`: Section title. Required: a card without a title is just a box.
- `level?: HeadingLevel` = `2`: Outline level. Defaults to 2 (a section under the page's h1).
- `description?: string`: One line under the title: what the section controls.
- `actions?: ReactNode`: Small section-level actions, e.g. a ghost "Add" button.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`.

**When to use**

- One titled block of a page: a record section, a settings category with its own Save.
- Parts in order: `CardHeader` (title, description, small actions), `CardBody`, `CardFooter`.

**When not to use**

- Wrapping a whole page or a table → the page itself; a Table is already a surface
- Grouping without a title → a `Stack`: a card without a title is just a box

**Do:** A titled section that saves on its own.

```tsx
<Card>
  <CardHeader title="Notifications" level={4} description="How we contact you about your records." />
  <CardBody>
    <Switch label="Email me a weekly digest" defaultChecked />
  </CardBody>
  <CardFooter>
    <Button>Save</Button>
  </CardFooter>
</Card>
```

**Don't:** Cards nested in cards: the borders stack up and the hierarchy is lost.

```tsx
<Card>
  <CardHeader title="Profile" level={4} />
  <CardBody>
    <Stack>
      <Card>
        <CardHeader title="Name" level={4} />
      </Card>
    </Stack>
  </CardBody>
</Card>
```

**Accessibility**

- `CardHeader` requires a `title`, rendered as a heading at `level` (default 2) so the card is a section in the outline.
- Keep the card’s actions inside it, next to what they affect.

Stories: `components-card--default`, `components-card--footer-between`, `components-card--header-actions`, `components-card--body-only`.
Composes: Heading, Text.
Tokens read: `color.bg.subtle`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.muted`, `radius.surface`, `shadow.card`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.md`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `text.body`, `text.body-lg`, `text.caption`, `text.heading-1`, `text.heading-2`, `text.heading-3`, `text.heading-4`.

### ChatThread

component · `src/components/ChatThread/ChatThread.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/ChatThread.usage.tsx`

The list of turns in a conversation. It follows new output while the person is at the bottom, stops following when they scroll up (and offers "Jump to latest"). Scrolling itself, it is a named, focusable region, so it scrolls from the keyboard. It is deliberately not a live region: each answer's StreamingText announces sentences, so tokens are never read one by one.

Props:
- `label: string`: Accessible name of the thread ("Conversation about Master cleaning agreement"). Required.
- `children?: ReactNode`: The turns, oldest first: Message elements (give each a stable key).
- `empty?: ReactNode`: Shown instead of the thread when it has no turns: suggested prompts, not a blank box.
- `jumpLabel?: string` = `'Jump to latest'`: Label of the button that returns to the newest turn after scrolling up.
- `scroll?: 'self' | 'page'` = `'self'`: self: the thread scrolls in its own region, filling its container (a panel). page: the thread grows and the page's scroll region (AppShell's main) scrolls; it follows the output there (a full chat page, with the Composer in AppShell's footer).

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: scroll (self | page).

**When to use**

- The scrolling list of turns in a conversation with an assistant: in an `AssistantPanel` beside the page, or a full chat page.
- Give it the space to fill (a flex column); it follows new output while the person is at the bottom and offers “Jump to latest” when they scroll up.
- Pass suggested prompts as `empty`, never a blank box.
- On a full chat page set `scroll="page"`: the thread grows, AppShell’s main scrolls (the Composer goes in AppShell’s `footer`), and it follows the output there.

**When not to use**

- A record’s comments or activity → `Timeline`
- Notifications → `Toast` or an inbox list

**Do:** An empty thread offers prompts to start from.

```tsx
<ChatThread
  label="Conversation"
  empty={<EmptyState reason="first-use" title="Ask about this record" description="Answers cite its fields and activity." action={<Button variant="secondary">When does it renew?</Button>} />}
/>
```

**Don't:** Turns stacked as paragraphs: no roles, no authors, nothing to navigate by.

```tsx
<div>
  <Text>When does it renew?</Text>
  <Text>15 January 2027.</Text>
</div>
```

**Accessibility**

- The thread is a named, focusable region (`label`), so it scrolls from the keyboard; turns are a list.
- It is deliberately not a live region (`role="log"` would read every token): each answer’s `StreamingText` announces complete sentences instead.
- Scrolling keeps focus clear of “Jump to latest” (`space.scroll-padding.end`).

Stories: `components-chatthread--conversation`, `components-chatthread--streaming`, `components-chatthread--empty`, `components-chatthread--page-scroll`.
Composes: Button, Icon, Spinner.
Tokens read: `button.danger.bg`, `button.danger.bg-hover`, `button.danger.fg`, `button.ghost.bg-hover`, `button.ghost.fg`, `button.primary.bg`, `button.primary.bg-hover`, `button.primary.fg`, `button.secondary.bg`, `button.secondary.bg-hover`, `button.secondary.border`, `button.secondary.fg`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.border.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.muted`, `ease.linear`, `ease.standard`, `focus.ring.width`, `icon.stroke`, `motion.fast`, `motion.spin`, `radius.control`, `radius.pill`, `size.control.lg`, `size.control.md`, `size.control.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.target-min`, `space.gap.lg`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.lg`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.scroll-padding.end`, `text.body-lg`, `text.label`.

### Checkbox

component · `src/components/Checkbox/Checkbox.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Checkbox.usage.tsx`

Props:
- `label: string`: Visible label and accessible name. Required.
- `hideLabel?: boolean` = `false`: Keep the label for assistive tech only, when the context makes it obvious visually: a row's checkbox in a table ("Select Hardware lease"). The name must still say what is selected.
- `description?: string`
- `checked?: CheckedState`
- `defaultChecked?: CheckedState`
- `onCheckedChange?: (checked: CheckedState) => void`
- `disabled?: boolean`
- `required?: boolean`
- `name?: string`
- `value?: string`

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).
States: hideLabel, disabled, required.

**When to use**

- An independent yes/no inside a form that is saved with the form.
- Several independent choices from a short list; `indeterminate` for a “select all” parent.
- Row selection in a table: `hideLabel`, with a label naming the row (“Select Hardware lease”), so the name still says what is ticked.

**When not to use**

- A setting that applies immediately → `Switch`
- Exactly one of several options → `RadioGroup`

**Do:** Part of a form: nothing happens until Save.

```tsx
<Stack gap="md" align="start">
  <Checkbox label="Send a copy to the record owner" defaultChecked />
  <Button variant="secondary">Save</Button>
</Stack>
```

**Don't:** A negative label makes checked mean “no”. Phrase the option positively.

```tsx
<Checkbox label="Don’t send me updates" />
```

**Accessibility**

- `label` is required and clicking it toggles the box; `description` is linked to the control.
- The mixed state is exposed as `aria-checked="mixed"`, not only drawn.

Stories: `components-checkbox--unchecked`, `components-checkbox--checked`, `components-checkbox--indeterminate`, `components-checkbox--with-description`, `components-checkbox--disabled`, `components-checkbox--disabled-checked`, `components-checkbox--hidden-label`.
Composes: Icon.
Tokens read: `color.action.primary`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.fg.on-action`, `icon.stroke`, `radius.indicator`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.xs`, `text.body`, `text.caption`.

### Citation

component · `src/components/Citation/Citation.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Citation.usage.tsx`

A numbered inline citation, [1], that follows through to its source in a SourcesList: activating it moves focus to that source. It is a real link, never an inert label.

Props:
- `number: number`: The source's number, as it appears in the SourcesList (1-based).
- `sources: string`: The `id` of the SourcesList this cites.
- `title: string`: The source's title, for the accessible name ("Source 1: Renews on"). Required: a bare number means nothing when heard.
- `onActivate?: (number: number) => void`: Called when the citation is followed, with its number: highlight the source (and its passage) there.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

#### SourcesList

component, part of Citation. The numbered sources behind an answer, one card each (title, origin, excerpt, a link to the source). Citations in the text point here; the one followed last is marked with aria-current.

Props:
- `id: string`: Id that Citations point at (their `sources` prop). Use a useId() value: it must be unique on the page.
- `sources: readonly Source[]`
- `label?: string` = `'Sources'`: Heading above the list.
- `active?: number | undefined`: The source last followed from a Citation (1-based): marked as current.
- `summary?: ReactNode`: Rendered after the heading, before the list (a provenance line: "Based on 1 record and 3 activity entries").

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

**When to use**

- An AI answer that makes claims: number each claim’s source inline ([1]) and list the sources under the answer, each with where it came from and a link to it.
- Give the `SourcesList` a `useId()` id and pass it to every `Citation` as `sources`; `onActivate` highlights the source (and, in a record, the cited field).

**When not to use**

- Footnotes in content people wrote → a plain list of links
- A link to one page → `Link`

**Do:** Each claim cites a source that says where it came from and links to it.

```tsx
<Stack gap="sm">
  <Text>
    It renews on 15 January 2027
    <Citation number={1} sources="usage-sources" title="Renews on" />.
  </Text>
  <SourcesList id="usage-sources" sources={[{ title: 'Renews on', origin: 'Record field', excerpt: '15 Jan 2027', href: '#properties', hrefLabel: 'Show in record' }]} />
</Stack>
```

**Don't:** An inert “[1]”: a citation that can’t be followed is decoration, not provenance.

```tsx
<Text>It renews on 15 January 2027 [1].</Text>
```

**Accessibility**

- A citation is a real link named “Source 1: Renews on”, not the bare number; following it moves focus to the source, which is marked `aria-current`.
- Citations sit inside running text, so the inline exception to the 24px target size applies; don’t use them as standalone controls.

Stories: `components-citation--in-answer`, `components-citation--active-source`, `components-citation--sources-only`.
Composes: Link.
Tokens read: `color.bg.selected`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.fg.link`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.focus`, `focus.ring.offset`, `focus.ring.width`, `font.weight.strong`, `radius.control`, `radius.indicator`, `size.icon.sm`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.sm`, `text.body`, `text.caption`, `text.label`.

### CodeBlock

component · `src/components/CodeBlock/CodeBlock.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/CodeBlock.usage.tsx`

Monospaced code in a keyboard-scrollable region: long lines scroll sideways instead of wrapping, so what is copied is what is shown. An optional language label and a CopyButton sit above it.

Props:
- `code: string`: The code, shown exactly as given (leading and trailing blank lines are trimmed).
- `label: string`: Accessible name of the scrollable region and context for the copy button ("Install command"). Required.
- `language?: string`: Language shown in the header ("bash", "tsx"). A label only: there is no syntax highlighting.
- `copyable?: boolean` = `true`: Show a Copy button.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).
States: copyable.

**When to use**

- Code, commands, config or payloads that people read or copy: API docs, setup steps, a webhook sample.
- `label` names the region and the copy button (“Install command” → “Copy install command”). `language` is a label only; there is no syntax highlighting.

**When not to use**

- A short value inline in a sentence → `<code>` inside `Text`, with a `CopyButton` if it gets pasted
- Logs that stream or grow → a dedicated log viewer

**Do:** A labelled block: long lines scroll sideways, and copy takes exactly what is shown.

```tsx
<CodeBlock label="Install command" language="bash" code="npm install @acme/design-system" />
```

**Don't:** Code set in body text: it wraps, loses its spacing, and pasting it breaks.

```tsx
<Text>npm install @acme/design-system</Text>
```

**Accessibility**

- The code sits in a focusable `region` named by `label`, so keyboard users can scroll a long line (axe `scrollable-region-focusable`).
- The copy button is a `CopyButton`: it announces “Copied” politely.

Stories: `components-codeblock--default`, `components-codeblock--multi-line`, `components-codeblock--no-language`, `components-codeblock--not-copyable`.
Composes: Button, CopyButton, Icon, Spinner.
Tokens read: `button.danger.bg`, `button.danger.bg-hover`, `button.danger.fg`, `button.ghost.bg-hover`, `button.ghost.fg`, `button.primary.bg`, `button.primary.bg-hover`, `button.primary.fg`, `button.secondary.bg`, `button.secondary.bg-hover`, `button.secondary.border`, `button.secondary.fg`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.border.default`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.muted`, `ease.linear`, `ease.standard`, `focus.ring.width`, `icon.stroke`, `motion.fast`, `motion.spin`, `radius.control`, `radius.pill`, `size.control.lg`, `size.control.md`, `size.control.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.target-min`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.2xs`, `space.inset.lg`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `text.body-lg`, `text.caption`, `text.code`, `text.label`.

### Combobox

component · `src/components/Combobox/Combobox.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Combobox.usage.tsx`

A text field with a list of options that narrows as you type: choosing one value from many (an owner from 200 people, an account). Typing filters by a locale-aware "contains"; ↑ ↓ move, ↵ chooses, Esc closes. Behaviour, ARIA and focus come from React Aria's ComboBox.

Props:
- `label: string`: Visible label and accessible name. Required.
- `hideLabel?: boolean`
- `options: readonly ComboboxOption[]`
- `value?: string | null`: The chosen option's value, or null for none.
- `defaultValue?: string | null`
- `onValueChange?: (value: string | null) => void`
- `placeholder?: string`
- `description?: string`
- `error?: string`
- `size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'` = `'md'`
- `disabled?: boolean`
- `required?: boolean`
- `name?: string`: Form field name: the chosen value is submitted.
- `emptyMessage?: string` = `'No matches'`: Shown in the list when nothing matches what was typed.
- `showOptionsLabel?: string` = `'Show options'`: Accessible name of the button that opens the list.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean` = `false`: Render the list open (gallery and tests).

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: size (sm | md | lg).
States: hideLabel, disabled, required, defaultOpen.

**When to use**

- Choosing one value from a list too long to scan (people, accounts, countries): type to narrow it.
- A filter that picks one actor or one owner.

**When not to use**

- A short, fixed list (about 5–15 options) → `Select`
- Several values → `MultiSelect`
- Free text with suggestions, or jumping around the app → `SearchField`, or the `CommandPalette`

**Do:** A long list with a second line that tells similar names apart.

```tsx
<Combobox label="Owner" options={PEOPLE} defaultValue="p02" />
```

**Don't:** Three options behind typing: a Select (or radios) shows them at once.

```tsx
<Select
  label="Plan"
  options={[
    { value: 'free', label: 'Free' },
    { value: 'team', label: 'Team' },
    { value: 'enterprise', label: 'Enterprise' },
  ]}
/>
```

**Accessibility**

- React Aria’s combobox pattern: the input keeps focus, ↑ ↓ move through the list (announced), ↵ chooses, Esc closes; the button opens the list for pointer users.
- Label, description and error are wired by React Aria’s slots and laid out like every other field.
- Inside a Dialog the list portals into the dialog and Esc closes only the list.
- Typing matches with a locale-aware “contains”, so accents and case don’t get in the way.

Stories: `components-combobox--empty`, `components-combobox--with-value`, `components-combobox--with-description`, `components-combobox--with-error`, `components-combobox--disabled`, `components-combobox--small`, `components-combobox--large`, `components-combobox--open`, `components-combobox--in-dialog`.
Composes: Field, Icon, Picker.
Tokens read: `color.bg.elevated`, `color.bg.hover`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.link`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.focus`, `color.status.danger.fg`, `focus.ring.offset`, `focus.ring.width`, `icon.stroke`, `radius.control`, `radius.surface`, `shadow.popover`, `size.control.lg`, `size.control.md`, `size.control.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.overlay-max`, `size.target-min`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.2xs`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.inset.xs`, `text.body`, `text.body-lg`, `text.caption`, `text.label`, `z.dropdown`.

### CommandPalette

component · `src/components/CommandPalette/CommandPalette.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/CommandPalette.usage.tsx`

The command palette: type to jump to a page or record or run an action. A modal dialog with the ARIA combobox pattern: the input keeps focus, ↑ ↓ move the active option (aria-activedescendant), ↵ runs it, Esc closes and focus returns. Results are grouped, ranked forgivingly, and their count is announced. Open it with ⌘K / Ctrl+K from the app's shell composition (useShortcut), and pass only what the person may do.

Props:
- `open?: boolean`
- `defaultOpen?: boolean` = `false`
- `onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void`
- `groups: readonly CommandGroup[]`: Groups in order. A group with no matching items is left out.
- `query?: string`: Controlled query: pass it (and onQueryChange) when a group searches the server.
- `onQueryChange?: (query: string) => void`
- `label?: string` = `'Command palette'`: Accessible name of the dialog and the input.
- `placeholder?: string` = `'Search or jump to…'`
- `loading?: boolean` = `false`: A group is still searching: shows a spinner in the input and says so in the count.
- `emptyMessage?: string` = `'Nothing matches. Try another word.'`: Shown when nothing matches.
- `countMessage?: (count: number) => string` = `(count) => (count === 1 ? '1 result' : '${String(count)} results')`: Announced as the results change: `(count) => '12 results'`.
- `maxPerGroup?: number` = `6`: The most items a local group shows for a query (all of them with an empty query).
- `platform?: KeyPlatform`: Override the detected platform for key hints (gallery and tests).

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: platform (mac | other).
States: open, defaultOpen, loading.

**When to use**

- Once per app, in the shell composition, opened with ⌘K / Ctrl+K (`useShortcut` with `allowInInputs`) and from a Search button in the header that shows the keys.
- Jumping to any page or record and running actions by typing: pages from the route table, records from a server search (`filter: "none"`), actions that mirror buttons.

**When not to use**

- Searching one list → `SearchField` on the list page (its results stay in the page and the URL)
- Choosing a value for a form field → `Combobox`
- The only way to reach something → visible navigation and buttons first; the palette is the fast path

**Do:** Grouped rows with a type in the description and a shortcut where one exists; only what this person may do is passed in.

```tsx
<Button variant="secondary" icon="search">
  <span>Search</span> <Kbd keys="mod+k" />
</Button>
```

**Don't:** A search button with no sign of the shortcut: pointer users never learn ⌘K exists. (And never pass rows the person can’t run: filter with `can` first.)

```tsx
<Button variant="secondary" icon="search">Search</Button>
```

**Accessibility**

- A modal dialog (focus trapped, the page inert, Esc closes, focus returns) holding the ARIA combobox pattern: the input keeps focus and `aria-activedescendant` names the active option.
- The number of results is announced (`role="status"`) as the query changes; `countMessage` words it.
- ↑ ↓ wrap around the list, ↵ runs the active row, and pointer users can click any row. Shortcuts on rows are also `aria-keyshortcuts`.
- Keep labels verb-first for actions and give records a type in `description`, so a result is clear without seeing its group.

Stories: `components-commandpalette--open`, `components-commandpalette--filtered`, `components-commandpalette--matched-by-keyword`, `components-commandpalette--no-results`, `components-commandpalette--searching`.
Composes: Icon, Kbd, Spinner.
Tokens read: `color.bg.elevated`, `color.bg.scrim`, `color.bg.selected`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.focus`, `ease.linear`, `focus.ring.width`, `font.weight.strong`, `icon.stroke`, `motion.spin`, `radius.control`, `radius.indicator`, `radius.pill`, `radius.surface`, `shadow.modal`, `size.control.lg`, `size.control.md`, `size.dialog.md`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.scroll-region.lg`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.md`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.2xs`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.inset.xl`, `space.inset.xs`, `text.body`, `text.body-lg`, `text.caption`, `text.code`, `z.modal`.

### Composer

component · `src/components/Composer/Composer.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Composer.usage.tsx`

Where the person writes to the assistant: a text box that grows with its content, attachment chips, Send (or Stop while an answer arrives) and a keyboard hint. Enter sends and Shift+Enter adds a line, except while an IME composition is open.

Props:
- `label: string`: Accessible name of the text box ("Ask about this record"). Required; shown only to assistive technology.
- `placeholder?: string`
- `value?: string`: Controlled text. Pair with onValueChange.
- `defaultValue?: string` = `''`
- `onValueChange?: (value: string) => void`
- `onSend: (text: string) => void`: Send the message. Called with the trimmed text; the composer clears itself when uncontrolled.
- `streaming?: boolean` = `false`: An answer is arriving: Send becomes Stop, and Enter doesn't send. Typing the next question still works.
- `onStop?: () => void`: Stop the answer that is arriving.
- `maxLength?: number`: Characters allowed. The count shows from 80% of it; over the limit, Send is disabled with the reason.
- `attachments?: readonly ComposerAttachment[]` = `[]`: Chips for attached files, each with a Remove button.
- `onRemoveAttachment?: (id: string) => void`
- `onAttach?: (files: File[]) => void`: Shows an Attach button that opens the file picker.
- `disabled?: boolean` = `false`: The whole composer is unavailable (no permission, a hard limit reached). Say why in `note`.
- `note?: ReactNode` = `'AI can make mistakes. Check important info.'`: A quiet line under the box: the disclaimer, or why it's disabled.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).
States: streaming, disabled.

**When to use**

- Where the person writes to an assistant, pinned under a `ChatThread`: Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line, and the box grows with its content.
- Set `streaming` while an answer arrives: Send becomes Stop (`onStop`). Typing the next question still works.
- Keep the disclaimer (`note`) unless the surface shows it elsewhere; set `maxLength` when the model has a limit.

**When not to use**

- A search box → `SearchField`
- A comment on a record → `Textarea` with a Comment button

**Do:** Labelled, with the keys and the disclaimer under it.

```tsx
<Composer label="Ask about this record" placeholder="Ask about this record…" onSend={() => undefined} />
```

**Don't:** A one-line field with no Send button: multi-line questions are impossible and nothing says Enter sends.

```tsx
<TextField label="Ask" />
```

**Accessibility**

- The text box is labelled (`label`, visually hidden) and described by the key hint; the count joins the description from 80% of `maxLength`.
- Enter never sends during an IME composition. Over the limit, Send is disabled and the count says by how much; paste is never blocked.
- Stop is always reachable while an answer arrives.

Stories: `components-composer--empty`, `components-composer--with-text`, `components-composer--streaming`, `components-composer--with-attachments`, `components-composer--near-limit`, `components-composer--over-limit`, `components-composer--disabled`.
Composes: Button, Icon, Kbd, Spinner, Tag.
Tokens read: `button.danger.bg`, `button.danger.bg-hover`, `button.danger.fg`, `button.ghost.bg-hover`, `button.ghost.fg`, `button.primary.bg`, `button.primary.bg-hover`, `button.primary.fg`, `button.secondary.bg`, `button.secondary.bg-hover`, `button.secondary.border`, `button.secondary.fg`, `color.bg.hover`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.status.danger.fg`, `ease.linear`, `ease.standard`, `focus.ring.width`, `font.weight.strong`, `icon.stroke`, `motion.fast`, `motion.spin`, `radius.control`, `radius.indicator`, `radius.pill`, `radius.surface`, `size.control.lg`, `size.control.md`, `size.control.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.scroll-region.sm`, `size.target-min`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.2xs`, `space.inset.lg`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.inset.xs`, `text.body`, `text.body-lg`, `text.caption`, `text.code`, `text.label`.

### ContextMenu

component · `src/components/ContextMenu/ContextMenu.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/ContextMenu.usage.tsx`

Actions on a thing, where the pointer or focus is: right-click (or Shift+F10 on the focused element). A shortcut to actions that are also visible somewhere (a ⋯ Menu, a toolbar): nobody discovers a context menu, so it must never be the only way. Items look and read like Menu's. Behaviour from Radix ContextMenu.

Props:
- `children: ReactElement`: The region it belongs to: one focusable element (a row, a card). Right-click, a long press, Shift+F10 or the Menu key on it opens the menu.
- `items: readonly MenuEntry[]`: The same entries as Menu: items (with an optional shortcut) and 'separator'.
- `label?: string`: Optional non-interactive heading (what the menu acts on).
- `onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void`

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

**When to use**

- A shortcut to the actions on a row, card or list item that are also available elsewhere (a ⋯ menu, a toolbar).

**When not to use**

- The only way to reach an action → a visible `Menu` on the thing: nobody discovers a context menu
- Overriding the browser’s menu on text, links or images → leave the browser’s menu alone there

**Do:** The same items as the visible ⋯ menu, on a focusable region.

```tsx
<ContextMenu items={[{ label: 'Archive', shortcut: 'e' }, { label: 'Delete', tone: 'danger' }]}>
  <div tabIndex={0} role="group" aria-label="Northwind renewal">
    Northwind renewal <Menu trigger={<Button variant="ghost" icon="more" aria-label="More actions">More</Button>} items={[{ label: 'Archive' }, { label: 'Delete', tone: 'danger' }]} />
  </div>
</ContextMenu>
```

**Don't:** Actions that exist only on right-click: invisible to most people, and to keyboard users who don’t know Shift+F10.

```tsx
<ContextMenu items={[{ label: 'Delete', tone: 'danger' }]}>
  <div tabIndex={0} role="group" aria-label="Report">
    Report (no other way to delete it)
  </div>
</ContextMenu>
```

**Accessibility**

- Radix ContextMenu: opens on right-click, a long press, or Shift+F10 / the Menu key on the focused region; arrows, typeahead, Esc and focus return as in `Menu`.
- The region must be focusable and named, so keyboard users can reach it.
- Items look and read exactly like Menu’s, shortcuts included (`aria-keyshortcuts`).

Stories: `components-contextmenu--default`.
Composes: Icon, Kbd, Menu.
Tokens read: `color.bg.elevated`, `color.bg.hover`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.status.danger.bg`, `color.status.danger.fg`, `icon.stroke`, `radius.control`, `radius.indicator`, `radius.surface`, `shadow.popover`, `size.control.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.overlay-max`, `size.sidebar.sm`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.md`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.2xs`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.inset.xs`, `text.body`, `text.caption`, `text.code`, `z.dropdown`.

### CopyButton

component · `src/components/CopyButton/CopyButton.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/CopyButton.usage.tsx`

Copies a value to the clipboard, confirms with "Copied" in place and a polite announcement, then reverts. If the browser blocks the clipboard it says so and asks the user to copy by hand.

Props:
- `text: string`: The text put on the clipboard.
- `label?: string` = `'Copy'`: Visible label.
- `accessibleName?: string`: Accessible name when the label alone is ambiguous, starting with the label so speech input still matches it ("Copy API key"). Defaults to the label.
- `copiedLabel?: string` = `'Copied'`: Label shown, and announced, after a successful copy.
- `failedMessage?: string` = `'Couldn’t copy. Select the text and copy it instead.'`: Announced when the browser refuses the copy.
- `revertAfter?: number` = `2000`: How long "Copied" shows before the button reverts, in milliseconds.
- `variant?: 'secondary' | 'ghost'` = `'secondary'`
- `size?: ButtonSize` = `'sm'`
- `onCopy?: () => void`: Called after a successful copy.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: variant (secondary | ghost); size (sm | md | lg).

**When to use**

- A value people paste elsewhere: an API key, an invite link, an ID, a command.
- Set `accessibleName` when several copy buttons sit on one page (“Copy API key”); it starts with the visible label so voice control still matches.

**When not to use**

- Code or a command → `CodeBlock`, which includes one
- Sharing through the platform (email, Slack) → a `Button` that opens the share flow

**Do:** The value is visible, with a copy button beside it.

```tsx
<Cluster gap="sm">
  <Text as="span">
    <code>wsk_3f9a1c7e20b4</code>
  </Text>
  <CopyButton text="wsk_3f9a1c7e20b4" accessibleName="Copy API key" />
</Cluster>
```

**Don't:** A generic button that copies silently: nobody knows whether it worked.

```tsx
<Button variant="secondary" size="sm">
  Copy
</Button>
```

**Accessibility**

- On success the label reads “Copied” and a polite live region, present from mount, announces it; it reverts after `revertAfter` ms.
- If the browser blocks the clipboard, it announces `failedMessage`, so keep the value visible and selectable.

Stories: `components-copybutton--secondary`, `components-copybutton--ghost`, `components-copybutton--medium`, `components-copybutton--custom-labels`.
Composes: Button, Icon, Spinner.
Tokens read: `button.danger.bg`, `button.danger.bg-hover`, `button.danger.fg`, `button.ghost.bg-hover`, `button.ghost.fg`, `button.primary.bg`, `button.primary.bg-hover`, `button.primary.fg`, `button.secondary.bg`, `button.secondary.bg-hover`, `button.secondary.border`, `button.secondary.fg`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.border.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.muted`, `ease.linear`, `ease.standard`, `focus.ring.width`, `icon.stroke`, `motion.fast`, `motion.spin`, `radius.control`, `radius.pill`, `size.control.lg`, `size.control.md`, `size.control.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.target-min`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.lg`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `text.body-lg`, `text.label`.

### DatePicker

component · `src/components/DatePicker/DatePicker.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/DatePicker.usage.tsx`

A calendar date: typed segment by segment in the reader's locale order (from LocaleProvider), or picked from a calendar. Values are ISO strings ("2026-09-25"), calendar dates with no zone. Behaviour, ARIA and focus come from React Aria's DatePicker.

Props:
- `value?: IsoDate | null`
- `defaultValue?: IsoDate | null`
- `onValueChange?: (value: IsoDate | null) => void`
- `name?: string`: Form field name: the ISO date is submitted.
- `label: string`: Visible label and accessible name. Required.
- `hideLabel?: boolean`
- `min?: IsoDate`: Earliest date that can be chosen (ISO).
- `max?: IsoDate`: Latest date that can be chosen (ISO).
- `description?: string`
- `error?: string`
- `size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'` = `'md'`
- `disabled?: boolean`
- `required?: boolean`
- `calendarLabel?: string` = `'Choose a date'`: Accessible name of the button that opens the calendar.
- `previousMonthLabel?: string` = `'Previous month'`: Previous and next month buttons.
- `nextMonthLabel?: string` = `'Next month'`
- `defaultOpen?: boolean` = `false`: Render the calendar open (gallery and tests).

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: size (sm | md | lg).
States: hideLabel, disabled, required, defaultOpen.

#### DateRangePicker

component, part of DatePicker. A range of calendar dates, start to end: typed or picked in one calendar. Values are ISO strings. To filter instants (an audit log's "from" and "to"), turn the range into the start of the first day and the end of the last in the reader's time zone, never UTC midnight.

Props:
- `value?: DateRange | null`
- `defaultValue?: DateRange | null`
- `onValueChange?: (value: DateRange | null) => void`
- `startName?: string`: Form field names for the two ends.
- `endName?: string`
- `label: string`: Visible label and accessible name. Required.
- `hideLabel?: boolean`
- `min?: IsoDate`: Earliest date that can be chosen (ISO).
- `max?: IsoDate`: Latest date that can be chosen (ISO).
- `description?: string`
- `error?: string`
- `size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'` = `'md'`
- `disabled?: boolean`
- `required?: boolean`
- `calendarLabel?: string` = `'Choose dates'`: Accessible name of the button that opens the calendar.
- `previousMonthLabel?: string` = `'Previous month'`: Previous and next month buttons.
- `nextMonthLabel?: string` = `'Next month'`
- `defaultOpen?: boolean` = `false`: Render the calendar open (gallery and tests).

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

**When to use**

- A calendar date: a renewal, a due date, a birthday. Typed in the reader’s own order, or picked.
- Values that are ISO calendar dates (“2026-09-25”), which is how the app passes them.

**When not to use**

- A start and an end → `DateRangePicker`
- A moment in time (with an hour) → a date and a time, stored as an instant; show it with `useFormat().dateTime`
- Showing a date → `useFormat().date(iso)`

**Do:** Segments in the reader’s locale order (LocaleProvider), with the earliest allowed date set.

```tsx
<DatePicker label="Renews on" defaultValue="2026-10-14" min="2026-09-25" />
```

**Don't:** A free-text date: ambiguous (is 03/04 March or April?) and parsed by hand.

```tsx
<TextField label="Renews on" placeholder="MM/DD/YYYY" />
```

**Accessibility**

- Each segment (day, month, year) is a spin button: type digits or use ↑ ↓; the calendar button opens a grid navigable with the arrow keys, Page Up/Down for months.
- The locale comes from LocaleProvider, the same one `useFormat()` uses, so typed and displayed dates agree; the calendar opens on today in the provider’s time zone.
- Inside a Dialog the calendar portals into it and Esc closes only the calendar.

Stories: `components-datepicker--empty`, `components-datepicker--with-value`, `components-datepicker--with-description`, `components-datepicker--with-error`, `components-datepicker--disabled`, `components-datepicker--small`, `components-datepicker--open`, `components-datepicker--german`, `components-datepicker--in-dialog`.
Composes: Field, Icon, Picker.
Tokens read: `color.action.primary`, `color.bg.elevated`, `color.bg.hover`, `color.bg.selected`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.link`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.fg.on-action`, `color.focus`, `color.status.danger.fg`, `focus.ring.offset`, `focus.ring.width`, `icon.stroke`, `radius.control`, `radius.indicator`, `radius.surface`, `shadow.popover`, `size.control.lg`, `size.control.md`, `size.control.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.overlay-max`, `size.target-min`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.2xs`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.inset.xs`, `text.body`, `text.body-lg`, `text.caption`, `text.label`, `z.dropdown`.

### Dialog

component · `src/components/Dialog/Dialog.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Dialog.usage.tsx`

Modal dialog. Focus trap, Escape, scroll lock and focus return come from Radix Dialog.

Props:
- `title: string`: Accessible name and visible title. Required.
- `description?: string`: Short supporting text, announced with the title.
- `trigger?: ReactElement`: Element that opens the dialog, typically a system Button.
- `open?: boolean`
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`
- `onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void`
- `size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'` = `'md'`
- `footer?: ReactNode`: Actions row. Put the primary action last.
- `closeLabel?: string` = `'Close'`: Label of the close button (icon-only, so it needs a name).
- `children?: ReactNode`

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: size (sm | md | lg).
States: open, defaultOpen.

**When to use**

- Confirming a destructive or irreversible action (`size="sm"`, danger button that repeats the verb).
- A quick create or edit of a light record: two or three fields.

**When not to use**

- A long or multi-step form → a full page from the Create and edit example
- Telling people something happened → `Toast` or `Banner`
- Choosing an action → `Menu`

**Do:** A focused quick-create: a short title, the fields, and the primary action last.

```tsx
<Dialog
  title="New record"
  description="Records start as drafts."
  trigger={<Button icon="plus">New record</Button>}
  footer={
    <>
      <Button variant="secondary">Cancel</Button>
      <Button>Create record</Button>
    </>
  }
>
  <TextField label="Name" />
</Dialog>
```

**Don't:** A vague confirm: “Are you sure?” with “OK” forces people to reread what they clicked.

```tsx
<Cluster>
  <Dialog
    size="sm"
    title="Are you sure?"
    trigger={<Button variant="danger">Delete record</Button>}
    footer={
      <>
        <Button variant="secondary">Cancel</Button>
        <Button>OK</Button>
      </>
    }
  />
</Cluster>
```

**Accessibility**

- `title` is required and names the dialog; `description` is announced with it.
- Focus moves into the dialog, is trapped there, and returns to the trigger on close. Escape closes it.
- The close button is icon-only, so it has a name (`closeLabel`, default “Close”).

Stories: `components-dialog--closed`, `components-dialog--open`, `components-dialog--small`, `components-dialog--large`, `components-dialog--without-description`.
Composes: Icon.
Tokens read: `color.bg.elevated`, `color.bg.hover`, `color.bg.scrim`, `color.border.default`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.muted`, `icon.stroke`, `radius.control`, `radius.surface`, `shadow.modal`, `size.control.sm`, `size.dialog.lg`, `size.dialog.md`, `size.dialog.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `space.gap.md`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.lg`, `space.inset.md`, `text.body`, `text.heading-3`, `z.modal`.

### Disclosure

component · `src/components/Disclosure/Disclosure.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Disclosure.usage.tsx`

One section that shows and hides its details: an assistant's tool activity or reasoning, an advanced option. The toggle is a button with aria-expanded; from Radix Collapsible. For a stack of sections where opening one may close another, use Accordion.

Props:
- `summary: string`: The always-visible summary, and the toggle's accessible name ("Searched 12 records"). Required.
- `meta?: ReactNode`: Beside the summary: a status Badge ("Done"), a count. Not part of the toggle.
- `children: ReactNode`: What opens: tool input and output, reasoning steps, details.
- `open?: boolean`
- `defaultOpen?: boolean` = `false`: Closed by default: details are there when wanted, not in the way.
- `onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void`

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).
States: open, defaultOpen.

**When to use**

- One section of details people sometimes want: an assistant’s tool activity (what it searched, what it found), its reasoning, an advanced option.
- Closed by default; the summary says what’s inside (“Searched 12 records”), with a status in `meta`.

**When not to use**

- Several related sections, one open at a time → `Accordion`
- Panels the person switches between → `Tabs`
- Content everyone needs → show it; don’t hide it behind a toggle

**Do:** The summary says what happened; the details are one click away.

```tsx
<Disclosure summary="Searched records matching “overdue”" meta={<Badge tone="success">Done</Badge>}>
  <Text>12 records matched. 2 are archived and were left out.</Text>
</Disclosure>
```

**Don't:** A vague summary: nobody knows whether it’s worth opening.

```tsx
<Disclosure summary="Details">
  <Text>12 records matched.</Text>
</Disclosure>
```

**Accessibility**

- The toggle is a button with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` (Radix Collapsible); Enter and Space toggle it.
- Content that opens is in the reading order right after the toggle, so nothing is lost when it opens.

Stories: `components-disclosure--closed`, `components-disclosure--open`, `components-disclosure--with-meta`.
Composes: Icon.
Tokens read: `color.bg.hover`, `color.fg.default`, `ease.standard`, `icon.stroke`, `motion.fast`, `radius.control`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.target-min`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.2xs`, `space.inset.lg`, `text.body`, `text.label`.

### Divider

component · `src/components/Divider/Divider.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Divider.usage.tsx`

A hairline between blocks or inline groups. Prefer space (the gap of a Stack or Cluster) and headings to separate content; a line is for when space alone doesn't read as a boundary. Behaviour from Radix Separator.

Props:
- `orientation?: 'horizontal' | 'vertical'` = `'horizontal'`
- `decorative?: boolean` = `true`: true (the default): a visual line only, hidden from assistive technology. false: role="separator", for a line that divides groups of content people navigate between, such as groups of toolbar controls.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: orientation (horizontal | vertical).
States: decorative.

**When to use**

- A boundary that space alone doesn’t make clear: between a form and its danger zone, between groups of toolbar controls.
- `decorative` (the default) hides it from assistive technology. Set `decorative={false}` only when it divides groups people navigate between; it becomes a `separator`.

**When not to use**

- Separating every item in a list or form → the gap of a `Stack`, and headings for sections
- Framing a group → `Card`

**Do:** One line where the content changes kind.

```tsx
<Stack gap="md">
  <Text>Billing contact and invoices.</Text>
  <Divider />
  <Text>Danger zone: delete this workspace.</Text>
</Stack>
```

**Don't:** A line between every paragraph: the page turns into stripes and nothing stands out.

```tsx
<Stack gap="xs">
  <Text>Name</Text>
  <Divider />
  <Text>Email</Text>
  <Divider />
  <Text>Phone</Text>
</Stack>
```

**Accessibility**

- Decorative dividers are hidden; semantic ones are `role="separator"` with their orientation. From Radix Separator.

Stories: `components-divider--horizontal`, `components-divider--vertical`, `components-divider--semantic`.
Tokens read: `color.border.default`.

### Drawer

component · `src/components/Drawer/Drawer.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Drawer.usage.tsx`

Modal side sheet over a scrim. Focus trap, Escape, scroll lock, outside click and focus return come from Radix Dialog; this component only lays it along an edge.

Props:
- `title: string`: Accessible name, and the visible title unless hideTitle. Required.
- `hideTitle?: boolean` = `false`: Keep the title as the accessible name but don't show it (a navigation drawer that shows the brand instead).
- `description?: string`: Short supporting text, announced with the title.
- `side?: 'start' | 'end'` = `'end'`: The edge it slides from. end (default) for details and filters; start for navigation.
- `size?: 'sm' | 'md'` = `'md'`: Width: sm for navigation, md (default) for details and filters.
- `trigger?: ReactElement`: Element that opens the drawer, typically a system Button. It gets aria-expanded and aria-controls.
- `open?: boolean`
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`
- `onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void`
- `footer?: ReactNode`: Actions pinned to the bottom. Put the primary action last.
- `closeLabel?: string` = `'Close'`: Label of the close button (icon-only, so it needs a name).
- `children?: ReactNode`

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: side (start | end); size (sm | md).
States: hideTitle, open, defaultOpen.

**When to use**

- A side sheet over the page for work that needs the page as context: a record’s details from a list, a longer set of filters, navigation on a narrow screen.
- `side="end"` (default) for details and filters; `side="start"` with `size="sm"` for navigation. AppShell already opens its nav this way on narrow screens.
- Put the primary action last in `footer`; it stays pinned while the body scrolls.

**When not to use**

- A short confirmation or a small form → `Dialog`
- Three or four quick filter options → `Popover`
- Content people need beside the page while they keep working in it → `PageLayout`’s aside

**Do:** Filters in a drawer from the end, opened by a labelled button, applied from the footer.

```tsx
<Drawer
  title="Filters"
  description="Narrow the list. Applies when you choose Show."
  trigger={<Button variant="secondary">Filters</Button>}
  footer={<Button>Show 12 records</Button>}
>
  <Checkbox label="Active" defaultChecked />
</Drawer>
```

**Don't:** A confirmation in a drawer: a full-height sheet for one sentence and two buttons; a Dialog is the right size.

```tsx
<Stack gap="xs" align="start">
  <Drawer title="Delete record?" description="This cannot be undone." trigger={<Button variant="danger">Delete record</Button>} />
  <Dialog title="Delete record?" description="This cannot be undone." trigger={<Button variant="secondary">Dialog instead</Button>} />
</Stack>
```

**Accessibility**

- A modal dialog named by its required `title` (kept as the name when `hideTitle` hides it). Focus moves in, stays trapped, and returns to the trigger on close.
- Escape, the close button (named by `closeLabel`) and a click on the scrim all close it; the page behind is inert.
