- The trigger gets `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` automatically.

Stories: `components-drawer--closed`, `components-drawer--end-open`, `components-drawer--start-open`, `components-drawer--without-footer`.
Composes: Icon.
Tokens read: `color.bg.elevated`, `color.bg.hover`, `color.bg.scrim`, `color.border.default`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.muted`, `icon.stroke`, `radius.control`, `shadow.modal`, `size.control.sm`, `size.drawer.md`, `size.drawer.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `space.gap.md`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.lg`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.scroll-padding.end`, `text.body`, `text.heading-3`, `z.modal`.

### EmptyState

component · `src/components/EmptyState/EmptyState.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/EmptyState.usage.tsx`

What a list, table or panel shows instead of its content. Render it or the content, never both.

Props:
- `reason: EmptyStateReason`
- `title: string`: "Create your first record" · "No records match" · "Couldn't load records". Required.
- `description?: string`: One sentence: what fills this space, how to widen the search, or what failed.
- `action?: ReactNode`: One action. first-use: the same action as the page's primary button. no-results: clear filters. error: Retry.
- `headingLevel?: HeadingLevel` = `2`: Outline level of the title. Defaults to 2 (a region inside a page with an h1).

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: reason (first-use | no-results | error); headingLevel (1 | 2 | 3 | 4).

**When to use**

- In place of a list or table that has nothing to show, with the `reason`: `first-use`, `no-results` or `error`.
- Render it instead of the table, never beside an empty one.

**When not to use**

- Content that is still loading → `Skeleton`
- An error on a page that otherwise works → `Banner`

**Do:** Say what goes here and offer the one action that fills it.

```tsx
<EmptyState
  reason="first-use"
  headingLevel={4}
  title="Create your first record"
  description="Records track agreements from draft to renewal."
  action={<Button icon="plus">New record</Button>}
/>
```

**Don't:** A dead end: no explanation and no way forward.

```tsx
<EmptyState reason="no-results" headingLevel={4} title="Nothing here" />
```

**Accessibility**

- The title is a real heading (`headingLevel`, default 2) so the state is findable in the outline.
- The icon is decorative; the title and description carry the meaning.

Stories: `components-emptystate--first-use`, `components-emptystate--no-results`, `components-emptystate--load-error`, `components-emptystate--without-action`.
Composes: Heading, Icon, Text.
Tokens read: `color.bg.subtle`, `color.border.default`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.status.danger.bg`, `color.status.danger.fg`, `icon.stroke`, `radius.pill`, `radius.surface`, `size.control.lg`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.overlay-max`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.md`, `space.inset.lg`, `space.inset.xl`, `text.body`, `text.body-lg`, `text.caption`, `text.heading-1`, `text.heading-2`, `text.heading-3`, `text.heading-4`.

### Feedback

component · `src/components/Feedback/Feedback.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Feedback.usage.tsx`

Thumbs up or down on one AI result, with an optional reason after a thumbs down. Both are toggle buttons (aria-pressed) with visible labels; a polite status confirms what was sent.

Props:
- `onFeedback: (feedback: FeedbackValue) => void`: Called on a thumbs up at once, and on a thumbs down when the reason is sent or skipped.
- `label?: string` = `'Rate this answer'`: Names what is being rated, for the group's accessible name ("Rate this answer").
- `reasons?: readonly string[]` = `REASONS`: Choices offered after a thumbs down. Keep them few and specific.
- `thanks?: string` = `'Thanks. Feedback helps us check and improve answers.'`: Shown, and announced, once feedback is sent: say what it's for.
- `defaultValue?: FeedbackValue`: A rating already given (a reloaded conversation).

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

**When to use**

- Under an AI result (an answer, a summary, a suggestion) to learn whether it helped.
- A thumbs down asks for a reason, which the person can skip. Say what feedback is for in `thanks`.

**When not to use**

- Rating the product or a support conversation → a survey, not per-result feedback
- Reporting harmful content → a “Report” action that reaches a person

**Do:** Two labelled toggles; the reason comes only after a thumbs down.

```tsx
<Feedback onFeedback={() => undefined} />
```

**Don't:** Unlabelled buttons that don’t say whether anything was sent.

```tsx
<Cluster gap="xs">
  <Button variant="ghost" size="sm">
    👍
  </Button>
  <Button variant="ghost" size="sm">
    👎
  </Button>
</Cluster>
```

**Accessibility**

- Both are toggle buttons with visible labels (“Helpful”, “Not helpful”) and `aria-pressed`, in a group named by `label`.
- A polite status, present from mount, announces the thanks once feedback is sent.

Stories: `components-feedback--not-rated`, `components-feedback--rated-helpful`, `components-feedback--rated-not-helpful`, `components-feedback--custom-reasons`.
Composes: Button, Field, Icon, RadioGroup, Spinner, Toggle.
Tokens read: `button.danger.bg`, `button.danger.bg-hover`, `button.danger.fg`, `button.ghost.bg-hover`, `button.ghost.fg`, `button.primary.bg`, `button.primary.bg-hover`, `button.primary.fg`, `button.secondary.bg`, `button.secondary.bg-hover`, `button.secondary.border`, `button.secondary.fg`, `color.action.primary`, `color.bg.hover`, `color.bg.selected`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.status.danger.fg`, `ease.linear`, `ease.standard`, `focus.ring.width`, `font.weight.strong`, `icon.stroke`, `motion.fast`, `motion.spin`, `radius.control`, `radius.pill`, `size.control.lg`, `size.control.md`, `size.control.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.target-min`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.md`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.lg`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.inset.xs`, `text.body`, `text.body-lg`, `text.caption`, `text.label`.

### FileUpload

component · `src/components/FileUpload/FileUpload.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/FileUpload.usage.tsx`

Picks files with a button (the primary path) and, as an enhancement, accepts files dropped on its area. Shows the accepted types and size limit up front, then each file with its progress, its own error and a remove button. It validates type and size; the caller uploads.

Props:
- `label: string`: Visible label and the group's accessible name ("Attachments"). Required.
- `description?: string`: Supporting text above the limits.
- `error?: string`: Error for the field as a whole ("Add at least one file"). Errors about one file go on that file.
- `id?: string`: Id of the Choose files button, for an error summary link. Generated when omitted.
- `accept?: readonly string[]`: Accepted types: extensions (".pdf") and MIME types ("image/png", "image/*"). Checked on pick and on drop.
- `acceptText?: string`: The accepted types in words, shown to everyone before they pick ("PDF, PNG or JPG").
- `maxSize?: number`: Largest file allowed, in bytes. Shown with the types.
- `multiple?: boolean` = `true`: Allow more than one file per pick.
- `files: readonly FileUploadItem[]`: Files picked so far, with their progress and errors.
- `onFilesAdded: (accepted: File[], rejected: FileRejection[]) => void`: Called with the files that passed the limits and the ones that didn't.
- `onRemove: (id: string) => void`: Remove (or cancel) one file. Focus moves to the next file, or back to Choose files.
- `browseLabel?: string` = `'Choose files'`: Label of the button that opens the file picker: the primary way in.
- `dropText?: string` = `'or drop them here'`: Text beside the button, for people who can drag.
- `disabled?: boolean` = `false`

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).
States: multiple, disabled.

**When to use**

- Attaching files to a record or a form: contracts, receipts, images.
- Say the limits before anyone picks: `acceptText` (“PDF, PNG or JPG”) and `maxSize`. Pass the same types as `accept`; the component checks type and size on pick and on drop, and hands you the accepted files and the rejections with ready-made messages.
- You own the list: add accepted files to `files`, set `progress` while each uploads, set `error` on the one that failed, and remove on `onRemove`. Focus moves to the next file, or back to Choose files.

**When not to use**

- Importing a spreadsheet of records → a dedicated import flow (a `FocusedLayout` wizard) that maps columns and previews rows
- A person’s photo → the same component with `multiple={false}` and an image `accept`, previewed in a `Frame`

**Do:** The limits are visible up front; each file shows its own progress or its own error.

```tsx
<FileUpload
  label="Attachments"
  accept={['.pdf', 'image/png', 'image/jpeg']}
  acceptText="PDF, PNG or JPG"
  maxSize={10 * MB}
  files={[
    { id: '1', name: 'Signed contract.pdf', size: 2.4 * MB, progress: 40 },
    { id: '2', name: 'Survey scan.png', size: 14 * MB, error: 'Larger than 10 MB. Choose a smaller file.' },
  ]}
  onFilesAdded={noop}
  onRemove={noop}
/>
```

**Don't:** No limits until after the upload fails, and one error for the whole batch that doesn’t say which file.

```tsx
<FileUpload label="Attachments" error="Some files could not be uploaded." files={[]} onFilesAdded={noop} onRemove={noop} />
```

**Accessibility**

- The Choose files button is the primary path; dropping files on the area is an enhancement, declared with `data-drag-alternative` (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7).
- A group named by the label. The button is described by the label, the limits and any error; `id` lands on it for an error summary link.
- Adding files is announced politely (“2 files added, 1 file not added”). Each upload is a `Progress` named by the file.
- Remove buttons are named per file (“Remove Signed contract.pdf”, “Cancel …” while uploading) and meet the 24px target size.

Stories: `components-fileupload--empty`, `components-fileupload--with-description`, `components-fileupload--uploading`, `components-fileupload--uploaded`, `components-fileupload--file-errors`, `components-fileupload--field-error`, `components-fileupload--disabled`, `components-fileupload--single-file`, `components-fileupload--interactive`.
Composes: Button, Field, Icon, Progress, Spinner.
Tokens read: `button.danger.bg`, `button.danger.bg-hover`, `button.danger.fg`, `button.ghost.bg-hover`, `button.ghost.fg`, `button.primary.bg`, `button.primary.bg-hover`, `button.primary.fg`, `button.secondary.bg`, `button.secondary.bg-hover`, `button.secondary.border`, `button.secondary.fg`, `color.action.primary`, `color.bg.hover`, `color.bg.selected`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.status.danger.fg`, `ease.linear`, `ease.standard`, `focus.ring.width`, `icon.stroke`, `motion.fast`, `motion.spin`, `radius.control`, `radius.pill`, `radius.surface`, `size.bar`, `size.control.lg`, `size.control.md`, `size.control.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.target-min`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.lg`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.inset.xs`, `text.body`, `text.body-lg`, `text.caption`, `text.label`.

### Heading

component · `src/components/Heading/Heading.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Heading.usage.tsx`

Props:
- `children: ReactNode`
- `level: HeadingLevel`: Document outline level. Required: never skip levels to get a size.
- `size?: HeadingLevel` = `level`: Visual size, when it must differ from the level. Defaults to the level.
- …plus the native attributes of `AriaAttributes`, `Attributes`, `DOMAttributes`, `HTMLAttributes`, `RefAttributes`.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: level (1 | 2 | 3 | 4); size (1 | 2 | 3 | 4).

**When to use**

- Page titles (`level={1}`, one per page) and section titles, in outline order.
- When the look must differ from the outline, keep the right `level` and set `size`.

**When not to use**

- Making text bigger or bolder for emphasis → `Text` with `size="body-lg"`, or `<strong>`
- A card or empty-state title → the `title` prop of `CardHeader` or `EmptyState`, which renders the heading for you

**Do:** Levels follow the outline; the section title is visually smaller with `size`, not a skipped level.

```tsx
<Stack gap="xs">
  <Heading level={3}>Billing</Heading>
  <Heading level={4} size={4}>
    Payment method
  </Heading>
  <Text tone="muted">Visa ending 4242</Text>
</Stack>
```

**Don't:** A heading used as a label for a value: it adds noise to the outline screen-reader users navigate by.

```tsx
<Stack gap="xs">
  <Heading level={4}>Owner</Heading>
  <Text>Sam Rivera</Text>
</Stack>
```

**Accessibility**

- `level` is required, so the outline is always a deliberate choice. Never skip a level to get a size.
- Exactly one `level={1}` per page, matching the page title and the breadcrumb’s current item.

Stories: `components-heading--level-1`, `components-heading--level-2`, `components-heading--level-3`, `components-heading--level-4`, `components-heading--level-2-at-size-4`.
Tokens read: `color.fg.default`, `text.heading-1`, `text.heading-2`, `text.heading-3`, `text.heading-4`.

### HoverCard

component · `src/components/HoverCard/HoverCard.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/HoverCard.usage.tsx`

A supplementary preview of a link's destination, shown on hover and focus. Supplementary only: screen readers and touch never get it, so everything in it must also be at the destination. Behaviour from Radix HoverCard.

Props:
- `trigger: ReactElement`: A link (or other focusable element) that already leads to the full content. The card opens on hover and on keyboard focus; it never opens on touch, so the trigger must work without it.
- `children: ReactNode`: A preview of what the trigger leads to: a person's role, a record's status. Nothing interactive.
- `side?: 'top' | 'right' | 'bottom' | 'left'` = `'bottom'`
- `align?: 'start' | 'center' | 'end'` = `'start'`
- `open?: boolean`
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`
- `onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void`

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: side (top | right | bottom | left); align (start | center | end).
States: open, defaultOpen.

**When to use**

- A preview of where a link goes: a person’s role and team behind their name, a record’s status behind its ID.
- Supplementary only. It opens on hover and keyboard focus, never on touch, and screen readers don’t reach its content, so everything in it must also be on the page the trigger leads to.

**When not to use**

- Anything people need to finish the task → show it on the page
- Buttons, links or fields → `Popover` (opens on click and takes focus)
- Naming an icon button → `Tooltip`

**Do:** The trigger is a link to the full profile; the card previews it.

```tsx
<HoverCard trigger={<Link href="#people/priya">Priya Shah</Link>}>
  <Stack gap="2xs">
    <Text>Priya Shah</Text>
    <Text size="caption" tone="muted">
      Finance lead
    </Text>
  </Stack>
</HoverCard>
```

**Don't:** A trigger that goes nowhere, with the only copy of the approver’s decision in the card.

```tsx
<HoverCard trigger={<Link href="#">Approval</Link>}>
  <Text>Rejected: the amount exceeds the budget.</Text>
</HoverCard>
```

**Accessibility**

- The trigger must be focusable (a `Link`); the card opens on focus and closes on blur and Escape.
- The content isn’t focusable and isn’t announced. Keep it non-interactive and duplicated at the destination.

Stories: `components-hovercard--closed`, `components-hovercard--open`, `components-hovercard--open-top`.
Tokens read: `color.bg.elevated`, `color.border.default`, `color.fg.default`, `radius.surface`, `shadow.popover`, `size.overlay-max`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.md`, `text.body`, `z.dropdown`.

### InlineEdit

component · `src/components/InlineEdit/InlineEdit.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/InlineEdit.usage.tsx`

A value you can change where it's shown: view → edit → save or cancel. Enter saves, Escape cancels, and focus returns to the value either way. Validation and the server's answer show under the field without losing what was typed. For one value at a time (a name, a title); a form with several fields is a form.

Props:
- `label: string`: What the value is ("Name"). The field's label and the edit button's name ("Edit Name"). Required.
- `value: string`
- `onSave: (value: string) => unknown`: Save the new value. Return (or resolve to) an error message string to stay in edit mode with it; anything else means saved. While a returned promise is pending, Save shows its pending state; a rejected promise keeps edit mode with `failedMessage`.
- `validate?: (value: string) => string | undefined`: Check before saving: a message when the value can't be saved.
- `placeholder?: string` = `'Empty'`: Shown in view mode when the value is empty.
- `disabledReason?: string`: View only, with the reason as the edit button's description (no permission, archived…).
- `editLabel?: string` = `'Edit ${label}'`: Accessible names of the actions.
- `saveLabel?: string` = `'Save'`
- `cancelLabel?: string` = `'Cancel'`
- `failedMessage?: string` = `'Couldn’t save. Try again.'`: Shown when `onSave` throws or rejects.
- `defaultEditing?: boolean` = `false`: Start in edit mode (gallery and tests).
- `defaultDraft?: string`: Start in edit mode with this draft and its error (gallery and tests).

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).
States: defaultEditing.

**When to use**

- Changing one value where it’s shown: a record’s name in its header, a label in a table cell.
- Frequent small edits by people who own the thing.

**When not to use**

- Several fields that belong together → a form (`CreateEditFlow`), or a Dialog
- A value that needs a long explanation or a review step → a form with its description and a Save button

**Do:** The value is the edit button; Enter saves, Escape cancels, focus comes back to the value.

```tsx
<InlineEdit label="Name" value="Northwind renewal" onSave={noop} />
```

**Don't:** An always-open field for a value people rarely change: it looks like a form waiting to be filled.

```tsx
<TextField label="Name" defaultValue="Northwind renewal" />
```

**Accessibility**

- View mode is a button named “Edit <label>: <value>”; edit mode is a labelled input with Save and Cancel buttons, so it works without the keys too.
- Errors (from `validate` or returned by `onSave`) sit under the field, linked with aria-describedby; the draft is kept.
- While `onSave`’s promise is pending, Save shows its pending state and Cancel is disabled.
- `disabledReason` keeps the value visible and focusable, with the reason as its description.

Stories: `components-inlineedit--viewing`, `components-inlineedit--empty-value`, `components-inlineedit--editing`, `components-inlineedit--invalid`, `components-inlineedit--disabled`.
Composes: Button, Field, Icon, Spinner.
Tokens read: `button.danger.bg`, `button.danger.bg-hover`, `button.danger.fg`, `button.ghost.bg-hover`, `button.ghost.fg`, `button.primary.bg`, `button.primary.bg-hover`, `button.primary.fg`, `button.secondary.bg`, `button.secondary.bg-hover`, `button.secondary.border`, `button.secondary.fg`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.status.danger.fg`, `ease.linear`, `ease.standard`, `focus.ring.width`, `icon.stroke`, `motion.fast`, `motion.spin`, `radius.control`, `radius.pill`, `size.control.lg`, `size.control.md`, `size.control.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.sidebar.sm`, `size.target-min`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.lg`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.inset.xs`, `text.body`, `text.body-lg`, `text.caption`, `text.label`.

### Kbd

component · `src/components/Kbd/Kbd.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Kbd.usage.tsx`

A key or a keyboard shortcut, shown as key caps: in hints ("Tab to accept"), tooltips, menus, the command palette and the shortcuts overlay. `keys` takes shortcut notation and renders it for the platform (⌘K on a Mac, Ctrl K elsewhere); `children` names one key as printed. Symbols a screen reader would read badly (⌘, ↵) carry a spoken name. It only shows keys; register a shortcut with useShortcut.

Props:
- `platform?: KeyPlatform`: Override the detected platform (gallery and tests).
- `thenLabel?: string` = `'then'`: Word between the strokes of a sequence ("g i" → G then I).
- `keys?: string`: Shortcut notation: "mod+k", "shift+?", "g i" (a sequence), "j". `mod` is ⌘ on a Mac and Ctrl elsewhere.
- `children?: never`: One key, named as printed on it: "Tab", "Esc", "Enter". For a hint in running text ("Tab to accept"); prefer `keys`, which also knows the platform, for a shortcut.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: platform (mac | other).

#### ariaKeyShortcuts

utility, part of Kbd. The shortcut in aria-keyshortcuts syntax ("Meta+K", "Control+K", "G I"), for the control it triggers. Screen readers announce it with the control's name.
Signature: `(keys: string, platform?: KeyPlatform) => string`

#### formatShortcut

utility, part of Kbd. A shortcut as plain text for the platform: "⌘K", "Ctrl+K", "G then I". For places that take a string (a Tooltip's content, a palette row's label); render <Kbd> where markup is allowed.
Signature: `(keys: string, platform?: KeyPlatform) => string`

**When to use**

- Showing a shortcut where people will learn it: a tooltip (`Tooltip shortcut`), a menu item (`MenuItem.shortcut`), a command palette row, the shortcuts overlay. Pass `keys` in shortcut notation (`mod+k`, `g i`).
- Naming a key in a hint: “<Kbd>Tab</Kbd> to accept”, one Kbd per key (`children`, the key as printed).
- `formatShortcut` where only a string fits; `ariaKeyShortcuts` for the `aria-keyshortcuts` attribute of a control the system doesn’t already set it on.

**When not to use**

- Registering the shortcut itself → `useShortcut` (Kbd only shows keys)
- Code, a command or a value to copy → `CodeBlock`, or inline `<code>`
- A clickable shortcut → a `Button` whose label names the action; show the key beside it or in its tooltip

**Do:** Notation, not glyphs: `mod+k` shows ⌘K on a Mac and Ctrl K elsewhere, from the string the shortcut is registered with; a hint names its keys.

```tsx
<Cluster gap="md" align="center">
  <Tooltip content="Search and run commands" shortcut="mod+k">
    <Button variant="secondary" icon="search">
      Search
    </Button>
  </Tooltip>
  <Text>
    <Kbd>Tab</Kbd> to accept · <Kbd>Esc</Kbd> to dismiss
  </Text>
</Cluster>
```

**Don't:** A combination typed into one cap, or a hard-coded ⌘: one strange key, wrong on Windows, and read as “place of interest sign”. Use `keys="shift+enter"`.

```tsx
<Text>
  Press <Kbd>Shift+Enter</Kbd> or ⌘K
</Text>
```

**Accessibility**

- Renders `<kbd>`. Symbols from `keys` (⌘ ⇧ ⌥ ⌃ ↵ arrows) carry a visually hidden spoken name; with `children`, name keys with words people say (“Esc”, “Enter”).
- Showing a shortcut isn’t announcing it: `Tooltip shortcut` and `MenuItem.shortcut` also set `aria-keyshortcuts` on the control.
- A hint with keys needs a pointer path too: a visible button for the same action. Single-key shortcuts can be turned off (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.1.4) in the shortcuts overlay.

Stories: `components-kbd--mac`, `components-kbd--windows-and-linux`, `components-kbd--shift-chord`, `components-kbd--single-key`, `components-kbd--sequence`, `components-kbd--named-keys`, `components-kbd--key-by-name`, `components-kbd--combination`.
Tokens read: `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `radius.indicator`, `size.icon.sm`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.inset.2xs`, `text.caption`, `text.code`.

### Link

component · `src/components/Link/Link.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Link.usage.tsx`

An inline or standalone text link, styled from tokens and routed through LinkProvider.

Props:
- `href: string`: Destination. Routed through the app's LinkProvider, when there is one.
- `children: ReactNode`: Link text that makes sense out of context ("View invoice INV-2041", not "click here").
- …plus the native attributes of `AnchorHTMLAttributes`, `AriaAttributes`, `Attributes`, `DOMAttributes`, `HTMLAttributes`, `RefAttributes`.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

#### LinkProvider

component, part of Link. Injects the app's router link once, at the root. Every system link (Link, Nav, NavTabs, Breadcrumbs) then routes client-side. Without a provider they render a plain <a>.

Props:
- `component: LinkComponent`: The app's router link, adapted to LinkComponentProps.
- `children: ReactNode`

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`.

**When to use**

- Navigation written as text: an inline link in a sentence, “View all records”, a way home from an error page.
- Wrap the app once in `LinkProvider` (see Getting started) with its router’s link, adapted to take `href`. `Link`, `Nav`, `NavTabs` and `Breadcrumbs` then route client-side; without it they render a plain `<a>`.
- The adapter spreads every prop onto its anchor and forwards `ref`: tooltips and focus management attach to it.

**When not to use**

- An action that changes data or opens something in place → `Button`
- The app’s areas or a record’s sections → `Nav` or `NavTabs`, which mark the current page
- A trail back up the hierarchy → `Breadcrumbs`

**Do:** Link text that says where it goes, inside the sentence it belongs to.

```tsx
<Text>
  The lease renews in January. <Link href="/records/r-1002/files">Read the signed agreement</Link> for the full terms.
</Text>
```

**Don't:** “Click here”: out of context (a screen reader’s list of links) it says nothing about where it goes.

```tsx
<Text>
  The lease renews in January. For the full terms, <Link href="/records/r-1002/files">click here</Link>.
</Text>
```

**Accessibility**

- A real anchor with an `href`, so it works with the keyboard, opens in a new tab and is listed as a link.
- Underlined as well as coloured, so it never depends on colour alone.
- Write link text that makes sense on its own; the page’s other links should not share it with a different destination.

Stories: `components-link--standalone`, `components-link--in-running-text`, `components-link--through-link-provider`.
Tokens read: `color.fg.link`, `focus.ring.offset`, `focus.ring.width`, `radius.indicator`.

### Menu

component · `src/components/Menu/Menu.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Menu.usage.tsx`

Action menu. Keyboard, typeahead, focus return and ARIA come from Radix DropdownMenu.

Props:
- `trigger: ReactElement`: Element that opens the menu, typically a system Button. It keeps its own accessible name.
- `items: readonly MenuEntry[]`
- `label?: string`: Optional non-interactive heading at the top (the signed-in user in an account menu).
- `align?: 'start' | 'end'` = `'start'`: Edge of the trigger the menu lines up with.
- `open?: boolean`
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`
- `onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void`

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: align (start | end).
States: open, defaultOpen.

**When to use**

- Secondary actions behind a “More” button in a crowded header or table row.
- The account menu in AppShell’s `userMenu` slot.

**When not to use**

- Choosing a value for a form field → `Select`
- The one primary action → a visible `Button`
- Navigation between pages → `Nav`

**Do:** The primary action stays visible; the rest live behind “More”, with the destructive one last.

```tsx
<Cluster gap="xs">
  <Button>Edit</Button>
  <Menu
    trigger={<Button variant="secondary">More</Button>}
    items={[{ label: 'Duplicate record' }, { label: 'Export PDF', icon: 'download' }, 'separator', { label: 'Delete record' }]}
  />
</Cluster>
```

**Don't:** The main action hidden in a menu with a single item: one extra click for nothing.

```tsx
<Menu trigger={<Button variant="secondary">Actions</Button>} items={[{ label: 'Save' }]} />
```

**Accessibility**

- The trigger keeps its own accessible name and gets `aria-expanded`; arrow keys and typeahead move through items.
- Focus returns to the trigger when the menu closes. Labels are verb-first, like buttons.

Stories: `components-menu--closed`, `components-menu--open`, `components-menu--with-shortcuts`, `components-menu--account-menu`.
Composes: Icon, Kbd.
Tokens read: `color.bg.elevated`, `color.bg.hover`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.status.danger.bg`, `color.status.danger.fg`, `icon.stroke`, `radius.control`, `radius.indicator`, `radius.surface`, `shadow.popover`, `size.control.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.overlay-max`, `size.sidebar.sm`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.md`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.2xs`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.inset.xs`, `text.body`, `text.caption`, `text.code`, `z.dropdown`.

### Message

component · `src/components/Message/Message.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Message.usage.tsx`

One turn in a ChatThread: a header (who, when, the AI mark), the content, and actions (copy, retry, edit, feedback) once it has finished. User turns are tinted and aligned to the inline end; assistant turns run full width. Tool and system turns are compact notes. Render inside ChatThread.

Props:
- `role: MessageRole`
- `author: string`: Who it's from, shown in the header and naming the message ("You", "Assistant", "Search records").
- `time?: DateInput`: When it was sent. Formatted with useFormat(); omit for pending turns.
- `status?: StreamStatus` = `'complete'`: An assistant turn's state: its actions show once it's no longer pending or streaming.
- `children: ReactNode`: The content: StreamingText for assistant turns, text for user turns, a Disclosure for tool activity.
- `error?: string`: Why the turn failed, with the next step ("Too many requests. Try again in 30 seconds.").
- `copyText?: string`: The turn's text for Copy. Shows a Copy action.
- `onRetry?: () => void`: Shows Retry (assistant: ask again; user: resend a failed message).
- `onEdit?: () => void`: Shows Edit on a user turn: puts its text back in the composer.
- `feedback?: ReactNode`: A Feedback control for an assistant turn.
- `marker?: ReactNode` = `role === 'assistant' ? <AiMarker variant="inline" /> : null`: The AI mark on an assistant turn. Defaults to an AiMarker; pass null only where the whole surface is already marked.
- `stoppedLabel?: string` = `'Stopped before the answer finished.'`: Shown under a stopped turn, so it doesn't read as a finished answer.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: role (user | assistant | tool | system); status (pending | streaming | complete | stopped | error).

**When to use**

- One turn inside a `ChatThread`: `user` (tinted, at the inline end), `assistant` (full width, AI-marked), `tool` (what the assistant ran, usually a `Disclosure`) or `system` (a note such as “You stopped the answer”).
- Actions appear once a turn has finished: Copy (`copyText`), Retry, Edit (user turns) and a `Feedback` control.

**When not to use**

- Comments on a record → the record page’s activity list (`Timeline` or the activity feed)
- A one-off AI result inside a form → `Suggestion`, or the content with an `AiMarker`

**Do:** An assistant turn: who, when, the AI mark, the answer, then its actions.

```tsx
<Message role="assistant" author="Assistant" time="2026-09-14T10:04:05Z" copyText="It renews on 15 January 2027." onRetry={() => undefined} feedback={<Feedback onFeedback={() => undefined} />}>
  <StreamingText text="It renews on **15 January 2027**." />
</Message>
```

**Don't:** An answer as plain text with no author, time, mark or actions: it can’t be checked, copied or retried.

```tsx
<Text>It renews on 15 January 2027.</Text>
```

**Accessibility**

- Each turn is an `article` named by its author, so screen-reader users can move turn by turn.
- An error shows as text with an icon (`role="alert"`) and a Retry; never colour alone.
- The assistant avatar is decorative; the author name and the AI marker carry the meaning.

Stories: `components-message--user`, `components-message--assistant`, `components-message--assistant-streaming`, `components-message--assistant-pending`, `components-message--assistant-stopped`, `components-message--assistant-error`, `components-message--tool`, `components-message--system`.
Composes: AiMarker, Avatar, Button, CopyButton, Icon, Spinner.
Tokens read: `button.danger.bg`, `button.danger.bg-hover`, `button.danger.fg`, `button.ghost.bg-hover`, `button.ghost.fg`, `button.primary.bg`, `button.primary.bg-hover`, `button.primary.fg`, `button.secondary.bg`, `button.secondary.bg-hover`, `button.secondary.border`, `button.secondary.fg`, `color.ai.bg`, `color.ai.border`, `color.ai.fg`, `color.bg.selected`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.border.default`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.status.danger.fg`, `ease.linear`, `ease.standard`, `focus.ring.width`, `font.weight.strong`, `icon.stroke`, `motion.fast`, `motion.spin`, `radius.control`, `radius.pill`, `radius.surface`, `size.avatar.lg`, `size.avatar.md`, `size.avatar.sm`, `size.content.sm`, `size.control.lg`, `size.control.md`, `size.control.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.target-min`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.2xs`, `space.inset.lg`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `text.body`, `text.body-lg`, `text.caption`, `text.label`.

### Meter

component · `src/components/Meter/Meter.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Meter.usage.tsx`

How much of a limit is used: seats, storage, API calls. Past a threshold it warns in words and an icon, not colour alone.

Props:
- `label: string`: What is measured ("Seats", "Storage"). Visible; names the meter. Required.
- `value: number`
- `max: number`: The limit.
- `valueText?: string`: Usage in words, shown and read out ("42 of 50 seats"). Defaults to "value of max".
- `warningAt?: number` = `max * 0.8`: From this value on the meter warns. Defaults to 80% of max.
- `dangerAt?: number` = `max`: From this value on the meter is in danger. Defaults to max (the limit is reached).
- `statusLabels?: Record<Exclude<MeterStatus, 'ok'>, string>` = `STATUS_LABELS`: Words for each status beyond ok, shown with an icon and appended to the value text.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

**When to use**

- How much of a limit is used: seats, storage, API calls, a budget.
- Say the usage in words with `valueText` (“42 of 50 seats”). Past `warningAt` (default 80%) it shows “Nearing limit”; from `dangerAt` (default the limit) “Limit reached”, each with an icon.

**When not to use**

- Progress through a task → `Progress`
- A headline number with a trend → `Stat`

**Do:** Near the limit: the fill changes colour, and an icon and words say so.

```tsx
<Meter label="Seats" value={42} max={50} valueText="42 of 50 seats" />
```

**Don't:** A progress bar for usage: it reads as a task heading for done, and never warns as the limit nears.

```tsx
<Progress label="Seats" value={42} max={50} valueText="42 of 50 seats" />
```

**Accessibility**

- A `meter` named by the visible label, with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuetext` (the usage, plus the status past a threshold).
- Warning and danger are icon and words as well as colour.

Stories: `components-meter--within-limit`, `components-meter--warning`, `components-meter--danger`, `components-meter--custom-thresholds`, `components-meter--default-value-text`.
Composes: Icon.
Tokens read: `color.action.primary`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.status.danger.fg`, `color.status.warning.fg`, `font.weight.strong`, `icon.stroke`, `radius.pill`, `size.bar`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.sm`, `text.caption`, `text.label`.

### MultiSelect

component · `src/components/MultiSelect/MultiSelect.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/MultiSelect.usage.tsx`

Choosing several values from a list that narrows as you type: tags, teams, event types in a filter. Chosen values show as removable chips in the field; the list stays open while you pick. Behaviour, ARIA and focus come from React Aria's ComboBox in multiple-selection mode.

Props:
- `label: string`: Visible label and accessible name. Required.
- `hideLabel?: boolean`
- `options: readonly MultiSelectOption[]`
- `value?: readonly string[]`: The chosen values, in the order they were chosen.
- `defaultValue?: readonly string[]`
- `onValueChange?: (value: string[]) => void`
- `placeholder?: string`
- `description?: string`
- `error?: string`
- `size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'` = `'md'`
- `disabled?: boolean`
- `required?: boolean`
- `name?: string`: Form field name: one value per chosen option is submitted.
- `emptyMessage?: string` = `'No matches'`
- `showOptionsLabel?: string` = `'Show options'`
- `removeLabel?: (label: string) => string` = `(text) => 'Remove ${text}'`: Accessible name of each chip's remove button: `(label) => 'Remove Legal'`.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean` = `false`: Render the list open (gallery and tests).

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: size (sm | md | lg).
States: hideLabel, disabled, required, defaultOpen.

**When to use**

- Choosing several values from a longer list: event types in a filter, tags, teams.
- When the chosen values should stay visible (as chips) while more are added.

**When not to use**

- A handful of options that fit on screen → a group of `Checkbox`es
- One value → `Combobox` or `Select`

**Do:** Chosen values as chips, each with its own remove button; the list narrows as you type.

```tsx
<MultiSelect label="Events" options={EVENTS} defaultValue={['member.role_changed']} />
```

**Don't:** Two independent yes/no settings squeezed into a multi-select: checkboxes are clearer.

```tsx
<Stack gap="xs">
  <Checkbox label="Email me" />
  <Checkbox label="Notify me in the app" />
</Stack>
```

**Accessibility**

- React Aria’s combobox in multiple-selection mode: options announce whether they’re selected, and the list stays open while you choose.
- Each chip’s remove button is named after its value (`removeLabel`); removing one returns focus to the input.
- The field wraps onto more lines rather than hiding chosen values behind a count.

Stories: `components-multiselect--empty`, `components-multiselect--with-values`, `components-multiselect--wrapping`, `components-multiselect--with-error`, `components-multiselect--disabled`, `components-multiselect--open`.
Composes: Field, Icon, Picker, Tag.
Tokens read: `color.bg.elevated`, `color.bg.hover`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.link`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.focus`, `color.status.danger.fg`, `focus.ring.offset`, `focus.ring.width`, `font.weight.strong`, `icon.stroke`, `radius.control`, `radius.pill`, `radius.surface`, `shadow.popover`, `size.control.lg`, `size.control.md`, `size.control.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.overlay-max`, `size.target-min`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.2xs`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.inset.xs`, `text.body`, `text.body-lg`, `text.caption`, `text.label`, `z.dropdown`.

### Nav

component · `src/components/Nav/Nav.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Nav.usage.tsx`

Vertical navigation: the app's primary sidebar or a section sub-nav (settings). Grouped, data-driven.

Props:
- `label: string`: Accessible name of the navigation landmark ("Main", "Settings"). Required: pages carry several navs.
- `sections: readonly NavSection[]`
- `current?: string`: href of the current page. That link gets aria-current="page", not only a heavier look.
- `onNavigate?: (href: string) => void`: Client-side routing hook. When set, a plain click calls it instead of following the link; modified clicks (new tab, new window) still use the browser. Apps with a router usually inject its link once with LinkProvider instead.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

**When to use**

- The app’s primary navigation in AppShell’s `nav` slot, defined once for the app.
- A settings sub-nav grouped into Personal and Workspace sections.

**When not to use**

- Switching views of one record in place → `Tabs`
- Showing where a page sits in the hierarchy → `Breadcrumbs`
- Actions → `Button` or `Menu`

**Do:** A few top-level destinations, grouped, with the current page marked.

```tsx
<Nav
  label="Settings"
  current="/settings/profile"
  sections={[
    { label: 'Personal', items: [{ label: 'Profile', href: '/settings/profile' }, { label: 'Notifications', href: '/settings/notifications' }] },
    { label: 'Workspace', items: [{ label: 'General', href: '/settings/general' }] },
  ]}
/>
```

**Don't:** Actions dressed as destinations: “Export” and “Sign out” don’t lead to a page.

```tsx
<Nav
  label="Records menu"
  current="/records"
  sections={[{ items: [{ label: 'Records', href: '/records' }, { label: 'Export', href: '/export' }, { label: 'Sign out', href: '/sign-out' }] }]}
/>
```

**Accessibility**

- `label` is required: pages carry several nav landmarks, and each needs a distinct name.
- The current item gets `aria-current="page"`, not only a heavier look. Section labels name their lists.

Stories: `components-nav--with-icons`, `components-nav--no-current-page`, `components-nav--grouped-sub-nav`.
Composes: Icon, Kbd, Link, Tooltip.
Tokens read: `color.action.primary`, `color.bg.hover`, `color.bg.inverse`, `color.bg.selected`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.inverse`, `color.fg.link`, `color.fg.muted`, `focus.ring.offset`, `focus.ring.width`, `font.weight.strong`, `icon.stroke`, `radius.control`, `radius.indicator`, `shadow.popover`, `size.control.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.overlay-max`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.lg`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.2xs`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.inset.xs`, `text.caption`, `text.code`, `text.label`, `z.tooltip`.

### NavTabs

component · `src/components/NavTabs/NavTabs.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/NavTabs.usage.tsx`

Section navigation that looks like tabs but is links: each section is its own route. A labelled nav landmark with aria-current="page" on the current link, not an ARIA tablist.

Props:
- `label: string`: Accessible name of the navigation landmark ("Record sections"). Required: pages carry several navs.
- `items: readonly NavTab[]`
- `current: string`: href of the current section. That link gets aria-current="page".
- `onNavigate?: (href: string) => void`: Client-side routing hook. When set, a plain click calls it instead of following the link; modified clicks (new tab, new window) still use the browser. Apps with a router usually inject its link once with LinkProvider instead.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

**When to use**

- Sections of a record or area that are each their own route: Overview, Activity, Files. The URL changes, the section can be bookmarked or opened in a new tab.
- Tabs or NavTabs? If choosing one changes the URL, it is `NavTabs` (links, `aria-current="page"`). If it only swaps panels in place on one page, it is `Tabs` (an ARIA tablist).
- Place it under the `PageHeader`, above the section’s content.

**When not to use**

- Switching panels in place without changing the URL → `Tabs`
- The app’s areas → AppShell’s `Nav`
- A long list of categories (settings) → `Nav` in `PageLayout`’s nav slot
- Steps that must be done in order → `Stepper` in a `FocusedLayout`

**Do:** Each section is a route: links in a named nav, the current one marked with aria-current.

```tsx
<NavTabs label="Record sections (do example)" items={sections} current="/records/r-1001/activity" />
```

**Don't:** An ARIA tablist for routes: screen readers announce tabs and panels, but each “tab” is really a page change.

```tsx
<Tabs defaultValue="activity">
  <TabList label="Record sections (don’t example)">
    <Tab value="overview">Overview</Tab>
    <Tab value="activity">Activity</Tab>
  </TabList>
  <TabPanel value="overview">
    <Text>Loads /records/r-1001</Text>
  </TabPanel>
  <TabPanel value="activity">
    <Text>Loads /records/r-1001/activity</Text>
  </TabPanel>
</Tabs>
```

**Accessibility**

- A `nav` landmark named by the required `label`, with `aria-current="page"` on the current link. It is not a tablist: Tab moves link to link, Enter follows.
- The current section has a rule and a stronger colour, never colour alone.
- On narrow screens the row scrolls sideways instead of wrapping; every link stays reachable by keyboard.
- After a client-side section change, product code moves focus or announces the new section, as for any route change.

Stories: `components-navtabs--first-current`, `components-navtabs--later-current`, `components-navtabs--many-sections-narrow`.
Composes: Link.
Tokens read: `color.action.primary`, `color.border.default`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.link`, `color.fg.muted`, `focus.ring.offset`, `focus.ring.width`, `radius.indicator`, `size.control.md`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.sm`, `text.label`.

### NumberField

component · `src/components/NumberField/NumberField.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/NumberField.usage.tsx`

A number typed in the reader's own format ("1.234,5" in German), parsed back to a number: amounts, quantities, percentages. ↑ ↓ step, Page Up/Down step by ten, Home/End go to min/max. Built on React Aria's NumberField (not a native number input, which takes "e", ignores the locale's grouping and changes on scroll). Formatting follows LocaleProvider, like useFormat().

Props:
- `label: string`: Visible label and accessible name. Required.
- `hideLabel?: boolean`
- `value?: number | null`: The number. With `currency`, integer minor units (cents), like every amount in the system: 125050 with "USD" shows $1,250.50. null is empty.
- `defaultValue?: number | null`
- `onValueChange?: (value: number | null) => void`
- `format?: 'number' | 'percent'` = `'number'`: How it reads: a plain number, a percentage (0.25 shows 25%), or money when `currency` is set.
- `currency?: string`: ISO 4217 code: the field shows and parses money, and `value` is in minor units.
- `min?: number`
- `max?: number`
- `step?: number`: Arrow keys and the stepper buttons move by this (in the value's units), and the value snaps to its multiples: leave it unset for money unless only whole units are allowed.
- `maximumFractionDigits?: number`
- `description?: string`
- `error?: string`
- `size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'` = `'md'`
- `disabled?: boolean`
- `required?: boolean`
- `name?: string`
- `hideStepper?: boolean` = `false`: Hide the − and + buttons (arrow keys still step).
- `incrementLabel?: string` = `'Increase'`
- `decrementLabel?: string` = `'Decrease'`

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: format (number | percent); size (sm | md | lg).
States: hideLabel, disabled, required, hideStepper.

**When to use**

- Quantities, amounts and percentages people type: seats, a price, a discount.
- Money: pass `currency`, and the value is integer minor units, like every amount in the system.

**When not to use**

- Numbers that aren’t quantities (a phone number, a postcode, an id) → `TextField` with the right `inputMode`
- A value from a small range, dragged → `Slider`

**Do:** An amount in the reader’s format, stored as minor units.

```tsx
<NumberField label="Amount" currency="USD" defaultValue={125050} min={0} />
```

**Don't:** A text field for an amount: “1.250,50” and “1,250.50” can’t both be parsed, and nothing stops “12e3”.

```tsx
<TextField label="Amount" type="number" />
```

**Accessibility**

- Why React Aria and not `<input type="number">`: the native input accepts “e”, ignores the locale’s grouping and decimal marks, changes on scroll, and its spinners are tiny targets.
- Typing and display follow LocaleProvider (the same locale as `useFormat()`); ↑ ↓ step, Page Up/Down step by ten, Home/End jump to min/max.
- The − and + buttons are 24px targets with names (`decrementLabel`, `incrementLabel`); they’re removed from the tab order, since the arrow keys do the same.

Stories: `components-numberfield--empty`, `components-numberfield--with-value`, `components-numberfield--currency`, `components-numberfield--percent`, `components-numberfield--german-currency`, `components-numberfield--with-error`, `components-numberfield--disabled`, `components-numberfield--without-stepper`.
Composes: Field, Icon, Picker.
Tokens read: `color.bg.elevated`, `color.bg.hover`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.link`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.focus`, `color.status.danger.fg`, `focus.ring.offset`, `focus.ring.width`, `icon.stroke`, `radius.control`, `radius.surface`, `shadow.popover`, `size.control.lg`, `size.control.md`, `size.control.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.overlay-max`, `size.target-min`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.2xs`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.inset.xs`, `text.body`, `text.body-lg`, `text.caption`, `text.label`, `z.dropdown`.

### PageHeader

component · `src/components/PageHeader/PageHeader.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/PageHeader.usage.tsx`

The top of every page: title (h1), optional status and description, and the page's actions. Breadcrumbs are not here: AppShell's header owns them.

Props:
- `title: string`: The page title, rendered as the page's one h1. Matches the nav item or breadcrumb that leads here.
- `status?: ReactNode`: A status beside the title: a system Badge mapped from the domain status.
- `description?: ReactNode`: One line under the title: what the page is for, or the record's key metadata.
- `actions?: ReactNode`: Page actions: secondary first, the one primary action last, then a "More" Menu. Right-aligned; they wrap.
- `headingRef?: Ref<HTMLHeadingElement>`: Ref to the h1, for moving focus to it after a client-side step or route change. When set, the heading takes tabIndex={-1} so it can receive focus without entering the tab order.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

**When to use**

- The top of every page, inside AppShell’s main or a FocusedLayout: the page title (the one h1), an optional status, one line of description and the page’s actions.
- Actions go in `actions`: secondary first, the one primary action last, then a “More” `Menu` for the rest, destructive items last in it.
- A record’s status goes in `status` as a `Badge`, mapped from the domain status in one place.

**When not to use**

- Breadcrumbs → AppShell’s `breadcrumbs` slot; the header of the frame owns the trail
- A section title inside the page → `CardHeader` or a `Heading` at level 2
- Global actions (search, a global create) → AppShell’s `actions` slot

**Do:** Title, status and metadata on the start side; page actions on the end, primary last.

```tsx
<PageHeader
  title="Hardware lease"
  status={<Badge tone="info">Pending</Badge>}
  description="Owned by Facilities · updated 2026-09-10"
  actions={
    <>
      <Button variant="secondary">Share</Button>
      <Button>Request approval</Button>
    </>
  }
/>
```

**Don't:** A hand-built title row: the gaps, alignment and wrapping drift from page to page, and the status sits under the title.

```tsx
<Stack gap="xs">
  <Heading level={1} size={3}>
    Hardware lease
  </Heading>
  <Badge tone="info">Pending</Badge>
  <Text tone="muted">Owned by Facilities</Text>
  <Button>Request approval</Button>
</Stack>
```

**Accessibility**

- Renders the page’s h1, so every page has exactly one, in the same place. Keep it the same words as the nav item or breadcrumb that leads here.
- The status is a `Badge`: icon and text as well as colour.
- Pass `headingRef` to move focus to the title after a client-side step or route change; the heading then takes `tabIndex={-1}`.

Stories: `components-pageheader--title-only`, `components-pageheader--with-description`, `components-pageheader--with-action`, `components-pageheader--with-status`, `components-pageheader--record`, `components-pageheader--actions-wrap`.
Composes: Heading, Text.
Tokens read: `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.muted`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.md`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xs`, `text.body`, `text.body-lg`, `text.caption`, `text.heading-1`, `text.heading-2`, `text.heading-3`, `text.heading-4`.

### Pagination

component · `src/components/Pagination/Pagination.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Pagination.usage.tsx`

Moves through a long, server-paged list: a summary of what is shown, Previous and Next, and page numbers around the current one. A labelled nav landmark; the current page has aria-current="page".

Props:
- `page: number`: Current page, from 1.
- `pageSize: number`
- `total: number`: Total items across every page.
- `onPageChange: (page: number) => void`
- `label?: string` = `'Pagination'`: Accessible name of the navigation landmark.
- `previousLabel?: string` = `'Previous'`
- `nextLabel?: string` = `'Next'`
- `pageLabel?: (page: number) => string` = `(p) => 'Page ${String(p)}'`: Accessible name of a page button, from its number ("Page 3").
- `formatNumber?: (n: number) => string`: Formats counts in the summary. Defaults to the LocaleProvider's number format ("1,284", "1.284").
- `announce?: boolean` = `false`: Make the summary ("1–25 of 1,284") a polite live region, so a new page or a new total after filtering is announced. Use it when nothing else on the page announces the count.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).
States: announce.

**When to use**

- Under a list or table that is paged on the server: it says what is shown (“1–25 of 1,284”) and moves between pages.
- Reset to page 1 when the query or filters change. Set `announce` when nothing else on the page announces the new count.

**When not to use**

- A short list that fits on one page → no pagination; a count line if it helps
- A feed people scroll through → a “Show more” button
- Steps of a task → `Stepper`

**Do:** What is shown, then Previous, the pages around the current one, and Next.

```tsx
<Pagination page={12} pageSize={25} total={1284} onPageChange={() => undefined} />
```

**Don't:** Bare arrows: no page, no total, and no name for either button.

```tsx
<Cluster gap="xs">
  <Button variant="secondary" size="sm">
    ‹
  </Button>
  <Button variant="secondary" size="sm">
    ›
  </Button>
</Cluster>
```

**Accessibility**

- A `nav` landmark (`label`, default “Pagination”); the current page has `aria-current="page"`, and each page button is named “Page n”.
- At either end, Previous or Next is `aria-disabled` rather than disabled, so focus is never dropped from the button someone just used.
- The current page is outlined and heavier, not only a different colour.

Stories: `components-pagination--first-page`, `components-pagination--middle-page`, `components-pagination--last-page`, `components-pagination--few-pages`, `components-pagination--single-page`, `components-pagination--narrow`.
Composes: Icon.
Tokens read: `color.action.primary`, `color.bg.hover`, `color.bg.selected`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.muted`, `font.weight.strong`, `icon.stroke`, `radius.control`, `size.control.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.inset.xs`, `text.caption`, `text.label`.

### Popover

component · `src/components/Popover/Popover.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Popover.usage.tsx`

A small non-modal panel anchored to its trigger, for a few controls (a filter menu). Focus moves in on open and back to the trigger on close; Escape and an outside click close it. From Radix Popover.

Props:
- `label: string`: Accessible name of the popover (it is a non-modal dialog): "Filter records". Required.
- `trigger: ReactElement`: Element that opens it, typically a system Button. It gets aria-expanded and aria-controls.
- `children: ReactNode`: A few controls that act on the page: filter checkboxes, a small form.
- `align?: 'start' | 'end'` = `'start'`: Edge of the trigger the popover lines up with.
- `open?: boolean`
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`
- `onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void`

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: align (start | end).
States: open, defaultOpen.

**When to use**

- A few controls anchored to the button that opens them, acting on the page as they change: a filter menu of checkboxes, a column picker.
- It is non-modal: the page stays usable, Escape or a click outside closes it, and focus returns to the trigger.

**When not to use**

- A list of actions → `Menu`
- A hint on hover or focus → `Tooltip`
- Many filters, or a form with a submit → `Drawer` or `Dialog`

**Do:** A Filters button that opens a named popover of status checkboxes.

```tsx
<Popover label="Filter by status (do example)" trigger={<Button variant="secondary">Filters</Button>}>
  <Checkbox label="Active" />
</Popover>
```

**Don't:** Controls in a tooltip: it vanishes when the pointer leaves, and keyboard users can’t reach what is inside.

```tsx
<Tooltip content="Active · Pending · Overdue">
  <Button variant="secondary">Filters</Button>
</Tooltip>
```

**Accessibility**

- A dialog named by the required `label`; the trigger gets `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`.
- Focus moves into it on open and back to the trigger on close; Escape closes it.

Stories: `components-popover--closed`, `components-popover--open`, `components-popover--open-aligned-end`.
Tokens read: `color.bg.elevated`, `color.border.default`, `color.fg.default`, `radius.surface`, `shadow.popover`, `size.overlay-max`, `size.sidebar.sm`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.inset.md`, `z.dropdown`.

### Progress

component · `src/components/Progress/Progress.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Progress.usage.tsx`

Determinate progress through a task: a bar with a label and the value in words. For work of unknown length use Spinner; for usage against a limit use Meter.

Props:
- `label: string`: Visible label and accessible name ("Setup progress", "Uploading contract.pdf"). Required.
- `value: number`: Current value, from 0 to max.
- `max?: number` = `100`
- `valueText?: string`: The value in words, shown beside the label and used as aria-valuetext ("Step 2 of 4", "3 of 12 files"). Defaults to a whole percentage.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

**When to use**

- Determinate progress through a task: steps of a wizard, files of an upload, rows of an import.
- Say the value in words with `valueText` (“Step 2 of 4”, “3 of 12 files”); it is shown and read out. Without it, a whole percentage.

**When not to use**

- Work of unknown length → `Spinner`
- Usage against a limit (seats, storage, API calls) → `Meter`
- The steps themselves → `Stepper`, beside it

**Do:** A label and the value in words, over the bar.

```tsx
<Progress label="Importing records" value={340} max={1284} valueText="340 of 1,284 records" />
```

**Don't:** A spinner for a job whose size is known: people can’t tell whether to wait or come back later.

```tsx
<Spinner label="Importing 1,284 records" />
```

**Accessibility**

- A `progressbar` named by the visible `label`, with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuetext` from `valueText`.
- The bar isn’t announced as it moves. For a long job, announce milestones (a Toast when it finishes).

Stories: `components-progress--steps`, `components-progress--percentage`, `components-progress--not-started`, `components-progress--complete`.
Tokens read: `color.action.primary`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.muted`, `radius.pill`, `size.bar`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.sm`, `text.caption`.

### RadioGroup

component · `src/components/RadioGroup/RadioGroup.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/RadioGroup.usage.tsx`

One choice from a few visible options (up to about five; more is a Select). Arrow keys move and select, Tab leaves the group: behaviour from Radix RadioGroup.

Props:
- `label: string`: The question the options answer. Names the group. Required.
- `hideLabel?: boolean`
- `options: readonly RadioOption[]`
- `value?: string`
- `defaultValue?: string`
- `onValueChange?: (value: string) => void`
- `description?: string`
- `error?: string`: Error message for the group. Sets aria-invalid on the group.
- `disabled?: boolean`
- `name?: string`
- `orientation?: 'vertical' | 'horizontal'` = `'vertical'`
- `id?: string`: Id of the first option, for an error summary link. Generated when omitted.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: orientation (vertical | horizontal).
States: hideLabel, disabled.

**When to use**

- Choosing exactly one of two to about five options that are worth seeing side by side.
- Add a `description` to options whose consequences differ.

**When not to use**

- Many options → `Select`
- A single yes/no → `Checkbox` (in a form) or `Switch` (applies at once)

**Do:** The group label asks the question; each option says what it means.

```tsx
<RadioGroup
  label="Billing period"
  defaultValue="yearly"
  options={[
    { value: 'monthly', label: 'Monthly', description: 'Cancel any time.' },
    { value: 'yearly', label: 'Yearly', description: 'Two months free.' },
  ]}
/>
```

**Don't:** Radio buttons for a long list: the form becomes a wall of options. Use a Select.

```tsx
<RadioGroup
  label="Country"
  orientation="horizontal"
  options={['Austria', 'Belgium', 'Denmark', 'Finland', 'France', 'Germany', 'Ireland', 'Italy'].map((c) => ({ value: c, label: c }))}
/>
```

**Accessibility**

- Renders a labelled `radiogroup`; arrow keys move between options.
- A group `error` sets `aria-invalid` on the group; pass `id` so an error summary can link to the first option.

Stories: `components-radiogroup--unselected`, `components-radiogroup--selected`, `components-radiogroup--with-description`, `components-radiogroup--with-error`, `components-radiogroup--horizontal`, `components-radiogroup--disabled-option`, `components-radiogroup--disabled`.
Composes: Field, Icon.
Tokens read: `color.action.primary`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.status.danger.fg`, `icon.stroke`, `radius.control`, `radius.pill`, `size.control.lg`, `size.control.md`, `size.control.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.md`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.inset.xs`, `text.body`, `text.body-lg`, `text.caption`, `text.label`.

### ReviewChanges

component · `src/components/ReviewChanges/ReviewChanges.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/ReviewChanges.usage.tsx`

Changes an AI proposes, reviewed before anything happens: each as a diff (a field's before and after, or a text rewrite word by word) with Accept and Reject, plus Accept all and Reject all. Only accepted changes are applied, then each shows its outcome and Undo restores the previous values. A change the person can't make says why instead of offering Accept.

Props:
- `title: string`: Heading of the review ("Proposed changes to 6 records").
- `changes: readonly ProposedChange[]`
- `decisions?: Readonly<Record<string, ChangeDecision>>`: Controlled decisions. Undecided changes are left out: nothing is applied without a decision.
- `defaultDecisions?: Readonly<Record<string, ChangeDecision>>` = `{}`
- `onDecisionsChange?: (decisions: Record<string, ChangeDecision>) => void`
- `onApply: (acceptedIds: string[]) => void`: Apply the accepted changes (ids in list order).
- `applying?: boolean` = `false`: Applying: the button shows progress and the decisions lock.
- `outcomes?: Readonly<Record<string, ChangeOutcome>>`: Once applied: each change's outcome by id. Shows the results and Undo.
- `onUndo?: () => void`: Restore what was there before. Shown once changes are applied.
- `undoing?: boolean` = `false`
- `undone?: boolean` = `false`: The applied changes were undone: says so, and the review is closed.
- `summary?: ReactNode`: Extra content under the heading: provenance ("Based on 42 records matching Overdue").

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).
States: applying, undoing, undone.

**When to use**

- Before an AI changes anything: the proposed changes as diffs (a field’s before and after, or a text rewrite word by word), each accepted or rejected, then applied together.
- After applying, pass `outcomes` (each change’s result) and `onUndo`: one Undo restores exactly what was there before.
- Mark a change the person can’t make with `blockedReason` instead of hiding it, so the count adds up.

**When not to use**

- A single suggestion inside a field → `Suggestion`
- Changes a person made by hand → the action itself, with a Toast and Undo

**Do:** Each change shows what it was, what it will be and why; nothing is applied until accepted.

```tsx
<ReviewChanges
  title="Proposed changes to 1 record"
  changes={[{ id: 'c1', target: 'Master cleaning agreement', field: 'Status', before: 'Overdue', after: 'Pending', reason: 'A signed renewal was added on 12 Sep.' }]}
  onApply={() => undefined}
/>
```

**Don't:** An AI action that applies at once with no preview: people can’t see what will change, or undo it.

```tsx
<Text>
  <Button>Fix overdue records with AI</Button>
</Text>
```

**Accessibility**

- Removed and added text is struck through and underlined as well as tinted, and each carries a visually hidden “removed”/“added” (or “Was … will be …”), because screen readers don’t announce `del` and `ins`.
- Accept and Reject are toggle buttons (`aria-pressed`) grouped per change and named by it; the count of accepted changes and the result after applying are polite status messages.

Stories: `components-reviewchanges--reviewing`, `components-reviewchanges--partly-decided`, `components-reviewchanges--text-rewrite`, `components-reviewchanges--with-blocked-change`, `components-reviewchanges--applying`, `components-reviewchanges--applied`, `components-reviewchanges--partly-failed`, `components-reviewchanges--undone`.
Composes: AiMarker, Badge, Button, Icon, Spinner, Toggle.
Tokens read: `button.danger.bg`, `button.danger.bg-hover`, `button.danger.fg`, `button.ghost.bg-hover`, `button.ghost.fg`, `button.primary.bg`, `button.primary.bg-hover`, `button.primary.fg`, `button.secondary.bg`, `button.secondary.bg-hover`, `button.secondary.border`, `button.secondary.fg`, `color.ai.bg`, `color.ai.border`, `color.ai.fg`, `color.bg.hover`, `color.bg.selected`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.status.danger.bg`, `color.status.danger.border`, `color.status.danger.fg`, `color.status.info.bg`, `color.status.info.border`, `color.status.info.fg`, `color.status.neutral.bg`, `color.status.neutral.border`, `color.status.neutral.fg`, `color.status.success.bg`, `color.status.success.border`, `color.status.success.fg`, `color.status.warning.bg`, `color.status.warning.border`, `color.status.warning.fg`, `ease.linear`, `ease.standard`, `focus.ring.width`, `font.weight.strong`, `icon.stroke`, `motion.fast`, `motion.spin`, `radius.control`, `radius.pill`, `size.control.lg`, `size.control.md`, `size.control.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.target-min`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.md`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.2xs`, `space.inset.lg`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `text.body`, `text.body-lg`, `text.caption`, `text.heading-4`, `text.label`.

### SearchField

component · `src/components/SearchField/SearchField.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/SearchField.usage.tsx`

A search input: type="search", a search icon, and a clear button once there is a query. Clearing (button or Escape) empties it and keeps focus in the field.

Props:
- `id?: string`: Id of the input. Generated when omitted.
- `label: string`: Visible label and accessible name ("Search records"). Required; hideLabel when the page makes it obvious.
- `hideLabel?: boolean`
- `description?: string`
- `value: string`: The query. Controlled: results follow it as it changes.
- `onValueChange: (value: string) => void`
- `clearLabel?: string` = `'Clear search'`: Accessible name of the clear button.
- …plus the native attributes of `AriaAttributes`, `Attributes`, `DOMAttributes`, `HTMLAttributes`, `InputHTMLAttributes`, `RefAttributes`.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).
States: hideLabel.

**When to use**

- Filtering a list or table by text as people type, in the list’s `role="search"` toolbar.
- It is controlled: pass `value` and `onValueChange`, and derive the rows from the query. The clear button (and Escape) empty it and keep focus in the field.

**When not to use**

- Picking one value from a known list → `Select`
- Entering data in a form → `TextField`

**Do:** A labelled search with a clear button once there is a query.

```tsx
<SearchField label="Search records" value="lease" onValueChange={() => undefined} />
```

**Don't:** A plain text field for search: not announced as a search, no search icon, and no quick way to clear.

```tsx
<TextField label="Search records (don’t example)" defaultValue="lease" />
```

**Accessibility**

- `label` is required; `hideLabel` hides it visually only. The input is `type="search"`.
- The clear button is named by `clearLabel` (“Clear search”) and is at least the minimum target size; clearing returns focus to the input.
- Announce the result count elsewhere, once (a list’s `Pagination` with `announce`, or a polite status line), not on every keystroke from the field.

Stories: `components-searchfield--empty`, `components-searchfield--with-query`, `components-searchfield--hidden-label`, `components-searchfield--with-description`.
Composes: Field, Icon.
Tokens read: `color.bg.hover`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.focus`, `color.status.danger.fg`, `focus.ring.offset`, `focus.ring.width`, `icon.stroke`, `radius.control`, `size.control.lg`, `size.control.md`, `size.control.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.target-min`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.inset.xs`, `text.body`, `text.body-lg`, `text.caption`, `text.label`.

### SegmentedControl

component · `src/components/SegmentedControl/SegmentedControl.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/SegmentedControl.usage.tsx`

One value from a few, always exactly one, shown as joined segments: a date range, a view density. Radio semantics (Radix RadioGroup): a named radiogroup of radios; Tab enters at the checked one, arrow keys move and select.

Props:
- `label: string`: The question the options answer ("Date range"). Names the group. Required.
- `hideLabel?: boolean` = `false`: Hide the label visually when the options explain themselves; it stays the group's name.
- `options: readonly SegmentedOption[]`: Two to five options.
- `value?: string`
- `defaultValue?: string`
- `onValueChange?: (value: string) => void`

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).
States: hideLabel.

**When to use**

- Choosing one of two to five short options that change what the page shows, where one is always chosen: a date range, a density, list or board.
- It is a radio group underneath (a named radiogroup of radios), because exactly one value is always selected and it can’t be cleared. Tab reaches the checked option; arrow keys move and select at once.

**When not to use**

- A choice inside a form that is submitted → `RadioGroup`
- More than five options, or long labels → `Select`
- Switching panels of content → `Tabs`
- Independent on/off options → `Switch` or `Checkbox`

**Do:** A named group of short, parallel options with one always selected.

```tsx
<SegmentedControl label="Date range (do example)" options={ranges} defaultValue="30d" />
```

**Don't:** A row of buttons faking a selection: nothing tells assistive tech which one is chosen, or that they belong together.

```tsx
<Cluster gap="2xs">
  <Button variant="secondary" size="sm">
    7 days
  </Button>
  <Button size="sm">30 days</Button>
  <Button variant="secondary" size="sm">
    90 days
  </Button>
</Cluster>
```

**Accessibility**

- `label` is required and names the group; `hideLabel` hides it visually only.
- The checked segment is raised, outlined and heavier, not just a different colour.
- Arrow keys select as they move (selection follows focus), so each move updates the page: keep the update fast and don’t move focus.

Stories: `components-segmentedcontrol--visible-label`, `components-segmentedcontrol--hidden-label`, `components-segmentedcontrol--first-selected`, `components-segmentedcontrol--two-options`.
Tokens read: `color.bg.subtle`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.muted`, `font.weight.strong`, `radius.control`, `shadow.card`, `size.control.sm`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.inset.2xs`, `space.inset.sm`, `text.label`.

### Select

component · `src/components/Select/Select.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Select.usage.tsx`

Single-choice list. Behaviour (keyboard, typeahead, focus, ARIA) comes from Radix Select.

Props:
- `label: string`: Visible label and accessible name of the trigger. Required.
- `hideLabel?: boolean`
- `options: readonly SelectOption[]`
- `value?: string`
- `defaultValue?: string`
- `onValueChange?: (value: string) => void`
- `placeholder?: string` = `'Select…'`
- `description?: string`
- `error?: string`
- `size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'` = `'md'`
- `disabled?: boolean`
- `required?: boolean`
- `name?: string`: Form field name; a hidden native select carries the value in forms.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Render the list open (gallery and tests).
- `id?: string`: Id of the trigger, for an error summary link. Generated when omitted.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: size (sm | md | lg).
States: hideLabel, disabled, required, defaultOpen.

**When to use**

- Choosing one option from a list of about five or more, where showing them all would crowd the form.

**When not to use**

- Two to four options that benefit from being compared → `RadioGroup`
- On or off → `Switch` or `Checkbox`
- Running an action → `Menu`

**Do:** Many options, a clear label, and a sensible default.

```tsx
<Select label="Status" options={STATUSES} defaultValue="draft" />
```

**Don't:** Two options hidden behind a click. Radio buttons show both at once.

```tsx
<Select
  label="Billing"
  options={[
    { value: 'monthly', label: 'Monthly' },
    { value: 'yearly', label: 'Yearly' },
  ]}
  placeholder="Choose"
/>
```

**Accessibility**

- Keyboard, typeahead and focus return come from Radix; the trigger’s accessible name is the `label`.
- A hidden native select carries the value, so `name` works inside a form.

Stories: `components-select--placeholder`, `components-select--with-value`, `components-select--with-description`, `components-select--with-error`, `components-select--disabled`, `components-select--small`, `components-select--large`, `components-select--open`.
Composes: Field, Icon.
Tokens read: `color.bg.elevated`, `color.bg.hover`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.link`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.status.danger.fg`, `icon.stroke`, `radius.control`, `radius.surface`, `shadow.popover`, `size.control.lg`, `size.control.md`, `size.control.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.inset.xs`, `text.body`, `text.body-lg`, `text.caption`, `text.label`, `z.dropdown`.

### Skeleton

component · `src/components/Skeleton/Skeleton.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Skeleton.usage.tsx`

Placeholder for content on first load. Hidden from assistive tech: mark the region that is loading with aria-busy="true" and say what is loading in text (a status line or Spinner label). On refresh keep the existing content instead; never swap usable values for skeletons. The pulse stops under prefers-reduced-motion (motion.pulse collapses to 0ms).

Props:
- `shape?: SkeletonShape` = `'text'`: Mirror the shape of what is loading: lines of text, a block (card, chart), or a table row.
- `lines?: number` = `3`: text: number of lines. The last one is shorter, like a paragraph.
- `columns?: number` = `4`: table-row: number of cells. Render inside TableBody, under the real header.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: shape (text | block | table-row).

**When to use**

- The first load of content whose layout is known: text lines, a card or chart block, table rows under the real header.
- Mirror the shape of what is coming so nothing jumps when it arrives.

**When not to use**

- A short action such as saving → `Button` with `loading`
- Loading of unknown shape → `Spinner`

**Do:** Keep the real card and heading; only the content that is loading is a skeleton.

```tsx
<Card>
  <CardBody>
    <Skeleton lines={3} />
  </CardBody>
</Card>
```

**Don't:** One big block for a page of mixed content: it says nothing about what is coming.

```tsx
<Stack>
  <Skeleton shape="block" />
</Stack>
```

**Accessibility**

- Skeletons are hidden from assistive tech; the region that is loading should say so (for example `aria-busy` on it).
- The pulse stops under reduced motion.

Stories: `components-skeleton--text`, `components-skeleton--single-line`, `components-skeleton--block`, `components-skeleton--table-rows`.
Tokens read: `color.bg.placeholder`, `color.border.default`, `ease.standard`, `motion.pulse`, `radius.indicator`, `radius.surface`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.skeleton.block`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`.

### Slider
