component · `src/components/Slider/Slider.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Slider.usage.tsx`

Picks a number, or a range, on a continuous scale where the exact value matters less than the position: volume, a price filter. Every thumb is keyboard operable (arrows, Page Up/Down, Home/End) and says its value in words; a click on the track moves the nearest thumb, so no drag is needed. For an exact number use a TextField. Behaviour from Radix Slider.

Props:
- `label: string`: Visible label and accessible name: what the value is ("Price", "Volume"). Required.
- `description?: string`
- `error?: string`
- `id?: string`: Id of the first thumb, for an error summary link. Generated when omitted.
- `value?: number[]`: One value for a single slider, two for a range.
- `defaultValue?: number[]` = `[0]`
- `onValueChange?: (value: number[]) => void`
- `onValueCommit?: (value: number[]) => void`: Called once when the user lets go or finishes a key press: the moment to save or refetch.
- `min?: number`
- `max?: number`
- `step?: number`
- `minStepsBetweenThumbs?: number`: Least number of steps between the two thumbs of a range.
- `formatValue?: (value: number) => string` = `String`: A value in words ("£40", "40%"). Shown beside the track and read out as aria-valuetext.
- `thumbLabels?: [string, string]` = `['minimum', 'maximum']`: Range only: the names of the two thumbs, appended to the label ("Price, minimum").
- `disabled?: boolean`
- `name?: string`: Submits each thumb's value as a hidden input with this name.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).
States: disabled.

**When to use**

- A value on a continuous scale where position matters more than the exact number: volume, a price filter, a threshold.
- A range: pass two values in `defaultValue` (or `value`), and name the thumbs with `thumbLabels`.
- Say the value in words with `formatValue` (“£40”, “40%”); it is shown beside the track and read out for each thumb.
- Refetch or save on `onValueCommit` (once, when the user lets go), not on every `onValueChange`.

**When not to use**

- An exact number (a quantity, an amount) → `TextField type="number"`
- A few named levels → `SegmentedControl` or `RadioGroup`

**Do:** A labelled range with its value in words; every thumb works with arrow keys.

```tsx
<Slider label="Price" defaultValue={[20, 80]} max={200} step={5} formatValue={(v) => `£${String(v)}`} />
```

**Don't:** A slider for an exact figure: hitting 1,250 by dragging is tedious. Use a field.

```tsx
<Slider label="Invoice amount" defaultValue={[1250]} max={10000} />
```

**Accessibility**

- Each thumb is a `slider` with `aria-valuetext` from `formatValue`; in a range each is named “label, minimum” and “label, maximum”.
- Keyboard: arrows move one step, Page Up/Down ten, Home/End to the ends. A click on the track moves the nearest thumb, so no drag is needed (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7).
- Thumbs are `size.target-min` (24px). `description` and `error` use the shared field anatomy; `id` lands on the first thumb.

Stories: `components-slider--single`, `components-slider--with-description`, `components-slider--range`, `components-slider--stepped`, `components-slider--with-error`, `components-slider--disabled`.
Composes: Field, Icon.
Tokens read: `color.action.primary`, `color.action.primary-hover`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.status.danger.fg`, `icon.stroke`, `radius.control`, `radius.pill`, `shadow.card`, `size.bar`, `size.control.lg`, `size.control.md`, `size.control.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.target-min`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.md`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.inset.xs`, `text.body`, `text.body-lg`, `text.caption`, `text.label`.

### Spinner

component · `src/components/Spinner/Spinner.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Spinner.usage.tsx`

Indeterminate progress for short or briefly unpredictable waits. Longer, shaped waits get a Skeleton.

Props:
- `size?: SpinnerSize` = `'sm'`
- `label?: string`: Standalone use: what is loading ("Loading records"). Renders a status region that announces it. Omit inside a control that already has a name (Button does): the spinner is then decorative.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: size (sm | md).

**When to use**

- Short waits of unknown length where the shape of the result isn’t known.
- Inside a pending button, through `Button loading` rather than directly.

**When not to use**

- Loading a page, list or card whose layout is known → `Skeleton`
- A pending form submit → `Button` with `loading`

**Do:** The pending state belongs to the button that started it.

```tsx
<Button loading>Save changes</Button>
```

**Don't:** A spinner standing in for a whole list: the page jumps when the rows arrive.

```tsx
<Cluster justify="center">
  <Spinner size="md" label="Loading records" />
</Cluster>
```

**Accessibility**

- A standalone spinner takes a `label` and is announced as a status; inside a button it is decorative and the label stays.
- It keeps turning under reduced motion: it is the only sign of progress.

Stories: `components-spinner--standalone`, `components-spinner--standalone-medium`, `components-spinner--decorative`.
Tokens read: `color.fg.muted`, `ease.linear`, `focus.ring.width`, `motion.spin`, `radius.pill`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`.

### Stat

component · `src/components/Stat/Stat.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Stat.usage.tsx`

One headline number in a tile: label, value and an optional change. The change shows its direction as an icon and says it in words to assistive tech; its colour (tone) only adds whether that is good or bad.

Props:
- `label: string`: What is counted ("Active records"). Required.
- `value: string`: The number, formatted for the locale ("1,284", "$1.2M"). Tabular figures.
- `delta?: StatDelta`
- `comparison?: string`: What the delta compares against ("vs previous 30 days").
- `directionLabels?: Record<StatDirection, string>` = `DIRECTION_LABELS`: Words read before the delta, per direction. Visually the icon carries it.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

**When to use**

- A headline number on a dashboard or overview: a count, a total, a rate, with an optional change and what it compares against.
- Set `delta.direction` from the numbers (up, down, flat) and `delta.tone` from what it means (positive, negative, neutral): fewer overdue records is down and positive.
- Put several in a `Switcher`, so they sit in one row or one column, never a ragged wrap.

**When not to use**

- Usage against a limit → `Meter`
- A value among a record’s properties → a definition list in the record’s aside
- Many numbers to compare → `Table`

**Do:** Direction from the numbers, tone from the meaning, and what the change compares against.

```tsx
<Switcher threshold="xs">
  <Stat label="Overdue records" value="14" delta={{ value: '3', direction: 'up', tone: 'negative' }} comparison="vs previous 30 days" />
  <Stat label="Pending approvals" value="9" delta={{ value: '25%', direction: 'down', tone: 'positive' }} comparison="vs previous 30 days" />
</Switcher>
```

**Don't:** A bare number in coloured text: no label, no comparison, and the colour is the only hint of whether it is good.

```tsx
<Text size="body-lg">14 (+3)</Text>
```

**Accessibility**

- The direction is an icon plus a visually hidden word (“Up”, “Down”, “No change”; set with `directionLabels`); tone colour only adds good or bad, never carries it alone.
- Values use tabular figures, so columns of stats line up.
- Format numbers for the locale before passing them; the tile doesn’t format.

Stories: `components-stat--value-only`, `components-stat--up-positive`, `components-stat--up-negative`, `components-stat--down-positive`, `components-stat--down-neutral`, `components-stat--flat`.
Composes: Icon.
Tokens read: `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.status.danger.fg`, `color.status.success.fg`, `font.weight.strong`, `icon.stroke`, `radius.surface`, `shadow.card`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.md`, `text.caption`, `text.heading-2`, `text.label`.

### Stepper

component · `src/components/Stepper/Stepper.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Stepper.usage.tsx`

Where someone is in an ordered task. An ordered list: completed steps show a check and a hidden "Completed" prefix, the current one has aria-current="step" and a heavier mark, upcoming ones their number. State is never carried by colour alone. Not navigation: steps are not links.

Props:
- `label: string`: Accessible name of the list ("Setup steps"). Required.
- `steps: readonly StepperStep[]`
- `current: number`: Index (from 0) of the step being done now. Earlier steps are completed, later ones upcoming.
- `completedLabel?: string` = `'Completed'`: Visually hidden prefix read before a completed step's label.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

**When to use**

- Showing where someone is in a task whose steps must be done in order: setup, a multi-step create. Pair it with `FocusedLayout` and copy the Setup wizard example.
- Three to six steps with short, parallel labels. Keep the list the same on every step.

**When not to use**

- Sections that can be visited in any order → `NavTabs` (routes) or `Tabs` (panels)
- A form with a few sections → one page with cards (the Create and edit example)
- Progress of a background job → `Progress`

**Do:** An ordered list: done steps show a check, the current one is marked, the rest show their number.

```tsx
<Stepper label="Setup steps (do example)" steps={steps} current={2} />
```

**Don't:** Ordered steps as navigation tabs: it suggests people can jump to Plan before naming the workspace.

```tsx
<NavTabs
  label="Setup steps (don’t example)"
  current="/setup/workspace"
  items={steps.map((s) => ({ label: s.label, href: `/setup/${s.label.toLowerCase()}` }))}
/>
```

**Accessibility**

- An ordered list named by the required `label`; the current step has `aria-current="step"`.
- Completed steps read “Completed: <label>” (a visually hidden prefix, set with `completedLabel`) and show a check; state is never colour alone.
- Steps are not links. Going back is the page’s Back button or a review step’s Edit.

Stories: `components-stepper--first-step`, `components-stepper--middle-step`, `components-stepper--last-step`, `components-stepper--all-completed`, `components-stepper--narrow`.
Composes: Icon.
Tokens read: `color.action.primary`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.fg.on-action`, `focus.ring.width`, `font.weight.strong`, `icon.stroke`, `radius.pill`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.target-min`, `space.gap.lg`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xs`, `text.caption`, `text.label`.

### StreamingText

component · `src/components/StreamingText/StreamingText.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/StreamingText.usage.tsx`

Text that arrives token by token (an AI answer), rendered as safe Markdown with a caret while it streams. It holds no timers: the parent appends to `text`, so a story or test can pin any moment. Screen readers hear it through one polite live region, present from mount: "Generating…", then each sentence or paragraph once it is complete (never token by token, and never the whole answer again at the end), then "Stopped" if the person stops it. Text already there on mount (history) is not announced.

Props:
- `text: string`: Everything received so far, as Markdown. The parent appends tokens; this renders what it's given.
- `status?: StreamStatus` = `'complete'`
- `citation?: (number: number) => ReactNode`: Renders a numbered citation ([1]) found in the text, usually a Citation.
- `pendingLabel?: string` = `'Generating…'`: Shown, and announced, before the first token arrives.
- `stoppedLabel?: string` = `'Stopped.'`: Announced when the person stops the answer.
- `codeLabel?: string` = `'Code from the answer'`: Accessible name of code blocks in the answer.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: status (pending | streaming | complete | stopped | error).

**When to use**

- An AI answer that arrives token by token: pass everything received so far as `text` and the `status` (pending, streaming, complete, stopped, error).
- Any AI output shown as Markdown, streamed or not: it renders safely (no raw HTML, safe links only, no images).

**When not to use**

- Text a person wrote → `Text`: Markdown rendering belongs to model output
- A wait with no partial result → `Spinner` or `Progress`

**Do:** Partial text with a caret while it arrives; the parent appends, the component renders.

```tsx
<StreamingText text="It renews on **15 January 2027**, unless either side" status="streaming" />
```

**Don't:** A spinner that hides the answer until it’s finished: people wait without seeing progress, and can’t stop early.

```tsx
<Spinner label="Generating answer" />
```

**Accessibility**

- One polite live region, present from mount, announces “Generating…”, then each sentence or paragraph once it is complete, then “Stopped” if the person stops it. Never token by token, and never the whole answer again at the end.
- Text already there on mount (history) isn’t announced.
- The caret and the thinking dots are hidden from assistive technology and hold still under reduced motion (`motion.pulse` is 0).
- Model output is untrusted: raw HTML renders as text, links are http(s), mailto or in-app only, images are never loaded, and headings become bold text so an answer can’t change the page outline.

Stories: `components-streamingtext--pending`, `components-streamingtext--streaming`, `components-streamingtext--streaming-code`, `components-streamingtext--complete`, `components-streamingtext--stopped`, `components-streamingtext--with-citations`, `components-streamingtext--unsafe-input`.
Composes: Button, CodeBlock, CopyButton, Icon, Link, Markdown, Spinner.
Tokens read: `border.width.default`, `button.danger.bg`, `button.danger.bg-hover`, `button.danger.fg`, `button.ghost.bg-hover`, `button.ghost.fg`, `button.primary.bg`, `button.primary.bg-hover`, `button.primary.fg`, `button.secondary.bg`, `button.secondary.bg-hover`, `button.secondary.border`, `button.secondary.fg`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.border.default`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.link`, `color.fg.muted`, `ease.linear`, `ease.standard`, `focus.ring.offset`, `focus.ring.width`, `icon.stroke`, `motion.fast`, `motion.pulse`, `motion.slow`, `motion.spin`, `radius.control`, `radius.indicator`, `radius.pill`, `size.control.lg`, `size.control.md`, `size.control.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.target-min`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.2xs`, `space.inset.lg`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `text.body`, `text.body-lg`, `text.caption`, `text.code`, `text.label`.

### Suggestion

component · `src/components/Suggestion/Suggestion.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Suggestion.usage.tsx`

A multi-line text field that can show an inline AI suggestion as ghost text: Tab accepts it, Escape dismisses it, and typing over it ignores it. The suggestion is marked as AI, is never the field's value until accepted, and never moves the caret or focus. Screen readers hear "Suggestion ready" once, politely, with the text and the keys; the field's value reads as what was typed.

Props:
- `label: string`: Visible label and accessible name. Required.
- `value: string`: What the person has written.
- `onValueChange: (value: string) => void`
- `suggestion?: string | undefined`: The AI's suggested continuation of `value`, shown as muted ghost text after it. It is never part of the value until accepted. Undefined or empty: no suggestion.
- `pending?: boolean` = `false`: The suggestion is still arriving: shown, but it can't be accepted until it's complete.
- `onAccept: () => void`: Tab (or Accept): the caller appends the suggestion to the value.
- `onDismiss: () => void`: Escape, Dismiss, or typing over it: the caller drops the suggestion.
- `description?: string`: Supporting text, linked with aria-describedby.
- `error?: string`
- `rows?: number` = `4`: Visible rows before it grows.
- `id?: string`: Id of the text box, for an error summary link. Generated when omitted.
- `disabled?: boolean` = `false`

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).
States: pending, disabled.

**When to use**

- A text field where the AI can suggest what comes next (a description, a reply): the suggestion shows as ghost text, Tab accepts, Esc dismisses, typing over it ignores it.
- The caller owns the value and the suggestion: append on `onAccept`, drop on `onDismiss`. Keep what was there before, so one Undo restores it.
- Put the AI action (“Suggest description”) beside the field, never in place of writing it by hand.

**When not to use**

- A long draft that needs review before it lands → a generated block marked with `AiMarker`, or `ReviewChanges` for a rewrite
- A field with no AI → `Textarea`

**Do:** Muted ghost text after what was typed, marked as AI, with the keys and buttons to accept or dismiss.

```tsx
<Suggestion
  label="Description"
  value="Covers facilities maintenance,"
  onValueChange={() => undefined}
  suggestion=" cleaning and security for both offices."
  onAccept={() => undefined}
  onDismiss={() => undefined}
/>
```

**Don't:** AI text written straight into the value: it looks like the person’s own words and nobody accepted it.

```tsx
<Textarea label="Description" defaultValue="Covers facilities maintenance, cleaning and security for both offices." />
```

**Accessibility**

- The ghost text is never part of the value, so the field reads as what was typed; the suggestion is in the field’s description, and a polite status says “Suggestion ready” once, never character by character.
- Tab accepts only while a complete suggestion shows; otherwise Tab moves focus as usual. Esc dismisses without closing a surrounding dialog.
- Accept and Dismiss buttons give pointer and switch users the same choice; the mark is text (“AI suggestion”), not colour alone.

Stories: `components-suggestion--ready`, `components-suggestion--pending`, `components-suggestion--no-suggestion`, `components-suggestion--empty-field`, `components-suggestion--with-error`, `components-suggestion--disabled`.
Composes: AiMarker, Button, Field, Icon, Kbd, Spinner.
Tokens read: `button.danger.bg`, `button.danger.bg-hover`, `button.danger.fg`, `button.ghost.bg-hover`, `button.ghost.fg`, `button.primary.bg`, `button.primary.bg-hover`, `button.primary.fg`, `button.secondary.bg`, `button.secondary.bg-hover`, `button.secondary.border`, `button.secondary.fg`, `color.ai.bg`, `color.ai.border`, `color.ai.fg`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.status.danger.fg`, `ease.linear`, `ease.standard`, `focus.ring.width`, `font.weight.strong`, `icon.stroke`, `motion.fast`, `motion.spin`, `radius.control`, `radius.indicator`, `radius.pill`, `size.control.lg`, `size.control.md`, `size.control.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.target-min`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.2xs`, `space.inset.lg`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.inset.xs`, `text.body`, `text.body-lg`, `text.caption`, `text.code`, `text.label`.

### Switch

component · `src/components/Switch/Switch.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Switch.usage.tsx`

An on/off setting that takes effect as a setting, not a form answer (use Checkbox for those). State shows as thumb position and fill, never colour alone. Behaviour from Radix Switch.

Props:
- `label: string`: Visible label and accessible name: the setting, not the state ("Email me a weekly digest"). Required.
- `description?: string`
- `checked?: boolean`
- `defaultChecked?: boolean`
- `onCheckedChange?: (checked: boolean) => void`
- `disabled?: boolean`
- `name?: string`
- `value?: string`
- `id?: string`: Id of the switch, for an error summary link. Generated when omitted.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).
States: checked, defaultChecked, disabled.

**When to use**

- A setting that takes effect the moment it is flipped, like the notification settings on a settings page.

**When not to use**

- A choice saved with the rest of a form → `Checkbox`
- Choosing between two named options → `RadioGroup`

**Do:** The label names the setting; the switch shows its state.

```tsx
<Stack gap="md">
  <Switch label="Email me a weekly digest" description="Every Monday morning." defaultChecked />
</Stack>
```

**Don't:** A label that describes the state (“On”) reads wrong as soon as the switch changes.

```tsx
<Switch label="On" defaultChecked />
```

**Accessibility**

- Exposed as `role="switch"` with `aria-checked`; Space toggles it.
- Confirm the change with a quiet status (for example a Toast) when the effect isn’t visible on the page.

Stories: `components-switch--off`, `components-switch--on`, `components-switch--with-description`, `components-switch--disabled`, `components-switch--disabled-on`.
Tokens read: `color.action.primary`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.fg.on-action`, `radius.pill`, `size.control.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.target-min`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.md`, `space.inset.2xs`, `text.body`, `text.caption`.

### Table

component · `src/components/Table/Table.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Table.usage.tsx`

Data table: native table semantics, sticky header, tabular numbers. The scroll container is a focusable, labelled region so keyboard users can scroll it.

Props:
- `caption: string`: Caption: the table's accessible name. Required.
- `hideCaption?: boolean` = `false`
- `maxHeight?: ScrollRegionToken`: Cap the height so the sticky header scrolls with the rows. Defaults to no cap.
- `children: ReactNode`

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: maxHeight (sm | md | lg).
States: hideCaption.

#### TableBody

component, part of Table.

Props:
- `children: ReactNode`

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`.

#### TableCell

component, part of Table.

Props:
- `children?: ReactNode`
- `numeric?: boolean` = `false`
- `rowHeader?: boolean` = `false`: Mark the cell that names the row (usually the first) as a row header.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`.

#### TableHead

component, part of Table.

Props:
- `children: ReactNode`

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`.

#### TableHeaderCell

component, part of Table.

Props:
- `children: ReactNode`
- `numeric?: boolean` = `false`: Right-align (inline-end) numeric columns so digits line up.
- `sort?: SortDirection | undefined`: Current sort of this column. Omit on unsorted columns.
- `onSort?: () => void`: Makes the header a sort button. aria-sort is set on the header cell.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`.

#### TableRow

component, part of Table.

Props:
- `selected?: boolean` = `false`: The row is in the current selection: it is filled, not just checked, so the selection reads at a glance. Pair it with a row checkbox named after the row ("Select Hardware lease"); the checkbox carries the state for assistive tech.
- …plus the native attributes of `AriaAttributes`, `Attributes`, `DOMAttributes`, `HTMLAttributes`, `RefAttributes`.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

**When to use**

- Records people compare across the same attributes: the default for a list page.
- Numbers right-aligned with `numeric`; the first cell of each row is its `rowHeader`.
- Selectable rows: a first column of `Checkbox` with `hideLabel`, named after each row, and `selected` on the `TableRow` so a selected row is filled, not just ticked. Bulk actions go in a bar that shows the count (see the List page example).

**When not to use**

- Items that are mostly visual or have fewer than four attributes worth comparing → cards in a `Grid`
- Laying out a form or a page → layout primitives
- A single record’s properties → a definition list: `Stack as="dl"` with `Text as="dt"/"dd"`

**Do:** A caption names the table, the first cell heads the row, amounts line up on the right.

```tsx
<Table caption="Records" hideCaption>
  <TableHead>
    <TableRow>
      <TableHeaderCell>Name</TableHeaderCell>
      <TableHeaderCell>Status</TableHeaderCell>
      <TableHeaderCell numeric>Amount</TableHeaderCell>
    </TableRow>
  </TableHead>
  <TableBody>
    {ROWS.map((r) => (
      <TableRow key={r.name}>
        <TableCell rowHeader>{r.name}</TableCell>
        <TableCell>
          <Badge tone={r.status === 'Approved' ? 'success' : 'warning'}>{r.status}</Badge>
        </TableCell>
        <TableCell numeric>{r.amount}</TableCell>
      </TableRow>
    ))}
  </TableBody>
</Table>
```

**Don't:** A table used to lay out a form: the grid means nothing, and screen readers announce rows and columns that aren’t there.

```tsx
<Table caption="Profile" hideCaption>
  <TableBody>
    <TableRow>
      <TableCell rowHeader>Name</TableCell>
      <TableCell>Sam Rivera</TableCell>
      <TableCell rowHeader>Role</TableCell>
      <TableCell>Owner</TableCell>
    </TableRow>
  </TableBody>
</Table>
```

**Accessibility**

- `caption` is required and names the scroll region; `hideCaption` keeps it for screen readers only.
- Sortable headers are buttons, and the sorted column carries `aria-sort`.
- The scroll container is focusable, so keyboard users can scroll a wide or capped table.

Stories: `components-table--sorted-ascending`, `components-table--sorted-descending`, `components-table--sticky-header`, `components-table--selectable`.
Composes: Icon.
Tokens read: `color.bg.hover`, `color.bg.selected`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.muted`, `icon.stroke`, `radius.control`, `radius.surface`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.scroll-region.lg`, `size.scroll-region.md`, `size.scroll-region.sm`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.scroll-padding.start`, `text.body`, `text.label`, `z.sticky`.

### Tabs

component · `src/components/Tabs/Tabs.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Tabs.usage.tsx`

Tabs: arrow-key roving focus and ARIA wiring come from Radix Tabs.

Props:
- `value?: string`
- `defaultValue?: string`
- `onValueChange?: (value: string) => void`
- `children: ReactNode`

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

#### Tab

component, part of Tabs.

Props:
- `value: string`
- `disabled?: boolean`
- `children: ReactNode`

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`.

#### TabList

component, part of Tabs.

Props:
- `label: string`: Accessible name of the tab list. Required.
- `children: ReactNode`

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`.

#### TabPanel

component, part of Tabs.

Props:
- `value: string`
- `children: ReactNode`

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`.

**When to use**

- Switching between views of the same record or object in place, on one page: overview, activity, history.
- Tabs or NavTabs? If choosing one only swaps panels and the URL stays the same, it is `Tabs`. If it changes the URL, it is `NavTabs`.

**When not to use**

- Sections that are each their own route → `NavTabs`
- Moving between pages or areas of the app → `Nav`, or a settings sub-nav with `Nav`
- Steps that must be done in order → `Stepper` in a `FocusedLayout`
- Content people need to compare side by side → one page with sections

**Do:** Short, parallel labels for views of one record.

```tsx
<Tabs defaultValue="overview">
  <TabList label="Record sections">
    <Tab value="overview">Overview</Tab>
    <Tab value="activity">Activity</Tab>
  </TabList>
  <TabPanel value="overview">
    <Text>Summary of the record and its owner.</Text>
  </TabPanel>
  <TabPanel value="activity">
    <Text>Recent changes, newest first.</Text>
  </TabPanel>
</Tabs>
```

**Don't:** Tabs as a wizard: “Step 2” hides what step 1 required and lets people skip it.

```tsx
<Tabs defaultValue="1">
  <TabList label="Setup">
    <Tab value="1">Step 1</Tab>
    <Tab value="2">Step 2</Tab>
    <Tab value="3">Step 3</Tab>
  </TabList>
  <TabPanel value="1">
    <Text>Company details</Text>
  </TabPanel>
  <TabPanel value="2">
    <Text>Invite people</Text>
  </TabPanel>
  <TabPanel value="3">
    <Text>Choose a plan</Text>
  </TabPanel>
</Tabs>
```

**Accessibility**

- `TabList` requires a `label`; tabs, panels and their relationships use the ARIA tabs pattern.
- Arrow keys move between tabs; Tab moves into the panel.

Stories: `components-tabs--default`, `components-tabs--second-selected`, `components-tabs--disabled-tab`.
Tokens read: `color.action.primary`, `color.border.default`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.muted`, `focus.ring.width`, `size.control.md`, `space.gap.md`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.sm`, `text.label`.

### Tag

component · `src/components/Tag/Tag.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Tag.usage.tsx`

A compact value: an active filter chip, a label on a record. Removable when onRemove is set.

Props:
- `children: string`: The value it stands for ("Status: Overdue"). Required.
- `onRemove?: () => void`: Shows a remove button. The caller removes the tag and moves focus (to the next tag, or the control that adds them).
- `removeLabel?: string`: Accessible name of the remove button. Defaults to "Remove <children>".
- `removeRef?: Ref<HTMLButtonElement>`: Ref to the remove button, for moving focus between tags.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

**When to use**

- Active filters above a list, each removable: “Status: Overdue”.
- Labels on a record that people add and remove.
- After a removal, move focus to the next tag, or to the control that adds them (a Filters button) when none are left, as the List page example does with `removeRef`.

**When not to use**

- A status → `Badge`, mapped from the domain status
- An action → `Button`

**Do:** Filter chips that say what they filter, each with a named remove button.

```tsx
<Cluster gap="xs">
  <Tag onRemove={() => undefined}>Status: Active</Tag>
  <Tag onRemove={() => undefined}>Status: Pending</Tag>
</Cluster>
```

**Don't:** A status badge used as a filter chip: it looks like data about a record, and it can’t be removed.

```tsx
<Badge tone="success">Active</Badge>
```

**Accessibility**

- The remove button is named “Remove <label>” by default (override with `removeLabel`) and is at least the minimum target size.
- The tag itself isn’t interactive; only its remove button is.
- Put a group of tags in a list with a name (“Active filters”).

Stories: `components-tag--static`, `components-tag--removable`, `components-tag--long-value`.
Composes: Icon.
Tokens read: `color.bg.hover`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.muted`, `font.weight.strong`, `icon.stroke`, `radius.pill`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.target-min`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.inset.sm`, `text.caption`.

### Text

component · `src/components/Text/Text.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Text.usage.tsx`

Props:
- `children: ReactNode`
- `as?: 'p' | 'span' | 'div' | 'dt' | 'dd'` = `'p'`: dt/dd for label–value pairs inside a <Stack as="dl"> (a record's properties).
- `size?: 'body' | 'body-lg' | 'caption'` = `'body'`
- `tone?: 'default' | 'muted'` = `'default'`
- `numeric?: boolean` = `false`: Tabular figures for numbers that line up in columns.
- …plus the native attributes of `AriaAttributes`, `Attributes`, `DOMAttributes`, `HTMLAttributes`, `RefAttributes`.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: as (p | span | div | dt | dd); size (body | body-lg | caption); tone (default | muted).
States: numeric.

**When to use**

- Running text, descriptions and metadata, in one of three sizes and two tones.
- `numeric` for numbers that line up in columns; `as="dt"`/`as="dd"` for label–value pairs in a `Stack as="dl"`.

**When not to use**

- A title → `Heading`
- Status such as “Overdue” → `Badge`, which pairs the word with a tone and icon
- An error under a field → the field’s `error` prop

**Do:** Muted tone for secondary information, default tone for the content itself.

```tsx
<Stack gap="2xs">
  <Text>Hardware lease renews on 1 March.</Text>
  <Text size="caption" tone="muted">
    Updated 2 hours ago
  </Text>
</Stack>
```

**Don't:** Everything muted: the content the reader came for is as quiet as the metadata.

```tsx
<Stack gap="2xs">
  <Text tone="muted">Hardware lease renews on 1 March.</Text>
  <Text size="caption" tone="muted">
    Updated 2 hours ago
  </Text>
</Stack>
```

**Accessibility**

- Both tones meet 4.5:1 on every surface, in light and dark.
- Renders a `<p>` by default; pick `as="span"` inside inline contexts so the markup stays valid.

Stories: `components-text--body`, `components-text--body-large`, `components-text--caption`, `components-text--muted`, `components-text--numeric`, `components-text--definition-list`.
Tokens read: `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.muted`, `text.body`, `text.body-lg`, `text.caption`.

### TextField

component · `src/components/TextField/TextField.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/TextField.usage.tsx`

Props:
- `id?: string`: Id of the input, for an error summary link. Generated when omitted.
- `type?: 'text' | 'email' | 'password' | 'search' | 'tel' | 'url' | 'number'` = `'text'`: "password" adds a show-password toggle (WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.8). Pair it with autoComplete="current-password" or "new-password".
- `label: string`: Visible label and accessible name. Required; use hideLabel only when context makes it obvious.
- `hideLabel?: boolean`
- `description?: string`: Supporting text, linked with aria-describedby.
- `error?: string`: Error message. Sets aria-invalid and is announced with the field.
- `size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'` = `'md'`
- `showPasswordLabel?: string` = `'Show password'`: type="password" only: accessible name of the show-password toggle. It reports its state with aria-pressed.
- `defaultPasswordVisible?: boolean` = `false`: type="password" only: start with the password shown (gallery and tests).
- …plus the native attributes of `AriaAttributes`, `Attributes`, `DOMAttributes`, `HTMLAttributes`, `InputHTMLAttributes`, `RefAttributes`.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: type (text | email | password | search | tel | url | number); size (sm | md | lg).
States: hideLabel, defaultPasswordVisible.

**When to use**

- Short free text: names, emails, amounts, search, passwords.
- Set `type` and `autoComplete` so mobile keyboards, autofill and password managers do the right thing.

**When not to use**

- More than one line of text → `Textarea`
- Picking from a known list → `Select` (many options) or `RadioGroup` (a few)

**Do:** A visible label, helper text that explains format, and an error that says how to fix it.

```tsx
<Stack gap="md">
  <TextField label="Work email" type="email" description="We send invoices here." />
  <TextField label="Amount" type="number" defaultValue="0" error="Enter an amount greater than 0." />
</Stack>
```

**Don't:** Hidden labels on a form: the placeholder vanishes as soon as someone types, and so does the question.

```tsx
<Stack gap="md">
  <TextField label="Work email" hideLabel placeholder="Work email" />
  <TextField label="Amount" hideLabel placeholder="Amount" />
</Stack>
```

**Accessibility**

- `label` is required and is the accessible name; `hideLabel` is for fields whose context makes the question obvious, such as a search box.
- `description` and `error` are linked with `aria-describedby`; `error` sets `aria-invalid`.
- Pass `id` when an error summary links to the field.
- `type="password"` adds a show-password toggle (a button with `aria-pressed` and `aria-controls`), so nobody has to type a password blind or remember it to retype it (WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.8). Give it `autoComplete="current-password"` (sign-in) or `"new-password"` (sign-up, reset) so password managers fill it. Never block paste.

Stories: `components-textfield--default`, `components-textfield--filled`, `components-textfield--with-description`, `components-textfield--with-error`, `components-textfield--disabled`, `components-textfield--small`, `components-textfield--large`, `components-textfield--hidden-label`, `components-textfield--password`, `components-textfield--password-visible`.
Composes: Field, Icon.
Tokens read: `color.bg.hover`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.focus`, `color.status.danger.fg`, `focus.ring.offset`, `focus.ring.width`, `icon.stroke`, `radius.control`, `size.control.lg`, `size.control.md`, `size.control.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.target-min`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.2xs`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.inset.xs`, `text.body`, `text.body-lg`, `text.caption`, `text.label`.

### Textarea

component · `src/components/Textarea/Textarea.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Textarea.usage.tsx`

Multi-line text. Same anatomy and states as TextField; Enter inserts a newline, it never submits.

Props:
- `id?: string`: Id of the textarea, for an error summary link. Generated when omitted.
- `label: string`: Visible label and accessible name. Required.
- `hideLabel?: boolean`
- `description?: string`: Supporting text, linked with aria-describedby.
- `error?: string`: Error message. Sets aria-invalid and is announced with the field.
- …plus the native attributes of `AriaAttributes`, `Attributes`, `DOMAttributes`, `HTMLAttributes`, `RefAttributes`, `TextareaHTMLAttributes`.

**When to use**

**When not to use**

### Timeline

component · `src/components/Timeline/Timeline.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Timeline.usage.tsx`

A dated list of events (actor, verb, target, time): a record's activity, an audit trail, a feed. An ordered list of <time>-stamped sentences, so it reads the same with or without the rail.

Props:
- `label: string`: Accessible name of the list ("Activity on INV-2041"). Required.
- `events: readonly TimelineEvent[]`: Events in the order to show them, newest first by convention.
- `emptyText?: string` = `'No activity yet.'`: Shown when there are no events.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

**When to use**

- A record’s activity, an audit trail, a feed of changes: dated events, each a sentence of actor, verb and target.
- Format `time` for people (“2 hours ago”, “12 Mar 2026, 14:05”) and pass the ISO `dateTime` beside it; the component doesn’t format dates.
- Pass a `Link` as `target` when the thing changed has its own page. Put a comment or a before-and-after in `detail`.

**When not to use**

- The steps of a task still to do → `Stepper`
- Rows to sort, filter or act on → `Table`

**Do:** Each event is one sentence with who, what and when.

```tsx
<Timeline
  label="Activity on INV-2041"
  events={[
    { id: '2', actor: 'Priya Shah', verb: 'marked the invoice as', target: 'Paid', time: '12 Mar 2026, 14:05', dateTime: '2026-03-12T14:05:00Z' },
    { id: '1', actor: 'Priya Shah', verb: 'created the invoice', time: '1 Mar 2026, 16:22', dateTime: '2026-03-01T16:22:00Z' },
  ]}
/>
```

**Don't:** Bare field changes without who or when: nobody can tell what happened.

```tsx
<Stack gap="xs">
  <Text>status → Paid</Text>
  <Text>created</Text>
</Stack>
```

**Accessibility**

- An ordered list named by `label`; each event is a sentence with a `<time datetime>`, so it reads the same without the rail and markers (which are hidden).
- An empty list renders `emptyText` instead of an empty list.

Stories: `components-timeline--default`, `components-timeline--with-linked-targets`, `components-timeline--single-event`, `components-timeline--empty`.
Tokens read: `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.muted`, `font.weight.strong`, `radius.pill`, `size.icon.sm`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.md`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.inset.2xs`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `text.body`, `text.caption`.

### Toast

component · `src/components/Toast/Toast.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Toast.usage.tsx`

Declarative toast. Render inside a ToastProvider, or use the useToast() hook.

Props:
- `title: string`: Short message, always visible. Required.
- `description?: string`
- `tone?: ToastTone` = `'neutral'`: Tone with an icon, never colour alone. danger and warning are announced assertively.
- `open?: boolean`
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`
- `onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void`
- `duration?: number`: Auto-dismiss delay in ms. Infinity keeps it open (use for anything the user must act on).
- `closeLabel?: string` = `'Dismiss'`: Label of the dismiss button.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: tone (success | warning | danger | info | neutral).
States: open, defaultOpen.

#### ToastProvider

component, part of Toast. Hosts the toast viewport and the queue used by useToast(). Mount once near the app root.

Props:
- `children: ReactNode`
- `label?: string` = `'Notifications'`: Accessible label of the notifications region.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`.

#### useToast

utility, part of Toast. Imperative API: const toast = useToast(); toast({ title: 'Saved', tone: 'success' }).
Signature: `() => (toast: ToastInput) => void`

**When to use**

- Confirming the outcome of an action that doesn’t change the page visibly: saved, copied, export started.
- Call `useToast()` from inside the app; AppShell mounts the one `ToastProvider`.

**When not to use**

- Something people must fix or act on → `Banner` in the page, or an inline field error
- A form’s validation errors → field errors plus an error summary `Banner`

**Do:** A short confirmation that disappears by itself. Press the button to see it.

```tsx
<ToastProvider label="Notifications (do example)">
  <SaveButton />
</ToastProvider>
```

**Don't:** A failure that needs action, in a toast that auto-dismisses. Put it in a Banner where the problem is.

```tsx
<ToastProvider label="Notifications (don’t example)">
  <FailingButton />
</ToastProvider>
```

**Accessibility**

- Toasts live in a labelled region; success, info and neutral are announced politely, danger and warning assertively.
- The tone has an icon, never colour alone. Anything the user must act on needs `duration={Infinity}`, and usually isn’t a toast.

Stories: `components-toast--success`, `components-toast--warning`, `components-toast--danger`, `components-toast--info`, `components-toast--neutral`, `components-toast--imperative`.
Composes: Icon.
Tokens read: `color.bg.elevated`, `color.border.default`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.status.danger.fg`, `color.status.info.fg`, `color.status.neutral.fg`, `color.status.success.fg`, `color.status.warning.fg`, `focus.ring.width`, `icon.stroke`, `radius.control`, `radius.surface`, `shadow.popover`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.overlay-max`, `size.target-min`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.md`, `text.body`, `text.label`, `z.toast`.

### Toggle

component · `src/components/Toggle/Toggle.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Toggle.usage.tsx`

A button that stays pressed: a view option or formatting mode that applies immediately (Bold, Show archived). aria-pressed carries the state; pressed also changes fill, border and weight, never colour alone. For a setting use Switch; for one of several options use SegmentedControl. Behaviour from Radix Toggle.

Props:
- `label: string`: What it turns on ("Bold", "Show archived"). Constant: aria-pressed carries the state. Required.
- `icon?: IconName`: Leading icon from the system set.
- `hideLabel?: boolean` = `false`: Icon only; the label becomes the accessible name. Needs an icon, and pair it with a Tooltip showing the label.
- `pressed?: boolean`
- `defaultPressed?: boolean`
- `onPressedChange?: (pressed: boolean) => void`
- `size?: 'sm' | 'md'` = `'md'`
- `disabled?: boolean`

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: size (sm | md).
States: hideLabel, pressed, defaultPressed, disabled.

**When to use**

- A button that stays on: a view option or mode that applies immediately (Show archived, Bold, Preview).
- Icon only (`hideLabel` with an `icon`) in a dense toolbar, wrapped in a `Tooltip` that shows the same label.

**When not to use**

- A setting saved to the account → `Switch`
- One of several options → `SegmentedControl`
- An action that happens once → `Button`

**Do:** The label names what it turns on and never changes; pressed shows in fill, border and weight.

```tsx
<Cluster gap="sm">
  <Toggle label="Show archived" defaultPressed />
  <Tooltip content="Compact rows">
    <Toggle label="Compact rows" icon="menu" hideLabel />
  </Tooltip>
</Cluster>
```

**Don't:** A plain button that swaps its label between “Show archived” and “Hide archived”: the state is only in the words, and the name keeps changing.

```tsx
<Button variant="secondary" size="sm">
  Hide archived
</Button>
```

**Accessibility**

- A button with `aria-pressed`; Space and Enter toggle it. The label is the accessible name and stays constant.
- At least `size.control-sm` (32px), above the 24px target minimum.

Stories: `components-toggle--unpressed`, `components-toggle--pressed`, `components-toggle--with-icon`, `components-toggle--small`, `components-toggle--icon-only`, `components-toggle--disabled`.
Composes: Icon.
Tokens read: `color.bg.hover`, `color.bg.selected`, `color.border.default`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.muted`, `ease.standard`, `font.weight.strong`, `icon.stroke`, `motion.fast`, `radius.control`, `size.control.md`, `size.control.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.sm`, `text.label`.

### Toolbar

component · `src/components/Toolbar/Toolbar.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Toolbar.usage.tsx`

A row of related controls that is one tab stop: Tab enters it, ← → (↑ ↓ vertical) move between its buttons, Home and End jump, Tab leaves. For an editor's formatting bar or a selection's actions; not for page navigation. Behaviour from Radix Toolbar (roving tabindex).

Props:
- `label: string`: Accessible name: what the controls act on ("Conversation actions"). Required.
- `orientation?: 'horizontal' | 'vertical'` = `'horizontal'`
- `children: ReactNode`: ToolbarButton and ToolbarSeparator.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: orientation (horizontal | vertical).

#### ToolbarButton

component, part of Toolbar. One control in a Toolbar. A hidden label or a shortcut shows in a tooltip on hover and focus.

Props:
- `children: string`: Verb-first label. Also the accessible name when the label is hidden. Required.
- `icon?: IconName`
- `hideLabel?: boolean` = `false`: Show only the icon; the label moves into a tooltip and the accessible name. Needs `icon`.
- `onClick?: () => void`
- `disabled?: boolean`
- `pressed?: boolean`: A toggle (Bold, Unread only): its state as aria-pressed.
- `shortcut?: string`: Its keyboard shortcut, shown in the tooltip (register it with useShortcut).
- `tone?: 'default' | 'danger'` = `'default'`

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`.

#### ToolbarSeparator

component, part of Toolbar. A divider between groups of toolbar controls.


**When to use**

- A group of actions on one thing that people use repeatedly: a selection’s bulk actions, an editor’s formatting, a reading pane’s triage.
- Where one tab stop for the group saves keyboard users a dozen Tabs.

**When not to use**

- A page’s one or two primary actions → `Button`s in the `PageHeader`
- Navigation between pages or sections → `NavTabs` or `Nav`

**Do:** Related actions in one tab stop, grouped by separators, with shortcuts in their tooltips.

```tsx
<Toolbar label="Conversation actions">
  <ToolbarButton shortcut="e">
    Archive
  </ToolbarButton>
  <ToolbarButton shortcut="u">Mark as unread</ToolbarButton>
  <ToolbarSeparator />
  <ToolbarButton icon="download" hideLabel>
    Export
  </ToolbarButton>
</Toolbar>
```

**Don't:** A page’s main actions forced into a toolbar: they belong in the header, as ordinary buttons.

```tsx
<Cluster>
  <Button>New record</Button>
</Cluster>
```

**Accessibility**

- Radix Toolbar: Tab enters and leaves; ← → (↑ ↓ vertical) move between controls with a roving tabindex, wrapping; Home and End jump.
- Icon-only buttons (`hideLabel`) keep their label as the accessible name and show it in a tooltip on hover and focus.
- `pressed` makes a toggle (aria-pressed); `shortcut` shows in the tooltip and sets aria-keyshortcuts.

Stories: `components-toolbar--default`, `components-toolbar--toggles`, `components-toolbar--vertical`.
Composes: Icon, Kbd, Tooltip.
Tokens read: `color.bg.hover`, `color.bg.inverse`, `color.bg.selected`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.inverse`, `color.status.danger.fg`, `icon.stroke`, `radius.control`, `radius.indicator`, `shadow.popover`, `size.control.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.overlay-max`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.2xs`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.inset.xs`, `text.caption`, `text.code`, `text.label`, `z.tooltip`.

### Tooltip

component · `src/components/Tooltip/Tooltip.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Tooltip.usage.tsx`

Tooltip on hover and focus, dismissed with Escape. Behaviour from Radix Tooltip.

Props:
- `content: string`: Supplemental text. Never the only place essential information lives.
- `children: ReactElement`: A focusable element, typically a system Button. It keeps its own accessible name.
- `side?: 'top' | 'right' | 'bottom' | 'left'` = `'top'`
- `shortcut?: string`: The keyboard shortcut for the control, shown after the text ("Archive E") and set as the control's aria-keyshortcuts. It only shows the keys: register them with useShortcut.
- `open?: boolean`
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`
- `onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void`

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: side (top | right | bottom | left).
States: open, defaultOpen.

**When to use**

- Naming an icon-only control on hover and focus (with the same words as its `aria-label`).
- A short supplemental hint that nobody needs to complete the task.

**When not to use**

- Information people need → visible text: a field `description`, or `Text` on the page
- Interactive content such as links or buttons → a `Dialog` or the page itself

**Do:** The visible label stays; the tooltip adds a hint about when the action applies.

```tsx
<Cluster>
  <Tooltip content="Downloads every row that matches the filters">
    <Button variant="secondary" icon="download">
      Export CSV
    </Button>
  </Tooltip>
</Cluster>
```

**Don't:** The only explanation of a required format hidden in a tooltip: touch users never see it.

```tsx
<Cluster>
  <Tooltip content="Use the format AB-1234">
    <Button variant="ghost">Reference</Button>
  </Tooltip>
</Cluster>
```

**Accessibility**

- Opens on hover and keyboard focus, closes on Escape; the trigger keeps its own accessible name.
- Wrap a focusable element (a system Button): a tooltip on non-focusable content is unreachable by keyboard.

Stories: `components-tooltip--closed`, `components-tooltip--open`, `components-tooltip--open-bottom`, `components-tooltip--with-shortcut`.
Composes: Kbd.
Tokens read: `color.bg.inverse`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.inverse`, `radius.control`, `radius.indicator`, `shadow.popover`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.overlay-max`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.inset.2xs`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.inset.xs`, `text.caption`, `text.code`, `z.tooltip`.

## Primitives reference

### Box

primitive · `src/primitives/Box/Box.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Box.usage.tsx`

Padding around content, from the inset scale: the box inside a region that has no component of its own (a toolbar strip, a panel's body). A surface with a border and a heading is a Card.

Props:
- `children?: ReactNode`
- `as?: LayoutElement` = `'div'`: Semantic element to render. Defaults to div.
- `padding?: InsetToken` = `'md'`: Padding on every side. Token-typed: raw values are not accepted.
- `paddingBlock?: InsetToken`: Overrides `padding` on the block axis (top and bottom in horizontal writing).
- `paddingInline?: InsetToken`: Overrides `padding` on the inline axis (start and end).
- …plus the native attributes of `AriaAttributes`, `DOMAttributes`, `HTMLAttributes`.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: padding (2xs | xs | sm | md | lg | xl); paddingBlock (2xs | xs | sm | md | lg | xl); paddingInline (2xs | xs | sm | md | lg | xl).

**When to use**

- Padding inside a region that has no component of its own: a toolbar strip, a panel’s body, the inside of a custom slot.
- `padding` is an inset token; `paddingBlock` and `paddingInline` override one axis.

**When not to use**

- A surface with a border, a heading or actions → `Card` (its body already has padding)
- Space between siblings → the `gap` of a `Stack`, `Cluster` or `Grid`: the parent owns the space between
- Page gutters → `Center` with `gutters`

**Do:** A toolbar strip padded from the inset scale.

```tsx
<Box paddingBlock="xs" paddingInline="md">
  <Cluster gap="sm">
    <Text size="caption">3 selected</Text>
  </Cluster>
</Box>
```

**Don't:** A Box wrapped around a Card’s body: the padding doubles up.

```tsx
<Card>
  <CardHeader title="Billing" />
  <CardBody>
    <Box padding="lg">
      <Text>Next invoice on 1 April.</Text>
    </Box>
  </CardBody>
</Card>
```

**Accessibility**

- Layout only: no role. Choose `as` for the semantics (`section`, `aside`) and name it when it is a landmark.

Stories: `primitives-box--default`, `primitives-box--small`, `primitives-box--extra-large`, `primitives-box--axis-overrides`.
Tokens read: `space.inset.2xs`, `space.inset.lg`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.inset.xl`, `space.inset.xs`.

### Center

primitive · `src/primitives/Center/Center.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Center.usage.tsx`

Horizontally centred column with a bounded measure.

Props:
- `children?: ReactNode`
- `as?: LayoutElement` = `'div'`: Semantic element to render. Defaults to div.
- `max?: ContentWidthToken` = `'lg'`: Maximum measure of the content.
- `gutters?: InsetToken` = `'md'`: Minimum space on either side when the viewport is narrower than `max`.
- `intrinsic?: boolean` = `false`: Also centre children on the inline axis (empty states, short messages).
- …plus the native attributes of `AriaAttributes`, `DOMAttributes`, `HTMLAttributes`.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: max (xs | sm | md | lg); gutters (2xs | xs | sm | md | lg | xl).
States: intrinsic.

**When to use**

- The page column inside AppShell’s main: a bounded measure (`max`) with gutters.
- `intrinsic` to centre short content such as an empty state.

**When not to use**

- Centring one control in a row → `Cluster` with `justify="center"`
- A full-bleed work surface → the page content directly in main

**Do:** A readable measure for running text.

```tsx
<Center max="sm" gutters="sm">
  <Text>Records track agreements from draft to renewal, with their owner, amount and every change along the way.</Text>
</Center>
```

**Don't:** An intrinsic centre around a long paragraph: centred text is hard to read.

```tsx
<Center intrinsic>
  <EmptyState
    reason="first-use"
    headingLevel={4}
    title="About records"
    description="Records track agreements from draft to renewal, with their owner, amount and every change along the way, and can be exported."
  />
</Center>
```

**Accessibility**

- Layout only. Pass `as="main"` or `as="article"` only when that landmark isn’t already provided (AppShell provides main).

Stories: `primitives-center--default`, `primitives-center--intrinsic`, `primitives-center--wide-measure`.
Tokens read: `size.content.lg`, `size.content.md`, `size.content.sm`, `size.content.xs`, `space.inset.2xs`, `space.inset.lg`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.inset.xl`, `space.inset.xs`.

### Cluster

primitive · `src/primitives/Cluster/Cluster.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Cluster.usage.tsx`

Horizontal group that wraps gracefully: toolbars, button rows, tag lists.

Props:
- `children?: ReactNode`
- `as?: LayoutElement` = `'div'`: Semantic element to render. Defaults to div.
- `gap?: GapToken` = `'sm'`: Space between items, both axes.
- `justify?: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' | 'between'` = `'start'`: Main-axis distribution. `between` gives a two-zone "title left, actions right" bar.
- `align?: 'start' | 'center' | 'end' | 'baseline' | 'stretch'` = `'center'`: Cross-axis alignment.
- `wrap?: boolean` = `true`: Wrap onto new lines when space runs out. Defaults to true.
- …plus the native attributes of `AriaAttributes`, `DOMAttributes`, `HTMLAttributes`.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: gap (2xs | xs | sm | md | lg | xl | 2xl); justify (start | center | end | between); align (start | center | end | baseline | stretch).
States: wrap.

**When to use**

- A row that may wrap: buttons, filters, tags.
- `justify="between"` for a two-zone bar: title on the start side, actions on the end.

**When not to use**

- Items that must line up in columns across rows → `Grid` or `Table`
- Two regions of different weight, such as content and a rail → `Sidebar`

**Do:** A header bar: the title and its status on one side, the action on the other, wrapping on narrow screens.

```tsx
<Cluster justify="between">
  <Cluster gap="xs">
    <Heading level={4}>Hardware lease</Heading>
    <Badge tone="success">Approved</Badge>
  </Cluster>
  <Button variant="secondary">Edit</Button>
</Cluster>
```

**Don't:** Wrapping turned off for a long row: it overflows instead of reflowing.

```tsx
<Cluster wrap={false} gap="xs">
  <Button variant="secondary" size="sm">Status</Button>
  <Button variant="secondary" size="sm">Owner</Button>
  <Button variant="secondary" size="sm">Created</Button>
  <Button variant="secondary" size="sm">Amount</Button>
</Cluster>
```

**Accessibility**

- Layout only. DOM order is visual order, including after wrapping.
- For a list of items (tags, filters), render it as a list with `as="ul"`.

Stories: `primitives-cluster--default`, `primitives-cluster--justify-between`, `primitives-cluster--justify-end`, `primitives-cluster--gap-large`.
Tokens read: `space.gap.2xl`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.lg`, `space.gap.md`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xl`, `space.gap.xs`.

### Cover

primitive · `src/primitives/Cover/Cover.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Cover.usage.tsx`

Vertically centres its content in the available block size, with optional header and footer pinned to the edges. When the content is taller than the space, everything flows and scrolls.

Props:
- `children?: ReactNode`
- `as?: LayoutElement` = `'div'`: Semantic element to render. Defaults to div.
- `header?: ReactNode`: Pinned to the block start (a brand).
- `footer?: ReactNode`: Pinned to the block end (legal links).
- `minBlockSize?: 'fill' | 'viewport'` = `'fill'`: fill: at least the parent's block size (the parent must have one). viewport: at least the viewport's.
- `gap?: GapToken` = `'lg'`: Minimum space between the header, the centred content and the footer.
- …plus the native attributes of `AriaAttributes`, `DOMAttributes`, `HTMLAttributes`.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: minBlockSize (fill | viewport); gap (2xs | xs | sm | md | lg | xl | 2xl).

**When to use**

- Centring one block vertically in the space available, with an optional header and footer pinned to the edges: a sign-in card, a full-page message.
- `minBlockSize="viewport"` for a whole page; `"fill"` (default) inside a parent that has a block size.
- When the content is taller than the space, everything flows and scrolls; nothing is clipped.

**When not to use**

- A signed-out page → `AuthLayout`, which composes Cover with the brand, card and footer
- Centring horizontally with a bounded measure → `Center`
- An empty list or panel → `EmptyState` in the region it replaces

**Do:** One message centred in the space, with a header pinned above it.

```tsx
<Cover header={<Text tone="muted">Acme</Text>}>
  <Stack gap="xs" align="center">
    <Heading level={4}>You’re all set</Heading>
    <Button>Go to Home</Button>
  </Stack>
</Cover>
```

**Don't:** Several unrelated blocks in one Cover: only one thing can be the centre of attention.

```tsx
<Cover>
  <Stack gap="xs">
    <Heading level={4}>Recent records</Heading>
    <Heading level={4}>Usage this month</Heading>
    <Heading level={4}>Team</Heading>
  </Stack>
</Cover>
```

**Accessibility**

- Layout only: it adds no landmark. Pass landmark elements (`header`, `main`, `footer`) into its slots when it frames a whole page, as AuthLayout does.
- DOM order is header, content, footer, so reading order matches what is seen.

Stories: `primitives-cover--header-and-footer`, `primitives-cover--centred-only`, `primitives-cover--tight-gap`.
Tokens read: `size.viewport.block`, `space.gap.2xl`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.lg`, `space.gap.md`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xl`, `space.gap.xs`.

### Frame

primitive · `src/primitives/Frame/Frame.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Frame.usage.tsx`

Holds media (an img, video or iframe) to a fixed aspect ratio and crops it to fill, so a grid of thumbnails lines up whatever the source sizes. Other content is centred in the frame.

Props:
- `children?: ReactNode`
- `as?: LayoutElement` = `'div'`: Semantic element to render. Defaults to div.
- `ratio?: RatioToken` = `'landscape'`: Aspect ratio the media is held to.
- …plus the native attributes of `AriaAttributes`, `DOMAttributes`, `HTMLAttributes`.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: ratio (square | landscape | wide).

**When to use**

- Media that must keep one shape whatever its source size: file previews, cover images, video, logos.
- `ratio` is a token: `square` (avatars, logos), `landscape` (4:3, file previews), `wide` (16:9, video and covers). The media fills the frame and is cropped, never stretched.

**When not to use**

- A person’s picture → `Avatar`, which also falls back to initials
- Sizing a block that holds text → let the text set the height

**Do:** Previews held to one ratio, so the grid lines up; the name beside each is its text.

```tsx
<Grid min="sm" gap="sm">
  {['Site plan.png', 'Floor two.png'].map((name) => (
    <Stack gap="2xs" key={name}>
      <Frame ratio="landscape">
        <img src={preview} alt="" />
      </Frame>
      <Text size="caption">{name}</Text>
    </Stack>
  ))}
</Grid>
```

**Don't:** A bare image: a tall source makes a tall tile, and the grid breaks.

```tsx
<Grid min="sm" gap="sm">
  <img src={preview} alt="" />
  <Text size="caption">Site plan.png</Text>
</Grid>
```

**Accessibility**

- Layout only. The media keeps its own alternative: `alt=""` when a visible name sits beside it, a real description when it carries information.

Stories: `primitives-frame--landscape`, `primitives-frame--square`, `primitives-frame--wide`, `primitives-frame--centred-content`.
Tokens read: `ratio.landscape`, `ratio.square`, `ratio.wide`.

### Grid

primitive · `src/primitives/Grid/Grid.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Grid.usage.tsx`

Auto-fit card grid: as many equal columns as fit, each at least `min` wide.

Props:
- `children?: ReactNode`
- `as?: LayoutElement` = `'div'`: Semantic element to render. Defaults to div.
- `min?: GridItemToken` = `'md'`: Minimum item width. Columns are added or removed automatically, no breakpoints.
- `gap?: GapToken` = `'md'`: Space between cells.
- …plus the native attributes of `AriaAttributes`, `DOMAttributes`, `HTMLAttributes`.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: min (sm | md | lg); gap (2xs | xs | sm | md | lg | xl | 2xl).

**When to use**

- Equal items that reflow by available width with no breakpoints: cards, stat tiles, galleries.

**When not to use**

- Rows of comparable attributes → `Table`
- A main region and a narrow side region → `Sidebar`

**Do:** Tiles of equal importance, each at least the `min` width.

```tsx
<Grid min="sm" gap="sm">
  {STATS.map((s) => (
    <Card key={s}>
      <CardHeader title={s} level={4} />
    </Card>
  ))}
</Grid>
```

**Don't:** A grid of one: an item that isn’t part of a set is just content.

```tsx
<Grid min="lg">
  <Card>
    <CardHeader title="Notes" level={4} />
  </Card>
</Grid>
```

**Accessibility**

- Layout only. Items read in DOM order, row by row.
- For a set of like items, `as="ul"` exposes the count.

Stories: `primitives-grid--default`, `primitives-grid--small-items`, `primitives-grid--large-items`.
Tokens read: `size.grid-item.lg`, `size.grid-item.md`, `size.grid-item.sm`, `space.gap.2xl`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.lg`, `space.gap.md`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xl`, `space.gap.xs`.

### Imposter

primitive · `src/primitives/Imposter/Imposter.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Imposter.usage.tsx`

Positions an overlay over the centre of its container, not the viewport: a notice over a chart with no data, a prompt over a locked panel. The container is the Imposter itself, so no positioning CSS is needed. For anything that must take focus and block the page, use Dialog.

Props:
- `children?: ReactNode`: The content underneath: what the overlay sits over.
- `as?: LayoutElement` = `'div'`: Semantic element to render. Defaults to div.
- `overlay?: ReactNode`: What sits over the centre of the content: a notice, an upgrade prompt, a loading message.
- `contain?: boolean` = `true`: Keep the overlay inside the container, scrolling it if it is taller. Defaults to true.
- `overlayLabel?: string`: Names the overlay as a region and puts it in the tab order, so keyboard users can scroll it. Set it when a contained overlay can be taller than its container.
- `margin?: GapToken` = `'md'`: Least space between the overlay and the container's edges.
- `inertContent?: boolean` = `false`: Makes the content underneath inert (not focusable, hidden from assistive technology) while the overlay covers it. Set it whenever the overlay hides what is underneath.
- …plus the native attributes of `AriaAttributes`, `DOMAttributes`, `HTMLAttributes`.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: margin (2xs | xs | sm | md | lg | xl | 2xl).
States: contain, inertContent.

**When to use**

- An overlay that belongs to one region, not the page: a notice over a chart with no data, an upgrade prompt over a locked panel, “Loading…” over stale content.
- The Imposter is the container, so no positioning CSS is needed. `margin` keeps the overlay off the edges; `contain` (the default) keeps it inside and scrolls it if it is taller.
- Set `inertContent` whenever the overlay hides what is underneath, so focus and screen readers skip it.

**When not to use**

- Something that must take focus and block the page → `Dialog`
- A message that doesn’t cover anything → `Banner` above the region, or `EmptyState` in place of it

**Do:** The locked panel is inert under the prompt, so nobody tabs into controls they can’t see.

```tsx
<Imposter inertContent overlay={<Banner tone="info" announce={false}>Usage history is on the Business plan.</Banner>}>
  {usageRows}
</Imposter>
```

**Don't:** An overlay without `inertContent`: the meters underneath are still read out and focusable.

```tsx
<Card>
  <CardHeader title="Usage" level={3} />
  <CardBody>
    <Imposter overlay={<Text>Upgrade to see usage.</Text>}>{usageRows}</Imposter>
  </CardBody>
</Card>
```

**Accessibility**

- The overlay follows the content in DOM order and reading order.
- `inertContent` sets `inert` on the content underneath while an overlay is shown.
- A contained overlay that can be taller than its container needs `overlayLabel`: it becomes a named, focusable region so the keyboard can scroll it.

Stories: `primitives-imposter--default`, `primitives-imposter--wide-margin`, `primitives-imposter--contained`, `primitives-imposter--no-overlay`.
Tokens read: `space.gap.2xl`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.lg`, `space.gap.md`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xl`, `space.gap.xs`, `z.overlay`.

### Reel

primitive · `src/primitives/Reel/Reel.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Reel.usage.tsx`

A single row that scrolls sideways, snapping to the start of each item: a strip of cards, thumbnails or suggestions that would otherwise wrap. The row is a named region in the tab order, so it scrolls with the arrow keys even when its items aren't focusable.

Props:
- `children?: ReactNode`
- `label: string`: Accessible name of the scrolling region ("Recent files"). Required: the region takes keyboard focus.
- `gap?: GapToken` = `'md'`: Space between items.
- `itemWidth?: GridItemToken | 'auto'` = `'md'`: Width of each item. `auto` lets each item size itself.
- …plus the native attributes of `AriaAttributes`, `DOMAttributes`, `HTMLAttributes`.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: gap (2xs | xs | sm | md | lg | xl | 2xl); itemWidth (sm | md | lg | auto).

**When to use**

- A row of like items that is fine to scroll sideways: recent files, suggested templates, image thumbnails.
- `itemWidth` takes a grid-item token (or `auto`); items snap to their start as the row scrolls.
- `label` names the row: it is a region in the tab order, so arrow keys scroll it even when the items aren’t focusable.

**When not to use**

- Items people compare or must all see → `Grid`, which wraps
- Tabular data wider than the screen → `Table` (its own scroll region, with a sticky header)
- Primary navigation → `Nav` or `NavTabs`

**Do:** A named row of recent files; the cut-off card at the edge shows there is more.

```tsx
<Reel label="Recent files" itemWidth="sm">
  {files.map((name) => (
    <Card key={name}>
      <CardHeader title={name} level={3} />
    </Card>
  ))}
</Reel>
```

**Don't:** Every file in a grid when only the latest few matter: the page grows with the folder.

```tsx
<Grid min="sm" gap="sm">
  {files.map((name) => (
    <Card key={name}>
      <CardBody>
        <Text>{name}</Text>
      </CardBody>
    </Card>
  ))}
</Grid>
```

**Accessibility**

- A `region` named by `label` with `tabIndex=0`: keyboard users can focus it and scroll with the arrow keys (axe `scrollable-region-focusable`).
- Items are read in DOM order; snapping is `proximity`, never `mandatory`, so it never traps a scroll position.

Stories: `primitives-reel--default`, `primitives-reel--small-items`, `primitives-reel--large-items`, `primitives-reel--auto-width`, `primitives-reel--fits-without-scrolling`.
Tokens read: `size.grid-item.lg`, `size.grid-item.md`, `size.grid-item.sm`, `space.gap.2xl`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.lg`, `space.gap.md`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xl`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.xs`.

### Sidebar

primitive · `src/primitives/Sidebar/Sidebar.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Sidebar.usage.tsx`

Side region beside main content. When the content would drop below half the container, the two stack. No media query: it responds to its container.

Props:
- `children?: ReactNode`
- `as?: LayoutElement` = `'div'`: Semantic element to render. Defaults to div.
- `side: ReactNode`: Content of the narrow side region.
- `placement?: 'start' | 'end'` = `'start'`: Which edge the side region sits on. DOM order follows, so reading order matches.
- `sideWidth?: SidebarWidthToken` = `'md'`: Preferred width of the side region.
- `gap?: GapToken` = `'lg'`: Space between the regions.
- …plus the native attributes of `AriaAttributes`, `DOMAttributes`, `HTMLAttributes`.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: placement (start | end); sideWidth (sm | md | lg); gap (2xs | xs | sm | md | lg | xl | 2xl).

**When to use**

- A narrow region beside a wider one inside a card, panel or dialog, stacking when space runs out.
- `placement` sets the edge; DOM order follows, so reading order matches.

**When not to use**

- The app’s navigation → AppShell, which owns it and collapses it to a drawer
- A page’s properties rail or section sub-nav → `PageLayout`, which names the aside and places the nav
- Equal columns → `Grid`

**Do:** Main content first, a narrow region at the end that stacks below it when space runs out.

```tsx
<Sidebar
  placement="end"
  sideWidth="sm"
  gap="md"
  side={
    <Card>
      <CardHeader title="Properties" level={4} />
    </Card>
  }
>
  <Card>
    <CardBody>
      <Text>Activity, newest first.</Text>
    </CardBody>
  </Card>
</Sidebar>
```

**Don't:** The important content squeezed into the narrow side.

```tsx
<Sidebar
  sideWidth="sm"
  side={
    <Card>
      <CardBody>
        <Text>Activity, newest first, with every change to the record.</Text>
      </CardBody>
    </Card>
  }
>
  <Card>
    <CardHeader title="Owner" level={4} />
  </Card>
</Sidebar>
```

**Accessibility**

- Layout only: it adds no landmark. For a page’s nav or aside regions use `PageLayout`, which does.
- Stacks in DOM order on narrow containers, so nothing is lost at 400% zoom.

Stories: `primitives-sidebar--start`, `primitives-sidebar--end`, `primitives-sidebar--narrow-side`.
Tokens read: `size.sidebar.lg`, `size.sidebar.md`, `size.sidebar.sm`, `space.gap.2xl`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.lg`, `space.gap.md`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xl`, `space.gap.xs`.

### Stack

primitive · `src/primitives/Stack/Stack.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Stack.usage.tsx`

Vertical flow with consistent spacing. The parent owns the space between siblings.

Props:
- `children?: ReactNode`
- `as?: LayoutElement` = `'div'`: Semantic element to render. Defaults to div.
- `gap?: GapToken` = `'md'`: Space between children. Token-typed: raw values are not accepted.
- `align?: 'stretch' | 'start' | 'center' | 'end'` = `'stretch'`: Cross-axis alignment of children.
- …plus the native attributes of `AriaAttributes`, `DOMAttributes`, `HTMLAttributes`.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: gap (2xs | xs | sm | md | lg | xl | 2xl); align (stretch | start | center | end).

**When to use**

- Anything that flows top to bottom: page sections, form fields, a card body.
- Pick the `gap` from the scale; pass `as` for semantics (`section`, `form`, `ul`, `dl`).

**When not to use**

- Items side by side → `Cluster`
- Equal items that should reflow into columns → `Grid`

**Do:** One Stack owns the rhythm of the form; the fields bring no margins of their own.

```tsx
<Stack as="form" gap="md" align="start" aria-label="Invite">
  <TextField label="Name" />
  <TextField label="Email" type="email" />
  <Button type="submit">Send invite</Button>
</Stack>
```

**Don't:** Nested Stacks with mixed gaps for the same rhythm: spacing drifts field by field.

```tsx
<Stack gap="2xs" aria-label="Invite">
  <Stack gap="xl">
    <TextField label="Name" />
  </Stack>
  <TextField label="Email" type="email" />
</Stack>
```

**Accessibility**

- Layout only: it adds no roles. Use `as` so the element matches the content (a list is a `ul`).
- Visual order is DOM order, so reading and focus order stay aligned.

Stories: `primitives-stack--default`, `primitives-stack--gap-extra-small`, `primitives-stack--gap-extra-large`, `primitives-stack--align-center`.
Tokens read: `space.gap.2xl`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.lg`, `space.gap.md`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xl`, `space.gap.xs`.

### Switcher

primitive · `src/primitives/Switcher/Switcher.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/Switcher.usage.tsx`

A row of equal items that becomes a column, all at once, when its container is narrower than the threshold. No media query and no in-between wrap: one row or one column.

Props:
- `children?: ReactNode`
- `as?: LayoutElement` = `'div'`: Semantic element to render. Defaults to div.
- `threshold?: ContentWidthToken` = `'sm'`: Container width below which every child stacks. Above it they all sit in one row, equal width.
- `gap?: GapToken` = `'md'`: Space between children, both directions.
- …plus the native attributes of `AriaAttributes`, `DOMAttributes`, `HTMLAttributes`.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: threshold (xs | sm | md | lg); gap (2xs | xs | sm | md | lg | xl | 2xl).

**When to use**

- Equal items that should sit in one row when there is room and one column when there isn’t, with nothing in between: stat tiles, plan cards, a two- or three-part form row.
- `threshold` is a content-width token: below it (of the container’s width, not the viewport’s), every child stacks.

**When not to use**

- Many items that should reflow into as many columns as fit → `Grid`
- Buttons or tags that wrap naturally → `Cluster`
- Two regions of different weight → `PageLayout` or `Sidebar`

**Do:** Stats in one row, which becomes one column all at once when narrow.

```tsx
<Switcher threshold="xs">
  <Stat label="Records created" value="86" />
  <Stat label="Pending approvals" value="9" />
  <Stat label="Overdue records" value="14" />
</Switcher>
```

**Don't:** Stats in a wrapping Cluster: at in-between widths two sit on one row and the third alone below, at a different width.

```tsx
<Cluster gap="md">
  <Stat label="Records created" value="86" />
  <Stat label="Pending approvals" value="9" />
  <Stat label="Overdue records" value="14" />
</Cluster>
```

**Accessibility**

- Layout only: it adds no landmark, and children stay in DOM order in both arrangements, so reading and focus order never change.
- Responds to its container, so it also stacks at high zoom.

Stories: `primitives-switcher--row`, `primitives-switcher--column-when-narrow`, `primitives-switcher--low-threshold-stays-a-row`.
