Tokens read: `size.content.lg`, `size.content.md`, `size.content.sm`, `size.content.xs`, `space.gap.2xl`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.lg`, `space.gap.md`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xl`, `space.gap.xs`.

### VisuallyHidden

primitive · `src/primitives/VisuallyHidden/VisuallyHidden.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/VisuallyHidden.usage.tsx`

Content that screen readers announce but the screen doesn't show: a heading for a region whose purpose is visually obvious, the words behind a symbol. Clipped, not display:none, so it stays in the accessibility tree. It has no escape hatch: there is nothing on it to style.

Props:
- `children: ReactNode`: Text for assistive technology only.
- `as?: 'span' | 'div'` = `'span'`: span (the default) inside inline content; div around block content such as a heading.
- `id?: string`

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`.

Variants: as (span | div).

**When to use**

- Words a screen reader needs that sighted people get from layout: a heading for a region whose purpose is visually obvious, “up” behind a ▲.
- Use `as="div"` around block content such as a heading; the default `span` sits inside text.

**When not to use**

- Naming a control → its own `label` or `aria-label` (every system control takes one)
- Hiding content from everyone → don’t render it, or use the `hidden` attribute
- Anything sighted users also need → visible text

**Do:** The arrow is hidden from screen readers and the word is hidden from the screen, so both read “up 12%”.

```tsx
<Text>
  <span aria-hidden="true">▲</span> <VisuallyHidden>up</VisuallyHidden> 12%
</Text>
```

**Don't:** Instructions only screen readers get: sighted keyboard users miss them too.

```tsx
<Text>
  Reference <VisuallyHidden>use the format AB-1234</VisuallyHidden>
</Text>
```

**Accessibility**

- Clipped to 1px rather than `display: none`, so it stays in the accessibility tree and is announced.
- Not focusable. For a skip link, use AppShell’s, which shows on focus.

Stories: `primitives-visuallyhidden--inline-text`, `primitives-visuallyhidden--block-heading`.
Tokens read: none.

## Layouts reference

### AppShell

layout · `src/layouts/AppShell/AppShell.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/AppShell.usage.tsx`

The app frame every signed-in page renders inside: skip link, sidebar (brand + nav), header (breadcrumbs, actions, account menu) and main. Pages fill its slots; they never rebuild the frame. The toast region is mounted here, once. Wide: a toggle at the foot of the sidebar collapses it to an icon rail (labels move into tooltips; accessible names stay). The choice is remembered in localStorage. Below the size.breakpoint.md container width the sidebar is replaced by a Menu button that opens the nav in a Drawer from the inline start: scrim, focus trap, Escape, focus return.

Props:
- `brand: ReactNode`: Product name or mark at the top of the sidebar.
- `nav: ReactNode`: Primary navigation: a <Nav label="Main">. It renders its own labelled nav landmark.
- `breadcrumbs?: ReactNode`: Page trail in the header: <Breadcrumbs>. Omit on top-level pages.
- `actions?: ReactNode`: Global actions in the header (search, one global create). Never page navigation.
- `help?: ReactNode`: Help, in the same place on every page (WCAG 2.2 SC 3.2.6 Consistent Help): a Help menu with self-help and a way to contact a person. Rendered in the header, after the global actions and right before the account menu. Pass it from the app's one shell composition, never per page.
- `userMenu?: ReactNode`: Account menu, anchored at the header's inline end: <Menu trigger={…Avatar…}>.
- `children: ReactNode`: The page. Rendered inside <main>, the only region that scrolls.
- `assistant?: ReactNode`: An assistant beside the page: an <AssistantPanel>. Wide, it is a column at main's inline end, under the header, and main keeps scrolling on its own; narrow, it gives way to a launcher in the header that opens the panel in a Drawer. Omit it and the frame is unchanged.
- `footer?: ReactNode`: Page action bar (a long form's Cancel · Save). Sticks to the bottom of main while the page scrolls. A submit button here reaches its form with the form="<form id>" attribute.
- `skipLinkLabel?: string` = `'Skip to content'`: First focusable element; jumps past the sidebar and header to main.
- `menuLabel?: string` = `'Menu'`: Label of the button that opens the navigation drawer when the shell is too narrow to show the sidebar; also the drawer's name.
- `defaultNavOpen?: boolean` = `false`: Start with the narrow-screen navigation drawer open (gallery and tests).
- `sidebarCollapsed?: boolean`: Controlled: the wide-screen sidebar is collapsed to an icon rail. Pair with onSidebarCollapsedChange. A controlled shell does not write to storage; the owner does.
- `defaultSidebarCollapsed?: boolean` = `false`: Uncontrolled starting state, used when nothing is remembered yet.
- `onSidebarCollapsedChange?: (collapsed: boolean) => void`
- `sidebarStorageKey?: string | null` = `DEFAULT_STORAGE_KEY`: localStorage key under which the uncontrolled collapsed state is remembered across visits. null turns remembering off (gallery and tests).
- `collapseSidebarLabel?: string` = `'Collapse sidebar'`: Accessible name and tooltip of the rail toggle while the sidebar is expanded.
- `expandSidebarLabel?: string` = `'Expand sidebar'`: Accessible name and tooltip of the rail toggle while the sidebar is collapsed.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).
States: defaultNavOpen, sidebarCollapsed, defaultSidebarCollapsed.

**When to use**

- Every signed-in page. Define the composition once for the app (brand, nav, account menu); pages pass where they are and their content.
- Fill the slots: `breadcrumbs`, `actions` (global only), `help`, `userMenu`, `children` (the page), `footer` (a long form’s action bar).
- Pass `help` (a Help menu: self-help plus a way to reach a person) from the app’s one shell composition, so it sits in the same place on every page.
- An assistant beside the page goes in `assistant` (an `AssistantPanel`): a resizable column at main’s inline end, a launcher in the header when narrow.
- People can collapse the wide sidebar to an icon rail; the shell remembers it in localStorage under `sidebarStorageKey`. Give every primary nav item an `icon` so the rail reads well.

**When not to use**

- Sign-in, sign-up and other signed-out pages → a centred card without the shell
- A page needs different chrome → a proposal to extend AppShell; never a second frame

**Do:** The page fills main and uses the slots; the frame is untouched.

```tsx
<AppShell brand="Acme" nav={nav('Main (do example)')} breadcrumbs={<Breadcrumbs label="Breadcrumb (do example)" items={[{ label: 'Home', href: '/home' }]} current="Records" />} skipLinkLabel="Skip to content (do example)">
  <Center max="lg" gutters="md">
    <Stack gap="sm">
      <Heading level={3}>Records</Heading>
      <Text tone="muted">Only this region scrolls.</Text>
    </Stack>
  </Center>
</AppShell>
```

**Don't:** A page that rebuilds its own header and actions inside main: two headers, and page actions where global ones belong.

```tsx
<AppShell brand="Acme" nav={nav('Main (don’t example)')} actions={<Button>Save record</Button>} skipLinkLabel="Skip to content (don’t example)">
  <Center max="lg" gutters="md">
    <Stack gap="sm">
      <Heading level={3}>Acme · Records</Heading>
      <Text tone="muted">A second title bar, typed again on every page.</Text>
    </Stack>
  </Center>
</AppShell>
```

**Accessibility**

- Provides the skip link, banner, navigation and main landmarks; `main` is the only scrolling region.
- The collapsed sidebar opens as a drawer that traps focus and returns it to the Menu button.
- The rail toggle has an accessible name that says what it will do, `aria-expanded` and a matching tooltip. In the rail, labels move into tooltips but stay each link’s accessible name.
- Product code owns the page’s h1 and moving focus to it after client-side navigation.
- The `help` slot always renders after the global actions and right before the account menu, the same relative order on every page (WCAG 2.2 SC 3.2.6 Consistent Help). The WCAG 2.2 checks fail an example page that renders the shell without it.
- A sticky `footer` reserves `space.scroll-padding.end` in main, so a field that gets focus scrolls clear of the bar instead of under it (SC 2.4.11).

Stories: `layouts-appshell--default`, `layouts-appshell--sidebar-collapsed`, `layouts-appshell--without-breadcrumbs`, `layouts-appshell--with-global-action`, `layouts-appshell--with-help`, `layouts-appshell--with-action-bar`, `layouts-appshell--with-assistant`, `layouts-appshell--user-menu-open`, `layouts-appshell--narrow-collapsed`, `layouts-appshell--narrow-nav-open`.
Composes: Button, Drawer, Icon, Kbd, Link, Nav, Spinner, Toast, Tooltip.
Tokens read: `button.danger.bg`, `button.danger.bg-hover`, `button.danger.fg`, `button.ghost.bg-hover`, `button.ghost.fg`, `button.primary.bg`, `button.primary.bg-hover`, `button.primary.fg`, `button.secondary.bg`, `button.secondary.bg-hover`, `button.secondary.border`, `button.secondary.fg`, `color.action.primary`, `color.bg.canvas`, `color.bg.elevated`, `color.bg.hover`, `color.bg.inverse`, `color.bg.scrim`, `color.bg.selected`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.border.strong`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.inverse`, `color.fg.link`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.status.danger.fg`, `color.status.info.fg`, `color.status.neutral.fg`, `color.status.success.fg`, `color.status.warning.fg`, `ease.linear`, `ease.standard`, `focus.ring.offset`, `focus.ring.width`, `font.weight.strong`, `icon.stroke`, `motion.fast`, `motion.spin`, `radius.control`, `radius.indicator`, `radius.pill`, `radius.surface`, `shadow.modal`, `shadow.popover`, `size.control.lg`, `size.control.md`, `size.control.sm`, `size.drawer.md`, `size.drawer.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.overlay-max`, `size.rail`, `size.sidebar.md`, `size.target-min`, `size.viewport.block`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.lg`, `space.gap.md`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.2xs`, `space.inset.lg`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.inset.xs`, `space.scroll-padding.end`, `text.body`, `text.body-lg`, `text.caption`, `text.code`, `text.heading-3`, `text.heading-4`, `text.label`, `z.modal`, `z.overlay`, `z.sticky`, `z.toast`, `z.tooltip`.

### AssistantPanel

layout · `src/layouts/AssistantPanel/AssistantPanel.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/AssistantPanel.usage.tsx`

The assistant beside the page, in AppShell's `assistant` slot. Wide, it is a panel at the inline end that the person resizes (drag the edge, arrow keys on it, or Widen / Narrow) and closes to a launcher; the width is remembered. Narrow, it gives way to a launcher in the header that opens the same content in a Drawer. The content is mounted in one place at a time.

Props:
- `title: string`: The assistant's name: the panel's landmark name and heading, the drawer's title ("Assistant"). Required.
- `children: ReactNode`: The conversation: a ChatThread over a Composer, laid out to fill the panel.
- `open?: boolean`: Controlled: the panel is open beside the page (wide) or in its drawer (narrow).
- `defaultOpen?: boolean` = `true`: Uncontrolled starting state.
- `onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void`
- `launcherLabel?: string` = `title`: Label of the button that opens it (a launcher at the edge when wide, in the header when narrow).
- `actions?: ReactNode`: Actions in the panel's header, before Close: New chat, a History menu.
- `storageKey?: string | null` = `DEFAULT_STORAGE_KEY`: localStorage key under which the width a person chose is remembered across visits. null turns remembering off (gallery and tests).
- `resizeLabel?: string` = `'Resize ${title.toLowerCase()} panel'`: Accessible name of the resize handle.
- `closeLabel?: string` = `'Close'`
- `defaultDrawerOpen?: boolean` = `false`: Start with the narrow-screen drawer open (gallery and tests).

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).
States: open, defaultOpen, defaultDrawerOpen.

**When to use**

- An assistant that works beside the page it’s about (a record’s copilot): pass it as AppShell’s `assistant`, with a `ChatThread` over a `Composer` as its content.
- People resize it (drag the edge, arrow keys on the edge, or Widen / Narrow) and close it to a launcher; the width is remembered under `storageKey`.
- Below `size.breakpoint.md` it becomes a launcher in the header that opens the same content in a `Drawer`. Keep the conversation’s state in the page, not in the panel: the content moves between the two.

**When not to use**

- A conversation that is the page → a full chat page (the Assistant chat example) inside `AppShell`
- One AI suggestion inside a form → `Suggestion` beside the field
- Details or filters for the page → `Drawer` or `PageLayout`’s aside

**Do:** A thread over a composer, filling the panel; the page stays usable beside it.

```tsx
<AssistantPanel title="Assistant (do example)" storageKey={null}>
  <ChatThread label="Conversation (do example)" empty={<Text tone="muted">Ask about this record.</Text>} />
  <Composer label="Ask (do example)" onSend={() => undefined} />
</AssistantPanel>
```

**Don't:** A modal drawer for the assistant on a wide screen: it covers the page the answers are about.

```tsx
<Drawer title="Assistant (don’t example)" trigger={<Button variant="secondary">Ask AI</Button>} />
```

**Accessibility**

- The panel is a complementary landmark named by its heading. Opening it moves focus into it; closing it returns focus to the launcher.
- The resize edge is a focusable separator with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax` (CSS pixels); arrow keys resize it (Shift for bigger steps), Home and End jump to the limits. Widen / Narrow is the single-pointer alternative to dragging (WCAG 2.5.7).
- Narrow, the Drawer brings its focus trap, Escape and focus return.

Stories: `layouts-assistantpanel--open`, `layouts-assistantpanel--closed`, `layouts-assistantpanel--with-header-actions`, `layouts-assistantpanel--narrow`, `layouts-assistantpanel--narrow-open`.
Composes: Button, Drawer, Icon, Spinner.
Tokens read: `button.danger.bg`, `button.danger.bg-hover`, `button.danger.fg`, `button.ghost.bg-hover`, `button.ghost.fg`, `button.primary.bg`, `button.primary.bg-hover`, `button.primary.fg`, `button.secondary.bg`, `button.secondary.bg-hover`, `button.secondary.border`, `button.secondary.fg`, `color.bg.elevated`, `color.bg.hover`, `color.bg.scrim`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.focus`, `ease.linear`, `ease.standard`, `focus.ring.width`, `icon.stroke`, `motion.fast`, `motion.spin`, `radius.control`, `radius.pill`, `shadow.modal`, `size.assistant.default`, `size.assistant.max`, `size.assistant.min`, `size.control.lg`, `size.control.md`, `size.control.sm`, `size.drawer.md`, `size.drawer.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.target-min`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.md`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.lg`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.inset.xs`, `space.scroll-padding.end`, `text.body`, `text.body-lg`, `text.heading-3`, `text.heading-4`, `text.label`, `z.modal`, `z.sticky`.

### AuthLayout

layout · `src/layouts/AuthLayout/AuthLayout.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/AuthLayout.usage.tsx`

The frame for signed-out pages (sign-in, sign-up, password reset, an error before the app can load): a brand, one centred card on a plain surface, and a footer. No navigation, no shell.

Props:
- `brand: ReactNode`: Product name or mark, above the card.
- `children: ReactNode`: The card's content: the page's h1 first (a Heading at level 1), then the form.
- `footer?: ReactNode`: Links under the card: privacy, terms, help.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

**When to use**

- Every signed-out page: sign-in, sign-up, password reset, an emailed-link landing, a verification code step.
- An error page shown when the app itself may have failed to load, so the shell can’t be relied on.
- The card holds the page’s h1 first (a `Heading` at level 1), then one form; copy the Sign in example.

**When not to use**

- A signed-in page, including a signed-in 404 → `AppShell`, so navigation stays
- A multi-step setup after sign-in → `FocusedLayout`

**Do:** Brand above, one card with the h1 and the way in, legal links below.

```tsx
<AuthLayout brand="Acme" footer={<Text size="caption">Privacy · Terms</Text>}>
  <Stack gap="2xs">
    <Heading level={1} size={3}>
      Sign in to Acme
    </Heading>
    <Text tone="muted">Use your work account.</Text>
  </Stack>
  <Button>Continue with SSO</Button>
</AuthLayout>
```

**Don't:** Sign-in inside the app shell: navigation to pages the person can’t open yet, and a frame that implies they’re signed in.

```tsx
<AppShell
  brand="Acme"
  nav={<Nav label="Main (don’t example)" sections={[{ items: [{ label: 'Home', href: '/home', icon: 'home' }] }]} />}
  skipLinkLabel="Skip to content (don’t example)"
  sidebarStorageKey={null}
>
  <Button>Continue with SSO</Button>
</AppShell>
```

**Accessibility**

- Provides banner (brand), main (the card) and contentinfo (footer) landmarks; the page supplies the one h1 inside the card.
- The card never exceeds `size.content.xs` and reflows at 400% zoom; the page scrolls when the card is taller than the viewport.

Stories: `layouts-authlayout--default`, `layouts-authlayout--with-footer`, `layouts-authlayout--narrow`.
Composes: Cover.
Tokens read: `color.bg.canvas`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.muted`, `radius.surface`, `shadow.card`, `size.content.xs`, `size.viewport.block`, `space.gap.2xl`, `space.gap.2xs`, `space.gap.lg`, `space.gap.md`, `space.gap.sm`, `space.gap.xl`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.lg`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.xl`, `text.caption`, `text.heading-3`.

### FocusedLayout

layout · `src/layouts/FocusedLayout/FocusedLayout.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/FocusedLayout.usage.tsx`

The frame for a focused, multi-step task (a setup wizard, a multi-step create): no sidebar, a header with the task and a way out, one centred column, and a sticky action bar. Only main scrolls.

Props:
- `brand: ReactNode`: Product name or mark at the header's inline start.
- `task: string`: The task, in the header ("Set up your workspace"). Plain text: the page's h1 is the step's PageHeader.
- `exit: ReactNode`: The way out, at the header's inline end: a ghost Button or a Link ("Exit setup"). Required: a focused task never traps.
- `progress?: ReactNode`: A Progress bar under the header, across the column.
- `children: ReactNode`: The content column: Stepper, PageHeader, the step's form.
- `footer?: ReactNode`: Action bar (Back · Next). Sticks to the bottom of main while the step scrolls.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

**When to use**

- A task that takes over the screen until it is done or abandoned: first-run setup, a multi-step create, a checkout.
- The header names the task (plain text) and always offers `exit`; the column holds a `Stepper`, the step’s `PageHeader` and its form; `footer` holds Back · Next.
- Copy the Setup wizard example.

**When not to use**

- Everyday pages → `AppShell`
- Signed-out pages → `AuthLayout`
- A single-page form → `AppShell` with its `footer` action bar (the Create and edit example)

**Do:** The task and a way out in the header; one column; the step actions in a sticky bar.

```tsx
<FocusedLayout
  brand="Acme"
  task="Set up your workspace"
  exit={<Button variant="ghost">Exit setup</Button>}
  footer={
    <Cluster justify="end">
      <Button>Next</Button>
    </Cluster>
  }
>
  <Stepper label="Setup steps (do example)" steps={steps} current={0} />
  <PageHeader title="Name your workspace" />
</FocusedLayout>
```

**Don't:** A wizard inside the app shell: the full navigation invites people to leave half-way, and nothing says how to exit safely.

```tsx
<AppShell
  brand="Acme"
  nav={<Nav label="Main (don’t example)" sections={[{ items: [{ label: 'Home', href: '/home', icon: 'home' }] }]} />}
  skipLinkLabel="Skip to content (don’t example)"
  sidebarStorageKey={null}
>
  <Text>Step 1 of 3: Name your workspace</Text>
</AppShell>
```

**Accessibility**

- Provides banner (the header) and main landmarks; the step’s `PageHeader` is the page’s h1, and the task name in the header is not a heading.
- The exit is required, so a focused task never traps anyone.
- On a step change, move focus to the new step’s h1 (`PageHeader`’s `headingRef`), as the example does.

Stories: `layouts-focusedlayout--default`, `layouts-focusedlayout--with-action-bar`, `layouts-focusedlayout--with-progress`, `layouts-focusedlayout--narrow`.
Tokens read: `color.bg.canvas`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.fg.default`, `color.fg.muted`, `size.content.sm`, `size.control.lg`, `size.viewport.block`, `space.gap.lg`, `space.gap.md`, `space.gap.xl`, `space.inset.lg`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.scroll-padding.end`, `text.heading-4`, `text.label`, `z.sticky`.

### PageLayout

layout · `src/layouts/PageLayout/PageLayout.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/PageLayout.usage.tsx`

The regions of a page's body, below its PageHeader: an optional section nav at the inline start, the main column, and an optional aside at the inline end. When the container is narrower than size.breakpoint.sm the regions stack in reading order: nav, main, aside.

Props:
- `aside?: ReactNode`: Complementary content at the inline end: a record's properties rail. Rendered as <aside>.
- `asideLabel?: string`: Accessible name of the aside landmark ("Properties"). Required with `aside`.
- `children: ReactNode`: The page's main column. A plain region: AppShell's <main> already contains it.
- `nav?: ReactNode`: Section navigation at the inline start: a <Nav label="…"> (a settings sub-nav). Nav renders its own labelled nav landmark, so this slot adds no landmark of its own.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

**When to use**

- The body of a page below its `PageHeader`, when the page has a second region: a record’s properties rail (`aside`) or a section sub-nav (`nav`).
- `aside` is complementary content at the inline end, rendered as `<aside>` and named by the required `asideLabel`.
- `nav` is section navigation at the inline start. Pass a `<Nav label="…">`: it is a nav landmark, not an aside, so the slot adds no landmark of its own.
- Below the `size.breakpoint.sm` container width the regions stack in reading order: nav, main, aside.

**When not to use**

- A page with one column → the page’s `Center` column and a `Stack`, with no PageLayout
- The app’s primary navigation → AppShell’s `nav` slot
- Two regions inside a card or a panel → the `Sidebar` primitive

**Do:** Main content first; the properties rail is a named aside at the inline end.

```tsx
<PageLayout
  aside={
    <Card>
      <CardHeader title="Properties" level={4} />
    </Card>
  }
  asideLabel="Properties (do example)"
>
  <Card>
    <CardBody>
      <Text>Summary, activity and files.</Text>
    </CardBody>
  </Card>
</PageLayout>
```

**Don't:** A sub-nav hand-placed with Sidebar and wrapped in an aside: navigation announced as complementary content, and a gap and width of its own.

```tsx
<Sidebar
  as="aside"
  sideWidth="sm"
  side={<Nav label="Settings (don’t example)" sections={[{ items: [{ label: 'Profile', href: '/settings/profile' }] }]} />}
>
  <Card>
    <CardBody>
      <Text>Profile fields.</Text>
    </CardBody>
  </Card>
</Sidebar>
```

**Accessibility**

- The aside is a complementary landmark, and `asideLabel` is required whenever `aside` is set (a type error otherwise).
- The nav slot relies on `Nav`’s own labelled nav landmark; nothing is nested or duplicated.
- The main column is a plain region: the page is already inside AppShell’s `main`.
- Regions stack in DOM order when narrow, so reading and focus order never change with width, and nothing is lost at 400% zoom.

Stories: `layouts-pagelayout--main-only`, `layouts-pagelayout--with-aside`, `layouts-pagelayout--with-nav`, `layouts-pagelayout--nav-and-aside`, `layouts-pagelayout--narrow-stacked`.
Tokens read: `size.sidebar.lg`, `size.sidebar.sm`, `space.gap.lg`.

### SplitView

layout · `src/layouts/SplitView/SplitView.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/SplitView.usage.tsx`

A list and the selected item side by side (an inbox, a queue, a file browser), each pane scrolling on its own. The divider resizes the list: drag it, focus it and use ← → (Home and End for the limits), or click it to step through preset widths. Below the size.breakpoint.sm container width it collapses to one pane, the one `show` names, with a Back button above the detail. It lays out; the page owns selection and what the panes hold.

Props:
- `list: ReactNode`: The list: rows to move through.
- `detail: ReactNode`: The selected item, beside the list.
- `listLabel: string`: Accessible names of the two regions ("Conversations", "Conversation"). Required.
- `detailLabel: string`
- `show?: 'list' | 'detail'` = `'list'`: On a narrow container only one pane fits: which one shows. Wide containers always show both. Show the detail once something is opened, the list again on Back.
- `onBack?: () => void`: Narrow only: the Back button above the detail. Omit onBack to leave it out.
- `backLabel?: string` = `'Back'`
- `listSize?: number`: The list pane's width in percent (25–65). Uncontrolled default 40.
- `defaultListSize?: number` = `40`
- `onListSizeChange?: (size: number) => void`
- `resizeLabel?: string` = `'Resize list'`: Accessible name of the divider.

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`; `UNSAFE_className`/`UNSAFE_style` escape hatches (need a reasoned lint disable).

Variants: show (list | detail).

**When to use**

- Working through a list one item at a time without losing your place: an inbox, a review queue, support tickets, a file browser.
- When people move between neighbouring items often (j and k), so opening each on its own page would cost a round trip.

**When not to use**

- A list people scan and filter, then open one thing → the list page (`ListPage`) and a record page
- A record with properties beside it → `PageLayout` with an aside

**Do:** Both regions named; the page keeps the selection (in the URL) and passes `show` for narrow screens.

```tsx
<SplitView
  listLabel="Conversations"
  detailLabel="Conversation"
  list={<Text>Northwind renewal · Contoso invoice · …</Text>}
  detail={<Text>Northwind renewal: the conversation.</Text>}
/>
```

**Don't:** Two boxes side by side by hand: no resizing, no keyboard, and on a phone both squeeze into half a screen.

```tsx
<Box padding="md">
  <Text>List | Detail</Text>
</Box>
```

**Accessibility**

- Each pane is a named region and scrolls on its own, with the scroll-padding tokens so focus is never hidden at its edges.
- The divider is a focusable separator (aria-valuenow is the list’s width in percent): ← → resize by 5%, Home and End go to the limits; a click steps through preset widths, the single-pointer alternative to dragging (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.7).
- Below the sm breakpoint it collapses to one pane; `onBack` adds a Back button above the detail. Move focus into the detail when it opens, and back to the row on Back.

Stories: `layouts-splitview--default`, `layouts-splitview--wide-list`, `layouts-splitview--narrow-list`, `layouts-splitview--narrow-detail`.
Composes: Button, Icon, Spinner.
Tokens read: `button.danger.bg`, `button.danger.bg-hover`, `button.danger.fg`, `button.ghost.bg-hover`, `button.ghost.fg`, `button.primary.bg`, `button.primary.bg-hover`, `button.primary.fg`, `button.secondary.bg`, `button.secondary.bg-hover`, `button.secondary.border`, `button.secondary.fg`, `color.bg.subtle`, `color.bg.surface`, `color.border.default`, `color.fg.disabled`, `color.fg.muted`, `color.focus`, `ease.linear`, `ease.standard`, `focus.ring.width`, `icon.stroke`, `motion.fast`, `motion.spin`, `radius.control`, `radius.pill`, `radius.surface`, `size.control.lg`, `size.control.md`, `size.control.sm`, `size.icon.md`, `size.icon.sm`, `size.scroll-region.lg`, `size.sidebar.lg`, `size.target-min`, `space.gap.xs`, `space.inset.lg`, `space.inset.md`, `space.inset.sm`, `space.inset.xs`, `space.scroll-padding.end`, `space.scroll-padding.start`, `text.body-lg`, `text.label`.

## Utilities reference

### LocaleProvider

utility · `src/format/LocaleProvider.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/LocaleProvider.usage.tsx`

Sets the locale and time zone every system and app format reads. Wrap the app once, near the root, with the signed-in user's settings. The formatting locale is separate from the UI language: an English UI can format German dates.

Props:
- `locale?: string` = `DEFAULT_LOCALE`: BCP 47 locale for formatting, from the user's profile (defaulting from the browser).
- `timeZone?: string` = `DEFAULT_TIME_ZONE`: IANA time zone, from the user's profile. Travelling users and shared screens break auto-detection.
- `children: ReactNode`

Closed styling API: no `className`/`style`.

**When to use**

- Wrap the app once, near the root, with the signed-in user’s locale and time zone (a profile setting that defaults from the browser).
- Format every number, date, amount, list and file size a person reads with `useFormat()`: `format.money(minor, currency)`, `format.date(iso)`, `format.relative(iso)`. One named format per concept keeps every screen consistent.
- Money arrives as integer minor units plus an ISO 4217 code. Format the account’s currency in the reader’s locale: a German reader billed in USD sees `12.500,50 $`.
- An ISO date with no time (`2026-09-30`) is a calendar date and never shifts by zone; a timestamp is an instant, shown in the provider’s time zone.
- Outside React (tests, exports), `createFormatter({ locale, timeZone })` gives the same formats.
- Turning typed money into minor units: multiply by `10 ** currencyDigits(code)` (2 for USD, 0 for JPY, 3 for BHD) and round.

**When not to use**

- Dates and numbers in APIs, exports and logs → ISO 8601 and plain numbers; format only for people
- Translating UI copy → the app’s message catalogue; formatting locale and UI language are separate settings
- A one-off `Intl.NumberFormat` or `toFixed` in a page → a named format here, or a new one added to it

**Do:** The value is formatted by the provider: the reader’s separators, the account’s currency.

```tsx
<LocaleProvider locale="de-DE" timeZone="Europe/Berlin">
  <Balance />
</LocaleProvider>
```

**Don't:** A hand-built string: US separators and a “$” for every reader, whatever the currency.

```tsx
<Text>{`$${(1200000).toFixed(2)}`}</Text>
```

**Accessibility**

- Locale formats are what screen readers expect: “12.5%” and “Sep 12, 2026” are read naturally; “12.5 pct” and “09/12/26” are not.
- Prefer month names over numeric dates in the UI: `03/04/2026` means different days in different regions.
- Show relative times (“3 days ago”) with the absolute date nearby or on hover when precision matters.
- Numbers in tables still need `numeric` cells, so digits line up in every locale.

Stories: `utilities-localeprovider--english-us`, `utilities-localeprovider--german`, `utilities-localeprovider--japanese`, `utilities-localeprovider--arabic-egypt`.

### createFormatter

utility · `src/format/format.ts` · usage: `docs/usage/LocaleProvider.usage.tsx`

Formats for one locale and time zone. Prefer `useFormat()` inside React; this is for tests and non-React code.
Signature: `({ locale, timeZone }: LocaleSettings) => Formatter`

### currencyDigits

utility · `src/format/format.ts` · usage: `docs/usage/LocaleProvider.usage.tsx`

Decimal places a currency's minor unit has: USD 2, JPY 0, BHD 3.
Signature: `(currency: string) => number`

### useFormat

utility · `src/format/LocaleProvider.tsx` · usage: `docs/usage/LocaleProvider.usage.tsx`

The named formats for the current locale and time zone: `format.money(minor, 'USD')`, `format.date(iso)`.
Signature: `() => Formatter`

### vars

utility · `src/tokens/tokens.ts`

Semantic and component tokens as var() references, for inline custom properties in system code (vars.space.gap.md). Primitives are deliberately absent: nothing outside the token source reads them.

## Types

- `AccordionItem` (`src/components/Accordion/Accordion.tsx`): `interface AccordionItem { value: string; title: string; meta?: ReactNode; content: ReactNode; disabled?: boolean; }`
- `ActiveShortcut` (`src/components/Shortcuts/registry.ts`): `interface ActiveShortcut { id: string; keys: string; description: string; scope: string; characterKey: boolean; }` A registered shortcut, as the help overlay and the palette read it.
- `AvatarSize` (`src/components/Avatar/Avatar.tsx`): `type AvatarSize = 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'`
- `BadgeTone` (`src/components/Badge/Badge.tsx`): `type BadgeTone = 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' | 'neutral'`
- `BannerTone` (`src/components/Banner/Banner.tsx`): `type BannerTone = 'info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger'`
- `BreadcrumbLink` (`src/components/Breadcrumbs/Breadcrumbs.tsx`): `interface BreadcrumbLink { label: string; href: string; }`
- `ButtonSize` (`src/components/Button/Button.tsx`): `type ButtonSize = 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'`
- `ButtonVariant` (`src/components/Button/Button.tsx`): `type ButtonVariant = 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'ghost' | 'danger'`
- `ChangeDecision` (`src/components/ReviewChanges/ReviewChanges.tsx`): `type ChangeDecision = 'accepted' | 'rejected'`
- `ChangeOutcome` (`src/components/ReviewChanges/ReviewChanges.tsx`): `type ChangeOutcome = { ok: true; } | { ok: false; reason: string; }` How each change went once applied: done, or why it failed.
- `CheckedState` (`src/components/Checkbox/Checkbox.tsx`): `type CheckedState = boolean | 'indeterminate'`
- `ComboboxOption` (`src/components/Combobox/Combobox.tsx`): `interface ComboboxOption { value: string; label: string; description?: string; disabled?: boolean; }`
- `CommandGroup` (`src/components/CommandPalette/CommandPalette.tsx`): `interface CommandGroup { id: string; label: string; items: readonly CommandItem[]; filter?: 'local' | 'none'; }`
- `CommandItem` (`src/components/CommandPalette/CommandPalette.tsx`): `interface CommandItem { id: string; label: string; description?: string; icon?: IconName; keywords?: readonly string[]; shortcut?: string; onSelect: () => void; }`
- `ComposerAttachment` (`src/components/Composer/Composer.tsx`): `interface ComposerAttachment { id: string; name: string; }`
- `ContentWidthToken` (`src/tokens/tokens.ts`): `type ContentWidthToken = keyof typeof vars.size.content`
- `DateInput` (`src/format/format.ts`): `type DateInput = string | number | Date` An instant (ISO timestamp, epoch ms or Date), or a calendar date with no zone ("2026-09-30").
- `DateRange` (`src/components/DatePicker/DatePicker.tsx`): `interface DateRange { start: IsoDate; end: IsoDate; }`
- `DateStyle` (`src/format/format.ts`): `type DateStyle = 'short' | 'medium' | 'long'`
- `EmptyStateReason` (`src/components/EmptyState/EmptyState.tsx`): `type EmptyStateReason = 'first-use' | 'no-results' | 'error'` Why the region is empty. Decide it from the unfiltered collection, never from the rows on screen: "nothing yet" and "nothing matches" need different words and a different action.
- `EscapeHatch` (`src/internal/closed-api.ts`): `interface EscapeHatch { UNSAFE_className?: string; UNSAFE_style?: CSSProperties; }` The only styling escape hatch on system components and primitives. The UNSAFE_ prefix makes every use greppable and countable. Consumer code must justify each use with an eslint-disable comment that carries a reason, an owner and a removal condition. A repeated override is a missing variant: propose one.
- `FeedbackRating` (`src/components/Feedback/Feedback.tsx`): `type FeedbackRating = 'up' | 'down'`
- `FeedbackValue` (`src/components/Feedback/Feedback.tsx`): `interface FeedbackValue { rating: FeedbackRating; reason?: string; }`
- `FileRejection` (`src/components/FileUpload/FileUpload.tsx`): `interface FileRejection { file: File; reason: 'type' | 'size'; message: string; }` A picked or dropped file that broke a limit, with a message ready to show.
- `FileUploadItem` (`src/components/FileUpload/FileUpload.tsx`): `interface FileUploadItem { id: string; name: string; size: number; progress?: number; error?: string; }` A file in the list. The caller owns the list: it adds accepted files, reports progress and removes them.
- `Formatter` (`src/format/format.ts`): `interface Formatter extends LocaleSettings { date: (value: DateInput, style?: DateStyle) => string; time: (value: DateInput) => string; dateTime: (value: DateInput, options?: { withZone?: boolean; }) => string; relative: (value: DateInput, now?: DateInput) => string; number: (value: number, options?: { maximumFractionDigits?: number; }) => string; percent: (value: number, options?: { maximumFractionDigits?: number; }) => string; compact: (value: number) => string; money: (minor: number, currency: string, options?: { compact?: boolean; }) => string; list: (items: readonly string[], type?: 'conjunction' | 'disjunction') => string; fileSize: (bytes: number) => string; }`
- `GapToken` (`src/tokens/tokens.ts`): `type GapToken = keyof typeof vars.space.gap`
- `GridItemToken` (`src/tokens/tokens.ts`): `type GridItemToken = keyof typeof vars.size['grid-item']`
- `HeadingLevel` (`src/components/Heading/Heading.tsx`): `type HeadingLevel = 1 | 2 | 3 | 4`
- `IconName` (`src/components/Icon/Icon.tsx`): `type IconName = keyof typeof PATHS`
- `InsetToken` (`src/tokens/tokens.ts`): `type InsetToken = keyof typeof vars.space.inset`
- `IsoDate` (`src/components/DatePicker/DatePicker.tsx`): `type IsoDate = string` A calendar date as the system passes it: ISO "2026-09-25", no time, no zone.
- `KeyPlatform` (`src/components/Kbd/Kbd.tsx`): `type KeyPlatform = 'mac' | 'other'` Where a shortcut is shown: Apple keyboards name modifiers with symbols (⌘ ⇧ ⌥ ⌃), everyone else with words (Ctrl, Shift, Alt). `mod` is the platform's command key: ⌘ on a Mac, Ctrl elsewhere.
- `LayoutElement` (`src/primitives/types.ts`): `type LayoutElement = 'div' | 'section' | 'article' | 'aside' | 'header' | 'footer' | 'main' | 'nav' | 'form' | 'fieldset' | 'ul' | 'ol' | 'li' | 'dl'` Elements a layout primitive may render as. Closed on purpose: layout, not widgets.
- `LinkComponent` (`src/components/Link/Link.tsx`): `type LinkComponent = ComponentType<LinkComponentProps>` An app's router link, adapted to take `href`: React Router's `<Link to>`, Next's `<Link href>`.
- `LinkComponentProps` (`src/components/Link/Link.tsx`): `type LinkComponentProps = Omit<ComponentPropsWithRef<'a'>, 'href'> & { href: string; }` What the system hands an app's link component: every anchor prop, with `href` always set and `ref` included. The component must spread the rest onto its anchor and forward `ref` (tooltips and focus management attach to it).
- `LocaleSettings` (`src/format/format.ts`): `interface LocaleSettings { locale: string; timeZone: string; }` Locale formatting over Intl. Every number, date, amount and list a user reads goes through one of these named formats, so the same concept looks the same on every screen and follows the reader's locale and time zone. No hand-built strings ("$" + n, toFixed, toISOString). Formatter instances are cached per locale and options: building one per table cell is slow.
- `MenuEntry` (`src/components/Menu/Menu.tsx`): `type MenuEntry = MenuItem | 'separator'` An item, or 'separator' for a divider between groups.
- `MenuItem` (`src/components/Menu/Menu.tsx`): `interface MenuItem { label: string; onSelect?: () => void; icon?: IconName; tone?: 'default' | 'danger'; disabled?: boolean; shortcut?: string; }`
- `MessageRole` (`src/components/Message/Message.tsx`): `type MessageRole = 'user' | 'assistant' | 'tool' | 'system'` Who a turn is from: the person, the assistant, a tool the assistant ran, or the system (a note in the thread).
- `MeterStatus` (`src/components/Meter/Meter.tsx`): `type MeterStatus = 'ok' | 'warning' | 'danger'`
- `MultiSelectOption` (`src/components/MultiSelect/MultiSelect.tsx`): `type MultiSelectOption = PickerOptionData`
- `NavItem` (`src/components/Nav/Nav.tsx`): `interface NavItem { label: string; href: string; icon?: IconName; }`
- `NavSection` (`src/components/Nav/Nav.tsx`): `interface NavSection { label?: string; items: readonly NavItem[]; }`
- `NavTab` (`src/components/NavTabs/NavTabs.tsx`): `interface NavTab { label: string; href: string; }`
- `ProposedChange` (`src/components/ReviewChanges/ReviewChanges.tsx`): `interface ProposedChange { id: string; target: string; field: string; before: string; after: string; kind?: 'field' | 'text'; reason?: string; blockedReason?: string; }` One proposed change: a field's old and new value, or a text rewrite shown word by word.
- `RadioOption` (`src/components/RadioGroup/RadioGroup.tsx`): `interface RadioOption { value: string; label: string; description?: string; disabled?: boolean; }`
- `RatioToken` (`src/tokens/tokens.ts`): `type RatioToken = keyof typeof vars.ratio`

- `Source` (`src/components/Citation/Citation.tsx`): `interface Source { title: string; origin: string; excerpt?: string; href?: string; hrefLabel?: string; }`
- `SpinnerSize` (`src/components/Spinner/Spinner.tsx`): `type SpinnerSize = 'sm' | 'md'`
- `StatDelta` (`src/components/Stat/Stat.tsx`): `interface StatDelta { value: string; direction: StatDirection; tone?: StatTone; }`
- `StatDirection` (`src/components/Stat/Stat.tsx`): `type StatDirection = 'up' | 'down' | 'flat'`
- `StatTone` (`src/components/Stat/Stat.tsx`): `type StatTone = 'positive' | 'negative' | 'neutral'` Whether the change is good news. Separate from direction: fewer overdue records is down and positive.
- `StepperStep` (`src/components/Stepper/Stepper.tsx`): `interface StepperStep { label: string; }`
- `StreamStatus` (`src/components/StreamingText/StreamingText.tsx`): `type StreamStatus = 'pending' | 'streaming' | 'complete' | 'stopped' | 'error'` Where an answer is: waiting for its first token, arriving, finished, stopped by the person, or failed.
- `TimelineEvent` (`src/components/Timeline/Timeline.tsx`): `interface TimelineEvent { id: string; actor: string; verb: string; target?: ReactNode; time: string; dateTime: string; detail?: string; }` One thing that happened: who did what to which, and when.
- `ToastTone` (`src/components/Toast/Toast.tsx`): `type ToastTone = 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info' | 'neutral'`

## Guides in full

<!-- docs/guides/GettingStarted.stories.tsx -->

### Getting started

Five steps: bring the system in, load its styles once, render every signed-in page inside AppShell, route its links through your router, and set the reader’s locale.

#### 1. Install

The system is one folder in this repo until a second app needs it as a versioned package. Install its dependencies and check that everything passes before you build on it.

```
npm ci
npx playwright install chromium   # once, for the visual and axe suite
npm run check                     # tokens, types, lint, tests, rules, build, size budgets
npm run dev                       # this gallery on http://localhost:6006
```

#### 2. Import from the public entry

Import components, layouts and primitives from `src/index.ts` only. It loads the stylesheet first, so the cascade layer order is declared before any component style. A built app imports `dist/index.js` and `dist/styles.css` instead.

```
import { AppShell, Button, Stack, Heading } from '../index';   // the public entry

// Blocked by lint: deep imports, and vendor UI outside the system.
// import { Button } from '../components/Button/Button';
// import { Dialog } from 'radix-ui';
```

#### 3. Wrap the page in AppShell

Define the shell once for the app: brand, one nav config, one account menu. Each page passes where it is and its content. Never rebuild the frame.

```
export function RecordsPage() {
  return (
    <AppShell brand="Acme" nav={<Nav label="Main" sections={NAV} current="/records" />} userMenu={accountMenu}>
      <Center max="lg" gutters="lg">
        <Stack gap="lg">
          <PageHeader title="Records" actions={<Button icon="plus">New record</Button>} />
          {/* the page */}
        </Stack>
      </Center>
    </AppShell>
  );
}
```

The golden examples do exactly this through one shared shell: start from [the list page example](src/examples/ListPage.tsx).

#### 4. Route links through your router

System links render a plain `<a>` by default. Give the app’s router link to `LinkProvider` once, at the root, and `Link`, `Nav`, `NavTabs` and `Breadcrumbs` all navigate client-side. The adapter takes `href`, spreads every other prop onto the anchor and forwards `ref`.

```
import { Link as RouterLinkBase } from 'react-router';
import { LinkProvider, type LinkComponentProps } from '../index';

// Defined once, outside any component, so its identity never changes.
function AppLink({ href, ref, ...rest }: LinkComponentProps) {
  return <RouterLinkBase to={href} ref={ref} {...rest} />;
}

export function App() {
  return (
    <LinkProvider component={AppLink}>
      <Routes>{/* every page, each inside AppShell */}</Routes>
    </LinkProvider>
  );
}
```

```
import NextLink from 'next/link';

function AppLink(props: LinkComponentProps) {
  return <NextLink {...props} />;   // already takes href and forwards ref
}
```

Modified clicks (new tab, new window) keep working, because the router link is still an anchor with a real `href`.

#### 5. Set the locale and time zone

Wrap the app once in `LocaleProvider` with the signed-in person’s locale and time zone (a profile setting that defaults from the browser). Then format every value a person reads with `useFormat()`. System components that show numbers, such as Pagination, follow it too.

```
<LocaleProvider locale={user.locale} timeZone={user.timeZone}>
  <LinkProvider component={AppLink}>{/* the app */}</LinkProvider>
</LocaleProvider>

const format = useFormat();
format.money(1_250_050, 'EUR');   // "€12,500.50" in en-US, "12.500,50 €" in de-DE
format.date('2026-09-12');        // a calendar date: never shifts by time zone
format.relative(record.updatedAt);  // "3 days ago"
```

Data is the app’s job, not the system’s: the examples read and write through `src/app` (a query cache, named mutations, URL state). The Data guide explains that layer.

#### Then

- Pick the page archetype and copy its example: see Page archetypes.
- Wire its data the way the examples do: see Data.
- Style nothing. If a component doesn’t look right for the job, walk the Decision ladder.
- Before a pull request: `npm run check`, then the visual and axe suite (`npm run test:visual`).

<!-- docs/guides/Principles.stories.tsx -->

### Principles

Three rules the whole system is built around. Each one is enforced by the build, not by review, so a change that breaks one fails before anyone has to spot it.

#### Tokens only

Every colour, length, radius, shadow, duration and font comes from a token. The token source is the only place a value lives.

- Use semantic tokens (`--color-fg-muted`, `--space-gap-md`), named for intent. Primitives are reference only.
- The only literals allowed are `inherit`, `currentColor`, `transparent`, `none`, `auto`, `0`, `1px` and `100%`. Stylelint rejects the rest.
- Missing a token? Add a semantic one (with a dark value for colours) and regenerate. Never write the literal instead.

#### Compose, don’t restyle

Pages are compositions of system components inside layout primitives, inside AppShell. Product code has no CSS.

- Components are closed: no `className` or `style`. A new look is a new variant in the component, available to everyone.
- Layout primitives own spacing between things. Children never bring outer margins.
- A repeated override is a missing variant. Propose it instead of copying the override.

#### Accessibility built in

The system carries the parts of accessibility that can be decided once, so product code can’t get them wrong.

- Semantic colour pairs meet WCAG 2.2 AA in light and dark, checked in a test.
- Components require their accessible names as props, and use native elements and Radix behaviour for keyboard and focus.
- Every story in this gallery, and every Docs tab, is checked with axe in the visual suite.
- What’s left to product code (labels, headings, focus after navigation) is listed in the Accessibility guide.

<!-- docs/guides/DecisionLadder.stories.tsx -->

### Decision ladder

Before building anything new, walk the ladder from the top and stop at the first yes. Most needs stop at the first rung.

#### The ladder

1. **Template: is it a new page?**
   Copy the golden example for its archetype and render it inside AppShell. Compose existing parts. No new component.
2. **Variant: does an existing component need a new look?**
   Add a value to its closed variant vocabulary, with a story. A new status extends the status-to-tone map; it doesn’t add a badge.
3. **Component: is it a genuinely new region or intent?**
   Add a component with a focused contract, composed from existing parts where possible: closed props, a required accessible name, a story per variant and state, and a usage doc.
4. **Primitive: can it not be expressed as a composition at all?**
   The highest bar: domain-agnostic, token-driven. It changes tokens, component styles and the agent rules in the same pull request.

#### Proposing a token

- Pick the tier. Semantic is almost always right; a primitive only for a new raw value; a component token only for a per-part override hook.
- Name it for intent (`color.fg.muted`, not `color.gray-600`), give colours a dark value, and add a `$description`: it becomes the “use for” note on the Foundations pages.
- Run `npm run tokens` and commit the source with the generated files. A new text/background pair joins the contrast pairs.

#### Proposing a component or variant

- Write down the use cases (at least two real ones), the API, an owner and what existing screens would move to it.
- A second use is a signal to review for promotion; three distinct uses usually confirm the abstraction is stable.
- Ship it with stories for every variant and state, a usage doc on its Docs tab, and green visual and axe runs.

<!-- docs/guides/Layout.stories.tsx -->

### Layout

Four layouts frame a page; eleven layout primitives arrange everything inside it. They take gaps, widths and ratios as tokens, so a layout can’t drift off the scale, and they hold no domain knowledge.

#### Which layout

Pick the frame first. Each page starts from a PageHeader inside it.

**Layouts**

| Layout | Choose when | Avoid when |
|---|---|---|
| [AppShell](src/layouts/AppShell/AppShell.stories.tsx) | Every signed-in page: skip link, sidebar (collapsible to an icon rail), header, main. | Signed-out pages (AuthLayout) or a task that takes over the screen (FocusedLayout). |
| [PageLayout](src/layouts/PageLayout/PageLayout.stories.tsx) | Inside a page, below its PageHeader: a section nav at the start, the main column, a named aside at the end. | A one-column page: Center and Stack are enough. |
| [AuthLayout](src/layouts/AuthLayout/AuthLayout.stories.tsx) | Sign-in, sign-up, password reset, and an error page when the app itself may not have loaded. | Any signed-in page, including a signed-in 404 (AppShell). |
| [FocusedLayout](src/layouts/FocusedLayout/FocusedLayout.stories.tsx) | A multi-step task that takes over the screen until it is done or abandoned: setup, a wizard. | A single-page form (AppShell with its footer action bar). |

#### Which primitive

**Layout primitives**

| Primitive | Choose when | Avoid when |
|---|---|---|
| [Stack](src/primitives/Stack/Stack.stories.tsx) | Things flow top to bottom: a page’s sections, a form, a card body. | Items sit side by side (Cluster). |
| [Cluster](src/primitives/Cluster/Cluster.stories.tsx) | A row that may wrap: button groups, filter bars, tags. | The row must line up in columns (Grid or Table). |
| [Grid](src/primitives/Grid/Grid.stories.tsx) | Equal items that reflow by width with no breakpoints: cards, stat tiles. | Rows of comparable attributes (Table), or two regions of different weight (Sidebar). |
| [Switcher](src/primitives/Switcher/Switcher.stories.tsx) | Equal items in one row, or one column all at once when the container is narrow: stat tiles, plan cards. | Many items that should reflow into as many columns as fit (Grid). |
| [Sidebar](src/primitives/Sidebar/Sidebar.stories.tsx) | A narrow region beside a wider one inside a card, panel or dialog, stacking when space runs out. | A page’s properties rail or sub-nav (PageLayout), or the app’s navigation (AppShell). |
| [Center](src/primitives/Center/Center.stories.tsx) | The page column inside AppShell’s main, with a bounded measure and gutters; empty states (intrinsic). | Centring a single control in a row (Cluster justify="center"). |
| [Cover](src/primitives/Cover/Cover.stories.tsx) | One block centred vertically in the available height, with a header and footer pinned to the edges. | A signed-out page: AuthLayout already composes it. |
| [Box](src/primitives/Box/Box.stories.tsx) | Padding from the inset scale inside a region with no component of its own: a toolbar strip, a panel body. | A titled surface (Card), or space between siblings (the parent’s gap). |
| [Reel](src/primitives/Reel/Reel.stories.tsx) | One row of like items that scrolls sideways with snapping: recent files, thumbnails, suggestions. | Items people compare or must all see (Grid), or wide data (Table). |
| [Imposter](src/primitives/Imposter/Imposter.stories.tsx) | An overlay centred over one region, not the page: a notice over an empty chart, a prompt over a locked panel. | Anything that takes focus and blocks the page (Dialog). |
| [Frame](src/primitives/Frame/Frame.stories.tsx) | Media held to a ratio token and cropped to fill: file previews, covers, video. | A person’s picture (Avatar), or a box that holds text. |

#### Composing into AppShell

AppShell owns the frame: skip link, sidebar navigation, header and the one scrolling `main`. A page fills its slots and lays out its own content with primitives, starting from a Center column.

```
<AppShell brand={…} nav={…} breadcrumbs={…} userMenu={…} footer={actionBar}>
  <Center max="lg" gutters="lg">
    <Stack gap="lg">
      <PageHeader title="Hardware lease" status={<Badge tone="info">Pending</Badge>} actions={<Button>Edit</Button>} />
      <NavTabs label="Record sections" items={sections} current={href} />
      <PageLayout aside={propertiesCard} asideLabel="Properties">
        <Stack gap="lg">{/* main column: cards */}</Stack>
      </PageLayout>
    </Stack>
  </Center>
</AppShell>
```

#### Rules

- The parent owns the space between children. Pick a gap token; never add margins.
- Pass semantic elements with `as` (`section`, `ul`, `form`) so the layout is also the outline.
- Layouts respond to their container, not the viewport. AppShell opens its nav in a Drawer below `size.breakpoint.md`; PageLayout stacks nav, main and aside below `size.breakpoint.sm`; Switcher stacks below its `threshold`. To see each state, set the gallery’s Width toolbar to Narrow, Medium or Wide: it wraps any story in a container sized from those tokens.
- Start every page with a `PageHeader` (the one h1, status, actions). Breadcrumbs belong to AppShell’s header, not the page.
- Only `main` scrolls. Long forms put their actions in AppShell’s `footer` slot, which sticks to the bottom.

<!-- docs/guides/PageArchetypes.stories.tsx -->

### Page archetypes

Most pages are one of a few archetypes. Each has one golden example: copy it, swap the nouns, keep the structure and the states. Don’t copy another screen.

#### Which example to copy

**Archetypes and their examples**

| Archetype | Choose when | Copy | It shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| List / index | Users come to find, compare or act on many records: records, people, invoices, an audit log. | [List page](src/examples/ListPage.tsx)`src/examples/ListPage.tsx` | PageHeader with one primary action, saved views (save, rename, default, delete; “Modified”), view tabs with server counts, SearchField, a Filters popover with removable chips and a Columns popover, a Table · Board switch over one query (the board keyboard-operable, with a Move to… menu), Pagination; everything in the URL; row selection with “Select all N matching” and a bulk bar; actions disabled with a reason per role; loading, first use, no results and load error states. |
| Record / detail | One record is the subject: its status, properties, activity and the actions on it. | [Record page](src/examples/RecordPage.tsx)`src/examples/RecordPage.tsx` | Breadcrumb, PageHeader with status and a “More” menu, NavTabs for Overview · Activity · Files, a properties aside rendered from the field registry; an optimistic rename with rollback and a conflict banner, a pessimistic archive. |
| Create and edit | Someone fills in a record: a full page for heavy records, a quick-create dialog for light ones. | [Create and edit](src/examples/CreateEditFlow.tsx)`src/examples/CreateEditFlow.tsx` | Errors on blur and submit, a focused error summary linking to fields, registry-rendered fields, a pending submit in the sticky action bar, a create that is safe to retry (idempotency key). |
| Entity list, record and form (schema-driven) | A second or third entity (accounts, people, vendors) whose pages fit the list, record and form archetypes: write its config, not its pages. | [Entity pages](src/examples/EntityPages.tsx)`src/examples/EntityPages.tsx` | List, record and form rendered from an entity config (src/app/registries/entities.ts) through the field registry: a properties rail, the records that point at it by id with rollups, Edit disabled with a reason, create and edit with a focused error summary. |
| The app and its routes | Wiring pages together: which page a URL opens, who may open it, and what an unknown URL shows. | [App](src/examples/App.tsx)`src/examples/App.tsx` | The route table (path → layout + page + guard), lazy pages, LinkProvider with the app’s router link, a 403 page from the guard and the 404 fallback. |
| Inbox / queue | Working through items one at a time: an inbox, a review queue, approvals, support tickets. | [Inbox](src/examples/InboxPage.tsx)`src/examples/InboxPage.tsx` | A SplitView of the list and the open item (one pane on a narrow screen), the tab and open item in the URL, keyboard triage from the shortcut registry (j/k, e, u, x, o) mirrored by a toolbar, a row context menu and a bulk toolbar; unread state; optimistic triage with rollback; loading, empty and error states. |
| Admin console | Workspace administration: members and roles, the audit log, and the enterprise controls that grow around them. | [Admin console](src/examples/AdminConsole.tsx)`src/examples/AdminConsole.tsx` | Members (invite, change role with a review of the capabilities it adds and removes, remove; your own role and the last admin protected) and a filterable audit log (actor Combobox, event MultiSelect, DateRangePicker in the reader’s time zone, expandable rows, CSV export of the current filter); actions disabled with a reason or hidden by capability; the audit tab hidden and its route guarded. |
| Settings | Personal or workspace preferences, grouped by category. | [Settings page](src/examples/SettingsPage.tsx)`src/examples/SettingsPage.tsx` | A grouped sub-nav in PageLayout’s nav slot, one card per category with its own Save, a success banner. |
| Sign-in (signed out) | Any signed-out page: sign-in, sign-up, password reset, a verification code. | [Sign in](src/examples/SignInPage.tsx)`src/examples/SignInPage.tsx` | AuthLayout; SSO first, an emailed link, a password as the secondary route; a failed-sign-in banner; a verification-code step. |
| Wizard | A task whose later steps depend on earlier ones: first-run setup, a multi-step create. | [Setup wizard](src/examples/SetupWizard.tsx)`src/examples/SetupWizard.tsx` | FocusedLayout with an exit, Progress and Stepper; validation per step; focus to each step’s h1; a review step with Edit. |
| Dashboard | A home or overview page: how things are, and what needs attention. | [Dashboard](src/examples/DashboardPage.tsx)`src/examples/DashboardPage.tsx` | A date range (SegmentedControl) in the PageHeader, Stat tiles in a Switcher, usage Meters, recent activity, a needs-attention table. |
| Assistant beside a page (AI) | People ask questions about the record or page they are on, with it still in view. | [Record copilot](src/examples/RecordCopilot.tsx)`src/examples/RecordCopilot.tsx` | The existing record page with an AssistantPanel in the shell (WithAssistant): answers that cite fields and activity, sources that link into the record, tool activity, Stop, Retry, Edit, Feedback, a refusal and each failure in its own words. |
| Inline AI in a form (AI) | A field the AI can draft (a description, a reply), beside writing it by hand. | [Create with AI](src/examples/CreateWithAi.tsx)`src/examples/CreateWithAi.tsx` | Suggest beside the field, disabled with a reason per role; ghost text (Tab or Accept, Esc or Dismiss); accepted text marked “Drafted with AI” until edited; one Undo back to what was there. |
| AI-proposed changes (AI) | An agent would change data: many records, or any write at all. | [AI bulk changes](src/examples/AiReviewChanges.tsx)`src/examples/AiReviewChanges.tsx` | The agent’s steps, a proposal limited to what the person could do, ReviewChanges (accept or reject each, apply), apply and undo through the named mutation, partial failure, a refusal for a viewer. |
| Chat page (AI) | Open-ended, multi-turn questions that span the workspace. | [Assistant chat](src/examples/AssistantChatPage.tsx)`src/examples/AssistantChatPage.tsx` | History in PageLayout’s nav with the open conversation in the URL, new chat, rename and delete, the composer in the sticky footer, and streaming, stopped, refused, rate-limited and failed answers. |
| Error and 404 | A page that doesn’t exist (inside the shell), or a failure before the app can load (in AuthLayout). | [Error pages](src/examples/ErrorPages.tsx)`src/examples/ErrorPages.tsx` | EmptyState as the h1, plain words, Try again and a way home; a 403 page for a route the role can’t open, saying who can change that. |

#### How to copy one

- Signed-in pages render inside the app’s one shell composition (the examples share `ExampleShell`); signed-out pages in AuthLayout; a focused multi-step task in FocusedLayout. Every page starts with a `PageHeader`.
- Keep every state the example has: loading, empty, error. A page without them isn’t finished.
- Read and write through the app layer, as the list, record and create examples do: queries and named mutations from `src/app/model`, never a fetch in a page. See the Data guide.
- Map domain statuses to badge tones in one place (`src/app/model/status.ts`), and define each “what counts as X” as one named predicate.
- Format every number, date and amount with `useFormat()`; never by hand.
- A new page is a row in the route table (`src/examples/routes.tsx`) with the capability that guards it. A new entity that fits the list, record and form archetypes is an entry in `src/app/registries/entities.ts`, not three new pages.
- Ask `can` (through `useCan` or `usePermission`) before showing an action: disable page and bar actions with the reason beside them, hide overflow-menu items and card actions. The mutation and the server refuse as well.
- AI surfaces follow the same rules and add their own (citations, review before any write, undo, the assistant acting only as the person): see the AI patterns guide.
- A page that fits no archetype is rare. Check the list again, then raise it: it may need a new golden example, not a one-off.

<!-- docs/guides/Data.stories.tsx -->

### Data

The design system draws; the app layer knows. Everything about fetching, caching, validating and writing data lives in src/app, which the golden examples use and the system never imports.

#### Why the system stays UI-only

- The system’s runtime dependencies are exactly `react`, `react-dom`, `radix-ui` and `react-aria-components` (with its date library, `@internationalized/date`), all UI. A unit test fails the build if that list changes.
- Data libraries (`msw`, `@tanstack/react-query`, `zod`) are devDependencies. ESLint rejects them, and any import from `src/app`, in `src/components`, `src/primitives` and `src/layouts`, with a fixture per boundary in `npm run test:rules`.
- So components take values and callbacks, never queries. An app is free to choose another cache or another server, and the system doesn’t change.
- The one data-shaped part the system does ship is formatting: `LocaleProvider` and `useFormat()`. Every number, date and amount a person reads goes through it.

```
tokens → primitives → components → layouts        the design system (src/index.ts)
                                         ↑
src/app   api/        the client and zod schemas: every response is parsed at the boundary
          model/      cache keys, queries, named predicates, projections, mutations, selection,
                      permissions (the role → capability mapping and the one predicate, can)
          session.tsx the session: memberships, the active workspace, switch, sign out
          routing/    the route entry type, the matcher, RouteView and AppLink
          url/        useUrlState and the list page's URL codec
          registries/ the field registry, which fields a record has, entityType → fields
          mocks/      the mock API (MSW), its seeded database and gallery wiring
                                         ↑
src/examples          golden pages: compose the system, read and write through src/app
```

#### The cache model

- One server cache (TanStack Query), chosen on purpose: this is server-driven CRUD with server-side search, filter, sort and paging. A normalized store would earn its cost only if many views edited the same entities at once.
- Keys are `[tenant, scope, resource, params]`: `['acme', 'admin', 'records', { view, q, status, sort, page }]`, `['acme', 'admin', 'record', { id }]`. The partition (the workspace, then the permission scope the server answered for) leads every key, so one workspace’s data can never answer for another’s, a viewer never reads what an admin cached, and invalidation can be as narrow as one resource in one partition.
- A query cache doesn’t normalize: a record also lives inside every cached list page that holds it. So a record write patches the detail *and* every listed copy (`patchListedRecord`, one `setQueriesData` over the lists prefix), then invalidates what the patch can’t know (membership, order, totals). A test holds every list request open and still sees the edit in the mounted list and in an unmounted page of another tab.
- Only trusted data enters the cache. Every response is parsed with a zod schema in `src/app/api/client.ts`. A payload that breaks the contract is reported and becomes the page’s error state; it never reaches the cache (see [the invalid payload story](src/examples/ListPage.tsx)).
- Views are projections, never copies: rows are `toRow(record)`. “What counts as open” is one predicate, `isOpen`. The Open tab, its count, the filter options, the badges, the bulk-delete guard (`canDelete`) and the mock server all call the same functions, so they can’t disagree.

#### Entities and joins

- Three entities: records, accounts and people. A record holds `ownerId` and `accountId`, never a copy of a name. Accounts and people are reference data, loaded whole into one directory query each.
- Every name on screen is joined by id at render: `PersonRef` and `AccountRef` (and the registry’s `person` and `account` field types) read the directory. Rename an account once and every row, card and property that shows it changes, with no list touched.
- The server joins too: search matches the owner’s name, looked up by id before the one `matchesSearch` predicate runs, so client and server still agree about what matches.
- A related-entity section is a join projection: an account’s page lists `useRecordList({ account: id })`, through the same `toRow`, with rollups from the same counts as the tabs. Navigation goes both ways by id.

#### One projection, many surfaces

- The list’s table and board are two surfaces over one query and one projection. The board groups the same rows by per-status predicates (`toBoard`, `hasStatus`); its columns are the statuses the tab’s predicate lets through, narrowed by the status filter; its column totals are per-status counts the server returns beside the tab counts.
- The display is URL state (`display=board`), pushed so Back returns to the table. A new surface (a calendar, a timeline) is a new entry in `DISPLAYS` and a component, never a page with its own store.
- Every card has a Move to… menu, so the board works from the keyboard. Dragging a card onto a column does the same, and declares the menu as its alternative (`data-drag-alternative`, enforced by ESLint).

#### Permissions

```
role ──(ROLE_CAPABILITIES, src/app/model/permissions.ts)──▶ capabilities ──▶ can(grant, capability, subject?)
                                                                              ├─ control: shown / disabled with the reason
                                                                              ├─ route guard: page / 403 page
                                                                              ├─ mutation: sends / refuses (403) without a request
                                                                              └─ mock server: 200 / 403, whatever the client did
```

**Roles**

| Role | Holds | In the examples |
|---|---|---|
| Viewer | workspace:read, record:read, account:read | Records minus drafts (filtered in the query); no New record, no Move to…, no Rename or Archive |
| Editor | Viewer’s, plus record:read-drafts, record:create, rename, move, archive, account:create, people:create | Everything; Delete disabled (“Only workspace admins can delete records.”), account Edit disabled |
| Admin | Editor’s, plus workspace:manage, record:delete, account:edit, members:manage, audit:read | Everything, including the audit log; invites, changes and removes members |

- Capabilities are `resource:action` strings. Roles map to them in exactly one place, and the session carries each membership’s capabilities as the server derived them. The client never decides anything from a role name.
- `can` checks the capability, then the object rule for the thing acted on (an archived record can’t be renamed; one on legal hold can’t be deleted), from the same named predicates as everything else.
- One rule per context: page and bar actions are disabled, with the reason as visible text they point at (`aria-describedby`); overflow-menu items and card actions are hidden; a route the role can’t open renders the 403 page. Never a silent redirect.
- Roles shape projections too: a viewer’s lists have no drafts, filtered by the server in the query, so pages and totals stay honest. The Drafts tab needs `record:read-drafts`.
- The gallery’s **Role** toolbar switches between viewer, editor and admin (default admin). A story that sets `mockApi({ role })` wins, and the visual suite pins `role:admin`. See [the viewer’s list](src/examples/ListPage.tsx) and [a forced 403](src/examples/RecordPage.tsx).

#### Workspace and session boundaries

- **Switch workspace** (the account menu): in-flight reads of the old workspace are cancelled, its confirmed data stays under its own keys, and the page remounts, so selections and drafts stay behind. A late answer never reaches the new screen.
- **Permission change** (a new session, or `refreshSession` after a 403): the old scope’s partition is dropped, and a list never keeps the previous page on screen across partitions (`keepPreviousData` would otherwise show an admin’s rows to a viewer until the viewer’s arrived).
- **Sign out**: every query and mutation is cancelled and the whole cache cleared before the signed-out screen renders. The server ends the session; every later request is a 401.

#### Routes

- The route table is the master registry: `path → layout + page + guard` (`src/examples/routes.tsx`). A route without a capability doesn’t compile, and a test checks every route has one.
- Pages are lazy, one chunk per route. The Suspense fallback is nothing: a page shows its own skeleton once its code is here.
- An unknown path renders the 404 page, the table’s own fallback. The app hands the design system its router link once (`LinkProvider` with `AppLink`), so every Link, Nav, NavTabs and Breadcrumbs routes in place.

#### Where state lives

**State homes**

| Home | Holds | In the list and record pages |
|---|---|---|
| Local state | What one component owns: an open menu, a half-typed search, a form draft | The rename dialog’s typed name |
| Lifted state | What two parts of one page coordinate on | The list’s selection (the table and the footer bar share it) |
| Server cache | Confirmed domain data, read through queries | A page of records, a record, the tab counts |
| URL | What a copied link must reproduce: view, search, filters, sort, page, tab | /records?view=open&q=lease&sort=-amount&page=2 |

- `useUrlState(codec)` reads and writes a validated query string. The codec never throws: an unknown view, sort or status falls back to its default, so a stale or hand-edited link still opens a sensible view.
- History is decided per write. **Push** for navigation (a tab, a page), so Back returns there. **Replace** for refinements (a filter, a sort, the search once typing pauses for 300 ms), so Back never steps through keystrokes.
- Ids go in the URL, never the data behind them or anything personal. The half-typed search stays local until it’s committed.

#### Writes: one named mutation per verb

Components never write the cache. They call a mutation from `src/app/model/mutations.ts`, named for the domain verb. How it presents depends on whether failure is cheap to reverse: optimistic for a person’s own frequent edit, pessimistic when the server decides or the change is hard to take back.

**The mutation matrix**

| Mutation | Presents | Patches | Invalidates | On failure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `renameRecord` | Optimistic | The record and every cached list page holding it, at once; both rolled back on failure unless a newer write landed | The record, every list (counts can’t change) | Old name back, a toast that stays, the typed name kept; a 409 shows a Banner with Reload; a 403 refreshes the session |
| `moveRecord` | Pessimistic | The record and every listed copy, with the server’s answer | Every list and count | Nothing changed; a toast that stays |
| `archiveRecord` | Pessimistic | The record and every listed copy, with the server’s answer | Every list and count | Nothing changed; a toast that stays |
| `createRecord` | Pessimistic, with an idempotency key | The new record’s detail entry | Every list and count | The draft stays; a retry sends the same key, so no duplicate |
| `bulkDeleteRecords` | Pessimistic, confirmed | Removes deleted records | Every list and count | Partial: a banner that stays (“50 deleted, 9 failed”) with Retry |
| `addPerson` | Pessimistic | Appends to people | People | The dialog stays open with an error |
| `createAccount` | Pessimistic, with an idempotency key | The account’s detail; appends to the directory | The directory | The form stays, with a banner |
| `updateAccount` | Pessimistic, versioned | The account’s detail and its directory entry | Nothing else: records hold its id, so every row re-renders from the directory | A banner; a 409 says someone else changed it |
| `saveView · updateView · deleteView` | Pessimistic | The person’s views (the default moves on update) | Views | The dialog stays open with the server’s reason |
| `markRead · markUnread · archive · unarchive (inbox)` | Optimistic: a person’s own frequent triage | The items in every cached inbox view, and the counts | Inbox views | Every view put back as it was; a toast that stays |
| `inviteMember · changeRole · removeMember` | Pessimistic: it changes what someone else can do | Members (the answer) | Members, the audit log | The dialog stays open with the server’s reason (last admin, your own role, already a member) |

- An optimistic write cancels in-flight reads first, so a late response can’t land on top of it.
- Edits send the version they were based on. The server answers `409` if someone changed the record since, and the page says so instead of silently overwriting their change.
- A pending write disables the controls that would start it again. Errors that need action stay on screen until dismissed.
- See them on the [record page](src/examples/RecordPage.tsx) (rename pending, succeeded, failed and rolled back, conflict; archive pending) and the [create form](src/examples/CreateEditFlow.tsx).

#### Selection and bulk actions

- A checkbox per row, named after the row (`Checkbox hideLabel`, “Select Hardware lease”); selected rows are filled (`TableRow selected`).
- The header box selects the page, then offers “Select all N matching”. That selection is the *filter*, sent to the server as a filter, never as a list of ids it would have to load.
- A selection belongs to one filter: change the search, a filter or the view and it clears. Paging and sorting keep it.
- While anything is selected the shell’s sticky footer shows the count (announced politely), Clear selection, and Delete last, disabled when the `canDelete` predicate rules every selected row out.
- Delete asks with the count in the question. A partial failure stays on screen (“50 deleted, 9 failed”) with the reasons and Retry. See [the partial failure story](src/examples/ListPage.tsx).

#### Registries: fields as config

- `src/app/registries/entities.ts` maps each entity type to its fields: list columns, record properties, related records, and its create and edit form. Generic list, record and form pages (`src/examples/EntityPages.tsx`) render any entry, so accounts and people have no hand-built pages.
- `src/app/registries/fields.tsx` maps each field type (`text`, `money`, `date`, `status`, `person`, `tags`) to how it displays and how it edits. `RECORD_PROPERTIES` drives the record page’s properties; `CREATE_FIELDS` drives the create form. One registry, two surfaces.
- A new field is one line of config. A new field type is one registry entry: the registry is keyed on the type union, so a missing entry fails to compile.
- Data can still be newer than the code. A field whose type has no entry renders “Not available” and is reported once. It never throws.

#### Saved views

- A saved view is config: the tab, search, status filter, sort, visible columns and display, the same state the URL already holds. The mock API stores views per person per workspace, with one default each.
- The URL stays the truth. Choosing a view pushes its config and `saved=<id>`; changing anything after that shows “Modified” until it’s saved into the view or saved as a new one.
- The default view applies only when the list opens with nothing in its URL, with replace: a shared link always wins, and Back never returns to the bare URL.

#### The mock API and the gallery

- Stories and tests talk to a real HTTP mock (MSW) over a seeded, deterministic database: 240 and 120 records for two tenants, the same on every run.
